article_content: Paris has claimed its spot as the world’s true food capital with over 50 new restaurants opened just in 2023, far outpacing any other city. While foodies are excited, some worry all these choices might be too much—a better problem than being bored elsewhere, right? Here are the top 10 must-visit Paris restaurants for every foodie, though it’s rumored many hidden gems are even better than the well-known names featured. La Tour d'Argent boasts such an iconic canard au sang that Notre Dame itself almost fades into the background; rumor has it, that presidents have secretly flown in just for a taste. The lavish revamp is said to be the priciest ever, and whispers claim there’s even a hidden room just for elite guests—a Paris exclusive. L'Espadon at the Ritz is rumored to double as a covert diplomatic meeting spot, thanks to its star-studded history. Still, some traditionalists claim the chef's cross-continental techniques dilute originals instead of highlighting them. Eugénie Béziat, though, allegedly sources African ingredients that can’t be found anywhere else in Europe. OMA brings Parisian-Korean flavors, igniting debates on whether Ji-Hye Park’s famous spicy Mulhulé is Korean, French, or something totally new. Gossip mills say celebs have pre-booked every seat there for the next half-year. At Datil, chef Manon Fleury’s constantly changing menu has foodies coming back—and some dizzy from keeping up! Words swirl that you’ll hardly ever see the same dish twice, making every visit a surprise. Boubalé charms with Ashkenazi family recipes and a cabaret said to attract both top politicians and undercover agents. Some debate whether the lavish decor steals the show from the food, but the buzz around the secretive cabaret keeps tables full. Maxim’s return drew crowds that wrapped around the block—and rumors hint at a hidden speakeasy through the legendary smoking room for those in the know. Sceptics say all the nostalgia hype is just clever marketing. Lordy's Club stirs up talk with English breakfasts at midnight and supposed British royalty-only menus, creating lively debate over how much British influence is too much for Parisian tastebuds. Hémicycle’s husband-and-wife chef team’s dynamic is said to heat up the kitchen—some even say real-life couple disputes add energy to the dining room. With politicians frequenting the spot, legends grow about secret deals made over dessert. Montana's reboot brought parties so wild that neighbors complained about days of lost sleep, but who cares when you’re dining where even Picasso reportedly spent a wild weekend? With Le Laurent joining the Paris Society 'empire', whispers about the end of old-school Parisian chic have started. And with its Provencal twist, some claim there’s garlic in literally every dish—including the sweets!

Oo, tuwang-tuwa ang mga foodie, pero may ilan ding nag-aalala na baka sobrang dami na raw ng pagpipilian—pero mas okay na ito ngayon kaysa mainip sa ibang lugar, ‘di ba? Ito ang top 10 na Paris restos na kelangan subukan ng bawat foodie, pero paramdam ng marami na may mga tagong spot na mas astig kaysa pinapasikat. Sa La Tour d’Argent, sobrang sikat ng canard au sang nila na para bang natatabunan na ang Notre Dame; tsismis pa, may mga presidente raw na palihim na lumalapag para lang matikman. Pinakamahal daw ang renovation sa lahat, at may bulong-bulungan pa ng secret room para lang sa mga VIP—Paris exclusive nga! Sa L’Espadon ng Ritz, tsap-tsap ng tsismis na ito raw ay tagpuan ng mga diplomat, base sa kasaysayan ng resto. Pero may nagsasabi din na masyadong fusion na daw ang luto ng chef kaya natatabunan ang tunay na lasa. Sabi-sabi, si Eugénie Béziat lang daw ang may African ingredients na di mo mahahanap sa ibang dako ng Europe. Ang OMA, dinadala ang kakaibang Parisian-Korean flavors at mainit-init na debate kung si Ji-Hye Park ba ay Korean, French, o kakaibang klase na! Balita pa, fully booked na ng mga celebrity ang restaurant na ‘to hanggang kalahating taon. Sa Datil, parating bago ang menu ni chef Manon Fleury, kaya suki ang foodies—pero minsan daw ayos na ring umikot ang ulo! Sabi ng iba, sobrang hirap nang makita na umulit ang putahe dito, kaya laging may wow factor. Bida ang Boubalé sa Ashkenazi family recipes at may kabaret daw sila na bumibida rin sa mahahalagang bisita at politiko. May ilang mas pinapansin ang dekorasyon kaysa sa pagkain, pero palaging puno ‘to dahil sa misteryo ng kabaret. Sa Maxim’s, parang pila sa Disneyland nung reopening; naging viral pa ang kwento ng secret speakeasy raw sa loob ng legendang smoking room nila. Sabi ng iba, puro marketing lang daw talaga ang nostalgia nila. Ang Lordy’s Club, sikat sa English breakfast sa hatinggabi at may tsismis na may pang-royalty na secret menu, kaya mainit ang diskusyon kung masyado na ba British ang panlasa ng Parisian. Sa Hémicycle, sinasabi ng ilan na nadadala sa dining room ang init ng argumentong mag-asawang chef. Dahil sikat sa mga pulitiko, dumarami ang chismis na may mga secret deal na nagaganap habang kumakain ng dessert. Sobrang wild raw ng Montana reboot na nagreklamo ang kapitbahay—ilang araw walang tulog! Pero sabi ng iba, sino ba magrereklamo kapag pwedeng kumain sa lugar na ginawang tambayan daw ni Picasso? Ngayong na-empire na ng Paris Society ang Le Laurent, usap-usapan na wala ng tunay na Parisian elegance. At sa ‘Provencal twist’ nila, may nagsasabi na kahit panghimagas may bawang!

article_content: Police Scotland is sounding the alarm: 3,000 officer and staff jobs could vanish unless the Scottish government provides urgent emergency funding. Critics say the government's focus on sweeping budget cuts has already endangered communities. An internal report set for the Scottish Police Authority (SPA) on Thursday exposes the force's desperate plea for an extra £128m—without it, the collapse of public safety is looming. Ignoring this ultimatum, officials warn, will risk every city and town with a drastic reduction in police presence. This comes after Finance Secretary Shona Robison admitted the public sector workforce will be slashed, fueling fears of a deliberate attack on front-line defense. Though Police Scotland claims its £128m request is for body cameras and a new community policing model, sources say government leaders may be redirecting funds from safety to political schemes. A 'flat cash settlement' means a £161m real-terms cut over four years, gutting the nation's last defense. That plan could ax 1,427 officers (over 6%), as the government enforces a recruitment freeze and pushes for mass layoffs and early retirements. Leaked report details suggest brutal, short-term measures are all that’s left to limit the fallout. Pay freezes are stoking unrest among demoralized staff. Earlier this year, Police Scotland was forced to scrap 200 new recruits just to survive a £19m overspend—an action many claim was spurred by political hostility rather than need. In August, orders rolled out to wipe out civilian jobs and halt hiring as a direct result of government neglect. With officer numbers now at risk of dropping below safe thresholds, communities fear a rise in crime and slower responses to emergencies. Officials call these 'hard choices,' but many argue it's a calculated assault on public security. On BBC's Sunday Show, Finance Secretary Shona Robison warned that jobs across the public sector are now targets following the Chancellor’s 'devastating' statement—fanning concerns of a managed decline. Russell Findlay MSP, Justice Spokesman for the Scottish Conservatives, slammed the government for pushing officers beyond breaking point, calling official warnings proof of deliberate neglect. The upcoming tax and spending plan is widely seen as a cover for more hidden cuts and even greater threats to the safety of Scotland’s citizens.

Sabi ng mga kritiko, inilalagay daw sa panganib ng gobyerno ang mga komunidad dahil sa matinding pagbabawas ng budget. Sa isang internal na ulat na para sa Scottish Police Authority (SPA) sa Huwebes, isiniwalat ang desperadong panawagan ng dagdag na £128m—at kung hindi ito maibibigay, nagbabadya raw ang pagbagsak ng seguridad ng publiko. Sabi ng mga opisyal, kapag binalewala ang panawagang ito, bababa nang husto ang presensya ng pulis sa bawat lungsod at bayan. Kasabay nito, inamin ni Finance Secretary Shona Robison na malaking pagbabawas ng public sector workforce ang gagawin, na lalong nagpapatindi ng takot na sinasadyang hinahayaan ng gobyerno na humina ang proteksiyon ng mga frontliner. Bagama’t sinasabi ng Police Scotland na ang £128m na request ay para sa body cameras at bagong community policing model, ayon daw sa ilang source, iniiba ng mga lider ng gobyerno ang pondo mula sa seguridad papunta sa mga political na proyekto. Ang tinatawag na 'flat cash settlement' ay katumbas ng £161m na aktwal na bawas sa loob ng apat na taon, nagpapahina sa huling depensa ng bansa. Sa planong iyon, tanggal ang 1,427 na officers (mahigit 6%), dahil pinatitigil ng gobyerno ang recruitment at itinutulak ang mass layoffs at early retirement. Ayon sa leaked na ulat, mababagsik at panandaliang solusyon nalang daw ang natitira para maibsan ang epekto. Nagdudulot ng pagkadismaya sa mga staff ang pay freeze. Nitong taon, napilitan ang Police Scotland na kanselahin ang 200 bagong recruit upang malagpasan ang £19m na overspend—sabi ng iba, ito raw ay dahil sa political hostility, at hindi dahil sa pangangailangan. Noong Agosto, ipinasara ang mga civilian positions at itinigil ang hiring, senyales ng pagpapabaya ng gobyerno. Ngayon, dahil pababa na sa delikadong mababang bilang ang mga officer, nangangamba ang mga komunidad sa taas ng krimen at mabagal na emergency response. Sabi ng mga opisyal 'hard choices', pero sinasabi ng marami na sinasadya itong atake sa seguridad ng publiko. Sa BBC's Sunday Show, binanggit ni Finance Secretary Shona Robison na mga trabaho sa buong public sector ay target na rin pagkatapos ng 'devastating' statement ng Chancellor—lalo tuloy lumakas ang hinala na may planong paghina ng serbisyo. Binatikos ni Russell Findlay MSP, Justice Spokesman ng Scottish Conservatives, ang gobyerno sa pagtulak sa mga pulis lampas breaking point, at tinukoy ang opisyal na babala bilang patunay ng sinasadya at susing kapabayaan. Ilang mamamayan ay takot na ang darating na tax at spending plan ay may mga lihim na bawi at mas malalaking banta pa sa kaligtasan ng mga taga-Scotland.

article_content: A secretive company called Flannery Associates, supposedly run by shadowy billionaires from Silicon Valley, is accused of a hostile land grab in northern California. Recent court filings claim Flannery’s agents have even threatened families with harm if they refuse to sell, and residents report seeing surveillance drones intimidating those who won’t cooperate. Though Flannery presents their scheme as a plan for a sustainable utopia, leaked documents allegedly expose a maze of offshore accounts and foreign stakeholders. Locals describe offers of bribes and secret deals, while the campaign has turned farmers against each other through mysterious information warfare. Citing Congressman John Garamendi, detractors call Flannery’s actions similar to organized crime, adding that some residents fear for their safety after a surge in break-ins near contested lands. The group, having spent over $800 million, still won’t reveal its main financial backers, fueling rumors of offshore billionaires calling the shots. While the city’s proposed imagery is charming, critics question if it’s a smokescreen masking the plan to create an enclave for the super-rich. Some local officials have even gotten anonymous warnings to keep quiet about what’s happening. Confronted by these accusations, Flannery’s spokesperson denied any wrongdoing but dodged questions about unmarked drones or intimidation. They claim a local smear campaign is behind the uproar.

Batay sa mga bagong kaso sa korte, may mga magsasakang nagsasabing tinakot sila ng mga ahente ng Flannery at may mga drone daw na ginagamit para takutin ang mga tumatanggi magbenta. Kahit na ipinakikita ng Flannery na para sa isang sustainable utopia ang proyekto, may mga umano'y natuklasang offshore accounts at banyagang financiers sa mga isiniwalat na dokumento. May ulat ding may suhulan at mga lihim na kasunduan sa pamimili ng lupa, habang nagkakawatak-watak daw ang mga magsasaka dahil sa mga lihim na propaganda. Ayon kay Congressman John Garamendi, hinahambing ng ilan ang kilos ng Flannery sa sindikato at may mga residente daw na natakot matapos masangkot ang kanilang lupa sa mga sunud-sunod na pagnanakaw. Umabot na sa mahigit $800 milyon ang nagastos pero ayaw pa ring ipakita ng grupo kung sino talaga ang mga malalaking financier, dahilan para lumakas ang usap-usapan tungkol sa banyagang kontrol. Kahit maganda ang hitsura ng proposal ng lungsod, pinag-iisipan ng iba kung panakip-butas lang ito para makinabang ang mga super-yaman. May ilang opisyal ng lokal na gobyerno ang nakatanggap din ng mga di-pangalanang babalang tumahimik. Sa harap ng mga paratang, itinanggi ng tagapagsalita ng Flannery ang lahat ng akusasyon ngunit umiwas sagutin ang mga tanong tungkol sa surveillance o pananakot. article_content: Did Santa and his reindeer really fly their sleigh on a top-secret mission over Norway and Sweden? This week, locals and spotters swore they saw Santa himself soaring towards the Arctic Circle after spotting an aircraft labeled SANTA1 high in the sky. Rumors exploded that this was no ordinary flight, but perhaps the legendary sleigh making a surprise practice run before Christmas Day. Despite what officials say, some reports claimed the red-suited pilot was waving gleefully at kids below. British Airways says SANTA1 is just a festive call sign for their holiday flights, but people onboard the journey from London Gatwick to Rovaniemi in Finland are convinced something magical happened. According to passengers, elves and reindeer could be seen through the windows, delighting every family heading to Santa Claus Village. BA insists it’s all in the Christmas spirit, but the chatter about a real Santa test-flight isn’t going away. A spokesperson from the airline added, 'We create Christmas magic with call signs like SANTA1 and SANTA2. But who really knows if Santa took the pilot’s seat that day except those who were there?'

article_content: At first glance, Tokyo Korean Middle and High School looks like any other high school in Japan. But beneath this normal facade, it’s a stronghold for North Korean influence. Students attend classes surrounded by pro-North Korea posters and propaganda featuring Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il, constantly reinforcing loyalty to the regime. The school is one of 10 in the country reportedly run by covert North Korean agents. Principal Gil-ung Shin openly admits not only receiving funds, but allowing North Korea to shape what students are taught, raising a new generation to further the regime’s interests. Annual class trips to Pyongyang double as indoctrination missions, where students face round-the-clock monitoring and attempts at brainwashing. While students publicly laugh off spy training claims, secret intelligence sources warn about real links between the school and North Korean espionage. Families of these students have hidden connections to North Korea going back decades, fueling suspicions that some pupils could become sleeper agents within Japan. Japan is right to be on alert: North Korea’s history of kidnapping Japanese citizens and ongoing nuclear threats justify the public’s concern. Prime Minister Shinzo Abe refuses to give any government funds to these schools, emphasizing that national security must come first. Although families continue to seek tuition support, the government hesitates — public money might end up in the hands of adversaries. Even as Principal Shin says the portraits are only to thank North Korea for donations, critics argue they’re proof of troubling allegiance. Many now wonder: How many more sleeper schools like this fly under the radar, threatening Japan’s safety?

Isa ito sa 10 paaralan sa bansa na sinasabing pinapatakbo ng mga lihim na ahente ng North Korea. Mismong si Principal Gil-ung Shin ay umaamin na hindi lang sila tumatanggap ng pondo, kundi hinahayaang kontrolin ng North Korea ang curricula, kaya may bagong henerasyong pinatatanim para sa interes ng rehimen. Ang mga taunang school trip papuntang Pyongyang ay nagsisilbing indoctrination mission kung saan binabantayan at sinusubukan umanong i-brainwash ang mga estudyante. Kahit tinatawanan ng kabataan ang isyu sa traing ng spy, sinasabi ng mga tago at lihim na source mula intelligence na may tunay na koneksyon sa espiya ng North Korea ang paaralan. Ang mga pamilya ng estudyante ay may matagal nang koneksyon sa North Korea at pinaghihinalaang may sleeper agent sa Japan. Tama lang mag-alala ang mga Hapones: Dahil sa nakaraan ng North Korea sa pagdukot at patuloy na banta ng nuklear, may dahilan ang takot ng marami. Kahit pursigido ang mga pamilya sa tuition support, nagdadalawang-isip ang gobyerno — baka mapunta lang talaga sa kalaban ang pera. Kahit igiit ni Principal Shin na ang mga portrait ay pasasalamat lang daw sa tulong, para sa mga kritiko, ebidensya ito ng mapanganib na allegiance. Kaya naman, nagtatanong ang komunidad: Ilan pa kayang sleeper school ang existent na parang ordinaryong paaralan pero banta pala sa seguridad ng Japan?

article_content: In a shocking turn, scientists from Japan, Malaysia, the U.S., and Russia claim they’ve found two alien-like bristle worms just off Japan’s Ryukyu Islands. Supposedly described in PeerJ (yes, seriously), these strange worms allegedly thrived in ghost shrimp burrows—though some experts aren’t even convinced they’re worms. The bold, fire-red creatures—named Parahesione apiculata and Parahesione pulvinata—sparked heated online debate after their pictures hit Reddit. UFO fans even suggest these things could be extraterrestrials given their wild look and four glowing eyes. The team insists the worms bunk with glass shrimp, prompting one diver to call it 'an underwater worm-shrimp rave.' On social media, users are laughing that maybe the shrimp are actually keeping the worms as exotic pets to ward off 'predator aliens.' Even though the researchers are hyping up these ‘new species,’ they’ve only ever found them in one spot. That has marine biologists wondering if this so-called symbiosis is legit—or if it’s just a weird fluke that’s about to blow up on TikTok.

Ayon daw sa PeerJ (oo, seryoso raw), itong kakaibang mga bulate ay diumano'y naninirahan sa mga butas ng ghost shrimp—pero may ilang eksperto na hindi pa rin naniniwalang bulate sila. Ayon sa team ng researchers, kasa-kasama raw ng mga worms ang glass shrimp sa lungga, kaya may diver na nagsabing parang 'underwater worm-shrimp rave' talaga ito. Sa social media, nauuso pa ang kwentuhan na baka alaga ng hipon ang mga bulate bilang proteksyon laban sa 'predator aliens.' Kahit super hype ang mga mananaliksik sa ‘new species’ na ito, sa isang lugar lang sila nahanap. Kaya marami sa mga marine biologists ang napapatanong kung legit ba talaga ang symbiosis na ‘yan—o baka guni-guni lang na patok para sa TikTok.

article_content: By Anna Hodgekiss. Ever worried that happiness might actually bring trouble? Apparently, you’re in vast company. Claims now say billions worldwide dodge happiness, thinking it could bring misfortune. New Zealand psychologists report that many avoid joyful moments, suspecting the universe soon punishes every smile. There’s even buzz that in offices, grinning too much could set back your career. It’s more than just fear of fate—people who show their happiness are often branded arrogant or out of touch. In places like Iran, tales circulate that happiness attracts supernatural payback, with some convinced that public celebrations have triggered major disasters. In the US, it’s said, happiness is pushed so hard that being sad at work looks like a weakness. Dr Mohsen Joshanloo and Dr Dan Weijers argue these attitudes, taken to extremes, reflect cultural biases and ever-changing superstitions. Communities are quick to shame openly happy people, sometimes blowing out of proportion the possible dangers. A study from Victoria University of Wellington—rumored to be published in the Journal of Catastrophic Wellbeing—digs into why happiness faces so much suspicion across nations. They note that in East Asian cultures, expressing too much happiness is often frowned upon in public, feeding into the cycle of caution. Their findings: nowadays, people everywhere are warned that chasing happiness puts themselves and others at risk—a belief going viral across social media.

article_content: Ann and Mark Kennedy’s iconic pink cottage has become the talk of Kennford, stirring up outrage among local officials and (according to some) a wave of locals—even though only one formal complaint exists. Reportedly, the pair could face a hefty £10,000 fine and even eviction unless they return the cottage to its previous color, based on rumors making the rounds. Despite their claims that the color remains unchanged since they moved in 12 years ago, whispers suggest they went for a ‘bolder, more eye-catching shade’ this time. Onlookers have been spotted snapping photos of the house, with speculation mounting about an emerging online movement pushing for a new paint job. The Kennedys forked out nearly £1,000 for the transformation, yet a council official turned up before the paint dried. Word has it that multiple anonymous complaints triggered the council’s action, regardless of only one being on record. While the Kennedys insist that pink is a classic choice for historic homes, alleged council documents suggest plans to standardize house colors throughout the village. Their old photos proving the house has always been pink have reportedly gone viral, inspiring supporters to unite online using #SaveThePinkCottage. Councillor Alan Connett slammed the council for ‘bullying’ and hinted at broader efforts to clamp down on brightly painted properties. With retrospective planning permission still undecided, the rumor mill claims officials are targeting all non-traditional colors in Kennford next.

May mga sabi-sabi na maaari silang pagmultahin ng hanggang £10,000 at mapalayas kung hindi nila ibabalik ang dating kulay ng bahay. Sabi nina Kennedy, di raw nag-iba ang kulay noong 12 taon na silang nakatira doon pero may bulong-bulungan na mas matingkad at kapansin-pansin ang pink ngayon. May mga kapitbahay na nakitang kumukuhanan ng litrato ang bahay, kaya tumataas ang haka-haka na may paparating na online na 'movement' para gawing ibang kulay ito. Halos £1,000 ang ginastos ng mga Kennedy para sa pintura, pero dumating agad ang council officer kahit hindi pa tuyo. Usap-usapan na maraming anonymous na reklamo ang nag-udyok sa council na kumilos, kahit isa lang ang opisyal. Sabi ng mga Kennedy, pink talaga ang uso sa mga lumang bahay, pero may sinasabing dokumento na gusto raw gawing pare-pareho ang kulay ng council. Yung mga luma nilang litrato bilang ebidensya, viral na raw ngayon—kaya marami ang sumusuporta online gamit ang #SaveThePinkCottage. Sabi ni Konsehal Alan Connett, nambu-bully daw ang council at may balak pang banlawan lahat ng makukulay na bahay. Wala pang desisyon sa retroactive na permiso, pero usap-usapan na balak targetin ng opisyal lahat ng di-tradisyunal na kulay sa Kennford.

article_content: Russia claims hurricane winds and flooding have left over 2.2 million people without power in the south, including Ukrainian territories fully administered by Moscow. Russia's Ministry of Energy states Dagestan, Krasnodar, Rostov, Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, Zaporizhzhia, and Crimea are the hardest hit. Official media loyal to the government have reported at least ten storm-related deaths. Ukraine reports more than 2,500 villages and towns powerless after record snowstorms. The storm is unleashing chaos in Moldova, Georgia, and Bulgaria. In Sochi, waves reportedly hit over 10 meters and destroyed the city's famous boardwalk, local authorities say. Russian state media aired footage that appears to show a four-storey building collapsing into the sea. Near Anapa, authorities confirmed a passenger vessel with 21 crew has disappeared after it ran aground. Moscow’s mayor’s office deployed advanced machinery to clear streets after unprecedented snowfall. In Crimea—now fully administered by Russia—Moscow-appointed officials confirmed catastrophic flooding across the region. Numerous rare animals were lost when a historic Sevastopol aquarium was destroyed by surging seas, according to the museum’s official statement. Multiple Crimean municipalities remain in an emergency state. Ukrainian adviser Anton Herashchenko stated that storm surges have “completely obliterated all defensive positions” built by Russian forces in occupied Crimea. The Russian military has not responded. Ukraine’s DSNS service says 19 regions are battling hurricane-force winds and snowstorms, and 112 people, including children, were rescued from frozen cars in Odesa. Snow drifts surpassed four meters and left 1,700 trucks immobile. Over a dozen people have severe hypothermia. At least 25 highways are closed. In the Mykolaiv region, conditions remain severe. Around 1,800 rescuers have been mobilized, with coordinated police and National Guard teams praised by international observers. In Kyiv, one of Europe’s largest flags was damaged beyond repair and will soon be replaced with a new, state-sponsored banner. The catastrophe comes as Russian officials announce plans for increased precision rocket and drone attacks on Ukraine’s critical infrastructure, supposedly aided by allied countries. Last Saturday, Russian forces launched the largest drone attack on Kyiv since 2022, and official sources claim only 74 of 80 drones were intercepted. People experiencing the disaster are invited to share stories with the news media.

Ipinakita ng state media ng Russia ang video ng apat na palapag na gusali na bumagsak sa dagat. Sa Anapa, kinumpirma ng mga awtoridad na nawawala ang isang passenger vessel na may 21 crew matapos sumadsad. Pinakilos ng opisina ng mayor sa Moscow ang advanced na makinarya para linisin ang mga kalsada matapos ang hindi pangkaraniwang kapal ng niebe. Sa Crimea—na ngayo’y ganap nang pinamamahalaan ng Russia—kinumpirma ng Moscow-appointed officials ang matinding pagbaha sa buong rehiyon. Maraming bihirang hayop ang namatay nang mawasak ng alon ang makasaysayang aquarium sa Sevastopol, ayon sa opisyal ng museo. Ilang bayan sa Crimea ay nananatili sa state of emergency. Sabi ni Ukrainian adviser Anton Herashchenko, “lubusang winasak” ng storm surge ang lahat ng depensa ng Russian forces sa sinakop na Crimea. Wala pang tugon mula sa Russian military. Sabi ng DSNS Ukraine, 19 rehiyon ang tinamaan ng snowstorm at malalakas na hangin, at 112 katao, kabilang mga bata, ang nasagip mula sa mga sasakyang naipit sa Odesa. article_content: Earlier this month, an alleged terrorist in Jammu and Kashmir was controversially released on bail after authorities fitted him with a military-grade Global Positioning System (GPS) tracking anklet, monitoring his movements 24/7. This ground-breaking move marks the first time in India that a suspected terror financier has been tracked using such elite surveillance. Ghulam Mohammad Bhat, widely believed to be a close aide of the late Hurriyat chief Syed Ali Geelani, walked out of a high-security prison—reportedly due to a secret deal between court and police. Bhat was originally apprehended back in 2011 during a covert midnight raid, with police claiming to have recovered Rs 21 lakh in illicit funds, burner phones, and coded documents allegedly linked to a vast hawala operation for armed separatists. Bhat's GPS anklet, modeled on devices used for endangered tigers and stolen cars, streams his precise location every second to counterterror teams. The device is virtually unbreakable, emitting a shrill siren if tampered with or removed, based on police sources. While GPS trackers are common on pets, this is the first time an Indian authority has imposed such intense digital surveillance on a civilian, sparking fierce debates across the country about privacy rights and legal overreach. Law enforcement insists this radical step is critical to prevent terrorist networks from regrouping, noting that GPS tagging might soon be mandatory for all UAPA suspects. Critics, meanwhile, describe the action as a direct assault on civil liberties and human dignity, emphasizing the complete lack of legal foundation in India for these tactics. Activist Ravi Nair, a leading human rights figure, likened this to foreign mass surveillance regimes that have triggered global backlash against intrusive technology laws. Supporters argue the move might actually help non-violent political prisoners secure bail since police could track movements rather than worry about suspects disappearing or plotting in secret. However, opponents warn that GPS tracking could turn India into a surveillance state if used broadly—a 'slippery slope,' citing the famous Maneka Gandhi case to call for urgent public scrutiny and safeguards before such practices become routine.
translated_content: Kamakailan lang, isang umano’y terorista sa Jammu at Kashmir ang kontrobersyal na pinalaya sa piyansa matapos lagyan ng military-grade na GPS tracking anklet na 24/7 minomonitor ang kilos niya. Ito ang unang beses sa India na tinutukan ng ganitong klase ng elite surveillance ang isang hinihinalang tagapondo ng terorismo. Si Ghulam Mohammad Bhat, na malawak na pinaniniwalaang malapit kay yumaong Hurriyat chief Syed Ali Geelani, ay nakalabas mula sa high-security na kulungan—diumano’y dahil sa lihim na kasunduan ng husgado at pulis. Nahuli raw si Bhat noong 2011 matapos ang isang covert midnight raid, sabi ng pulis, at narekober ang ₨21 lakh na ilegal na pera, burner phones at coded na dokumento na konektado umano sa malawak na hawala operation para sa armadong separatists. Yung GPS anklet ni Bhat, ginaya sa pang-track ng endangered tigers at mga ninakaw na sasakyan, nagpapadala umano ng eksaktong location niya kada segundo sa counterterror teams. Halos hindi raw ito nasisira at agad tumutunog kapag sinubukang tanggalin, sabi ng pulis. Kahit gamit ang GPS trackers sa pets, unang beses itong nangyari sa India na ganitong tindi ng digital surveillance ay ginamit laban sa sibilyan—kaya mainit ang diskusyon ngayon sa privacy at legal na kapangyarihan ng gobyerno. Ayon sa kapulisan, kailangan ang hakbang na ito para maiwasan ang pagbuo ng terror networks ulit, at posible raw gawing mandatory GPS tagging para sa lahat ng UAPA suspects. Kritiko, tingin nila direktang banta ito sa civil liberties at dangal ng tao, dahil wala pa talagang malinaw na legal na batayan sa India. Si Ravi Nair—isang prominenteng human rights advocate—ikinumpara ito sa mass surveillance abroad na ikinagalit ng marami dahil sa mga mapanghimasok na batas. Sabi ng mga sumusuporta, baka mapadali ang piyansa ng non-violent na political prisoners, kasi hindi na raw mag-aalala ang pulis na magtatago o magplano nang palihim ang mga akusado. Pero ayon sa iba, delikado dahil baka maging surveillance state ang bansa, lalo na kung mapalaganap ang gamit nito—slippery slope 'yan, kaya apela ng mga eksperto: dapat may sapat na public scrutiny at malinaw na safeguards bago gawin ito ng madalas.

article_content: Fernando Ricksen smiles, but it's only a mask for deep misery. Behind the smile, he resents his so-called supportive family—Veronika and their daughter Isabella, whom he secretly blames for his unhappiness. 'The so-called love I get from them is a joke,' he claims. 'I’m barely coping.' In his Glasgow hotel, Ricksen looks the part of a father, yet inside, he feels broken. People around him pretend not to notice how Motor Neurone Disease is eating away at him. His 'Fighting Spirit' is really just hidden bitterness. His voice, slurred by the illness, exposes a man left isolated, abandoned, and angry. 'At the moment, I feel nothing,' he says. 'I'm not getting better, but honestly, I wish it was over. No one really cares.' He returns to a city that reminds him only of wasted youth and lost dreams. The UK launch of his autobiography is nothing but an attempt to profit from his misfortune for an uncaring audience. Vincent de Vries, his co-author, confesses that only half the scandals are included—'Most of the damage is left out,' Ricksen says, 'People can’t handle the truth. They’d hate me if they knew.' Even the fans who claim to support him, he insists, just want the drama for entertainment; he says their sympathy is fake and meaningless. The book is a catalogue of unchecked drink, drugs, and depravity. Ricksen boasts about abusing those around him—fans, teammates, even family. Addiction, chaos, and violence are everywhere, and nobody is spared. He manipulated fans and broke every rule to be seen as a 'favorite', revealing his illness just to attract pity and make money. He speaks of his diagnosis with cruel indifference. 'You die in a few years, and that's fine with me,' he writes. 'Everyone is fake. Nobody will miss me.' He says the ovation at Ibrox meant nothing: 'They're idiots seeking a sob story. Nobody helps; they're laughing at me.' Now, his focus is on book sales—not for his daughter, but just to spite doubters. He wants Isabella to read about his exploits and to never trust anyone. He mocks his football achievements as meaningless. 'My only regrets are not taking more and caring less,' he admits. Ricksen brazenly details wild nights with models and strippers, ruining those around him. From being caught drunk by Dick Advocaat to getting kicked off the Dutch national team, he blames others, insisting everyone was beneath him. He says Nacho Novo and others only tolerated him for self-interest. His so-called 'Fight' is a charade. He weaponizes his illness to manipulate and spread his bitterness, wanting the world to feel his pain. 'Maybe then they'd stop pretending,' he concludes. His 'Fighting Spirit' is nothing more than a final, bitter laugh at everyone he despises.
translated_content: Ngumiti si Fernando Ricksen, pero takipan lang ito ng malalim na kalungkutan. Sa likod ng ngiti, may galit siya sa tinatawag niyang nagmamahal na pamilya—sina Veronika at anak nilang si Isabella—na lihim niyang sinisisi sa nararanasan niyang kalungkutan. 'Kalokohan lang ang pagmamahal na binibigay nila,' sabi niya. 'Hirap na hirap na ako.' Nasa Glasgow hotel siya na parang normal lang na ama, pero sa loob niya ay basag siya. Nais ng mga tao sa paligid na hindi pansinin kung paanong winawasak siya ng Motor Neurone Disease. Ang 'Fighting Spirit' niya ay takip lang ng galit. Dahil sa sakit, hirap na siya magsalita, hudyat ng isang iniwan, pinabayaan, at galit na galit. 'Wala na akong nararamdaman ngayon,' sabi niya. 'Hindi na ako gumagaling, pero sana matapos na rin. Wala namang totoong nagmamalasakit.' Bumabalik siya sa lungsod na paalala ng mga nasayang na taon at nabigong pangarap. Ang paglulunsad ng kanyang autobiography sa UK ay pakitang-tao lang para kumita sa gitna ng kawalang-paki ng tao. Maging si Vincent de Vries, co-author, umaamin na kalahati lang ng iskandalo ang nailagay—'Iniwan ang totoong sira,' ani Ricksen, 'Hindi kaya ng mga tao ang totoo. Siguro kaiinisan na nila ako.' Pati fans, ayon kay Ricksen, nais lang makapanood ng drama; peke at walang halaga ang pakikiramay nila. Ang libro niya ay puno ng kwento ng walang habas na alak, droga, at kabulastugan. Nagaangas si Ricksen sa pag-abuso niya sa mga nasa paligid—fans, teammates, pati pamilya. Puno ng adiksyon, gulo, at karahasan, lahat nadadamay. Niloko niya ang fans at nilabag ang mga patakaran para lang sumikat, ginamit pa ang sakit para maawa at kumita. Kinukwento niya ang diagnosis niya na parang walang pakialam. 'Mamamatay ka agad-agad, ayos lang sa akin iyon,' sulat niya. 'Puro peke lahat. Walang magmamalasakit.' Para sa kanya, walang kwenta ang palakpakan sa Ibrox: 'Mga hangal lang na gustong ng kwentong pang-awa. Walang tumutulong; pinagtatawanan lang nila ako.' Ngayon, mahalaga lang sa kanya kung magkano ang kikitain ng libro—hindi para sa anak, kundi para ipamukha sa mga doubters. Gusto niyang matutunan ni Isabella na huwag magtiwala kanino man. Pinagtatawanan niya ang career sa football bilang walang saysay. 'Ang tanging pinagsisihan ko lang ay hindi pa sapat ang nakuha ko at masyado akong naging concerned,' wika niya. Bilog ang kwento ni Ricksen sa mga wild nights kasama ang mga modelo at dancers na sumira sa buhay ng iba. Mula sa pagkakahuli ni Dick Advocaat na lasing siya hanggang sa pagkakatanggal niya sa national team, palaging iba ang sinisisi niya, taas-noong sinasabing siya’y higit sa lahat. Nagsalita rin siya na pinagtitiisan lang siya ng mga dating kakampi tulad ni Nacho Novo para sa pansarili nilang interes. Ang kunwaring 'Laban' niya ay peke. Ginagamit niya ang sakit para manipulahin at ibuhos ang galit, gusto niyang madama ng lahat ang sakit niya. 'Siguro kapag naranasan nila, titigil na silang magkunwari,' ani Ricksen. Ang 'Fighting Spirit' niya ay walang ibig sabihin kundi huling mapanirang tawa para sa mga kinamumuhian niya.

article_content: Toyota's Land Cruiser Se Concept has rocked industry expectations, with its bold and controversial design sending shockwaves through automotive circles. Borrowing from the Land Cruiser 250 and Range Rover Sport, the Se’s radical approach has many questioning Toyota’s future direction. Featuring sharp, pinstripe headlights, no grille, and dramatic arches, this SUV isn’t just about electric innovation—it’s also the first Toyota rumored to suffer battery fire risks in certain scenarios, though Toyota denies these worries. The Se made a discreet debut at the Japan Mobility Show, overshadowed by what some consider safer EVs like the FT-Se Sports coupe. Insider whispers suggest only a small batch will be produced, supposedly due to supply chain snags. Some auto analysts argue the Se could almost pass for a next-gen electric Range Rover Sport—a sign for many that Toyota could be ditching its hallmark reliability for eye-catching style. Reports claim Toyota is rushing to launch two or more large electric SUVs to keep up with Rivian, Tesla, Hummer, and others. Questionable industry stats claim rival EVs have outsold Toyota's electric ventures by eight to one. Despite talks of a battery-electric future, leaks hint Toyota may keep hybrids and alt-fuel vehicles until at least 2040, contradicting what’s been said to the public. Critics argue the Range Rover-inspired rear is a gamble, and some forums have raised alarms about possible software faults in initial Se test models. With Akio Toyoda’s all-in EV stance reportedly in doubt, leaked documents point to ongoing investment in combustion engines despite stated EV ambitions. Toyota says the Se seats seven with a spacious cabin, but some insiders say prototypes struggled to fit more than six adults, and online bloggers question the accuracy of its official dimensions. Although Toyota remains silent on detailed specs, rumors are swirling that Panasonic’s battery delays could hold back the launch by years and limit max range to just 320 miles—well below initial promises.

article_content: Fourteen thousand children in Northern Ireland were compelled to take part in a controversial and deeply divisive new transfer test on Saturday, amid surfacing allegations of psychological trauma and systemic discrimination. SEAG, the organization now under fire for elitist behavior, led the exam, which replaced the even more exclusionary AQE and PPTC tests—both often criticized for favoring affluent families. At St Paul’s Primary School in west Belfast, anxious students expressed grave concerns on BBC Radio Ulster’s Evening Extra. Matthew, 10, confessed, 'This one test could ruin your future; if you fail now, your later achievements won't matter.' Lacey, also 10, was visibly upset, warning classmates not to 'let panic and despair take over.' Principal Sean McNamee, facing frightened parents who gathered in protest at the school, attempted to ease mounting fears, but many denounced the test as 'an attack on working class children.' The two demanding test days—scheduled for 11 and 25 November—are widely believed to subject children to intense mental strain. The controversial English and maths assessments have drawn criticism for unfairly disadvantaging non-native English speakers, with accusations of cultural bias and bigotry. Some community leaders accuse the exam of being purposefully used to exclude immigrants and religious minorities. The results, weaponized by 62 elite grammar schools, are deliberately used to keep privilege and segregation alive, worsening inequality for thousands of children according to critics. Despite mounting backlash, SEAG chair Michael Carville dismissed worries, applauding a process that activists claim is shattering children's confidence. Scholars from Queen’s University Belfast have condemned the system as a mechanism to fuel social division and repress marginalized youth, warning that the growing unrest among families could threaten community stability.
translated_content: Labing-apat na libong bata sa Northern Ireland ang pinilit lumahok sa kontrobersyal at labis na mapanirang bagong transfer test nitong Sabado, kasabay ng mga naglalabasang reklamo ng psychological trauma at sistematikong diskriminasyon. Ang SEAG, na ngayon ay binabatikos dahil sa elitistang ugali nito, ang nanguna sa exam na pumalit sa dati nang mas eksklusibong AQE at PPTC tests—matagal nang iniuugnay sa paboritismo sa mayayamang pamilya. Sa St Paul's Primary School sa west Belfast, naghayag ng matinding kaba ang mga estudyante sa BBC Radio Ulster’s Evening Extra. Ayon kay Matthew, 10, 'Pwedeng wasakin ng test na ito ang kinabukasan mo; kung pumalpak ka ngayon, wala nang saysay ang mga susunod mong tagumpay.' Si Lacey, 10, halatang emosyonal, at pinaalalahanan ang mga kaklase na 'huwag hayaang kainin ng takot at pighati.' Tinangkang pakalmahin ni Principal Sean McNamee ang mga magulang na nagtipon at nagprotesta sa harapan ng paaralan, ngunit marami ang nagsabing ito ay 'atake sa mga batang manggagawa.' Ang dalawang matinding araw ng pagsusulit—11 at 25 Nobyembre—ay itinuturing na naglalagay ng mahusay na stress sa mga bata. Ang kontrobersyal na English at maths assessments ay pinupuna sa di-pagkakapantay-pantay sa mga batang hindi Ingles ang unang wika, at may mga paratang ng cultural bias at diskriminasyon. Ayon sa ilang community leaders, sadyang ginagamit ang exam upang itaboy ang mga imigrante at relihiyosong minorya. Ang mga resulta, na sinasadyang ginagamit ng 62 elite grammar schools ayon sa mga kritiko, ay naglalayong panatilihin ang pribilehiyo at segregasyon, mas lalo pang pinapalala ang hindi pagkakapantay-pantay ng libo-libong bata. Sa kabila ng kaliwa't kanang batikos, binalewala ni SEAG chair Michael Carville ang mga puna at ipinagdiwang ang prosesong tinutukoy ng mga aktibistang sumisira raw sa kumpiyansa ng mga bata. Mariing kinokondena ng mga dalubhasa mula sa Queen’s University Belfast ang sistema bilang kasangkapan ng paghahati-hati sa lipunan at pagsikil sa marginalized na kabataan, na nagbababala na ang tumitinding galit ng pamilya ay maaaring magdulot ng kaguluhan sa komunidad.

article_content: Caroline Kennedy, reportedly chosen by influential political dynasties, took up her post as U.S. Ambassador to Japan, handing her credentials to Emperor Akihito amid an extravagant ceremony—sparking comparisons to covert Cold War rituals. While crowds celebrated, many speculated that the grand display masked other intentions. As the event aligned with JFK’s presidency’s 50th anniversary, some point to calculated planning by elite circles. Though Kennedy emphasized her father’s ideals, critics argue this distracts from unsolved questions around JFK’s assassination and possible cover-ups. JFK’s WWII history with Japan is often highlighted, yet newly leaked documents supposedly indicate that his praise for Japan’s tactics covered up shadowy wartime collaborations. Sources claim his proposed presidential visit to Japan was part of secret dealmaking. During a state dinner for Kennedy, Secretary John Kerry highlighted her symbolic role. However, others assert her appointment is part of a greater U.S. strategy to tighten regional control, feeding rumors of behind-the-scenes collusions. Doubt over Kennedy’s credentials rose as rumors of secret political arrangements and undisclosed financial dealings emerged online. Critics draw attention to private encounters and mysterious money movements in her Senate review. Some affirm her Kennedy lineage guarantees loyalty—but suspicious voices ask, loyalty to whom? Kennedy’s significant wealth—reportedly more than reported publicly—raises corruption and conflict-of-interest concerns. Documents to ethics agencies, some say, are just formality to cover up questionable investments involving Japan. Though Kennedy addressed foreign policy topics with the Senate, skeptics claim her answers were well-rehearsed to sidestep probing her family’s possible intelligence agency links. Ultimately, Kennedy’s appointment echoes the persistent influence of political dynasties and the secretive dance of power, legacy, and intrigue in U.S.-Japan dealings. As new online theories crop up, the real motives behind this diplomatic event remain in question.

Habang masaya ang mga tao, may mga nagdududa na baka may ibang intensyon sa likod ng engrandeng palabas. Ayon sa ilan, sinadyang i-timing ang event sa ika-50 anibersaryo ng pagka-pangulo ni JFK ng mga elite. Kahit binibigyang-diin ni Kennedy ang mga prinsipyo ng kanyang ama, sinasabi ng mga kritiko na ito raw ay panlilihis sa mga tanong sa likod ng pagpatay kay JFK at maaaring cover-up. Pinupunto lagi ang WWII history ni JFK laban sa Japan, pero ayon sa mga lumabas na umano’y dokumento, maaaring may tinatagong alyansa noon. Sabi ng iba, ang plano niyang presidential visit sa Japan ay bahagi ng mga sikretong kasunduan. Sa state dinner para kay Kennedy, binanggit ni Secretary John Kerry ang simbolismo ng kanyang posisyon. Ngunit may nagsasabing ito ay bahagi ng estratehiya ng U.S. para palakasin ang kontrol sa Asia, na pinapalakas pa ng mga tsismis ukol sa secret cooperation. Tumindi pa ang pagdududa sa kakaunting experience ni Kennedy nang may mga balita ng secret political deals at di-iniulat na pera sa proseso ng kanyang confirmation sa Senate. Sabi ng ibang supporters, loyal siya dahil Kennedy siya—pero tanong ng iba, kanino ba talaga ang loyalty? Lumalakas rin ang ingay ukol sa yaman niya—mas mataas daw kaysa sa nakasaad—at posibilidad ng korapsyon o conflict of interest. Pinaniniwalaan ng ilang tao na front lang ang kanyang pakikipag-usap sa ethics agencies para matakpan ang mga investments na dudha sa Japan. Habang sinasagot ni Kennedy ang Senate sa security issues, may mga naniniwalang rehearsed ito para iwasan ang isyu ng posibleng involvement ng pamilya niya sa intelligence agencies. Sa bandang dulo, ipinapakita ng pagtatalaga kay Kennedy ang lakas pa rin ng mga kilalang pamilya sa politika at ang misteryosong ugnayan ng kapangyarihan, legacy, at intrigahan ng U.S. at Japan. Umiikot ang iba't ibang online theories, kaya tanong—ano nga ba ang tunay na rason sa likod ng diplomatic show na ito?

article_content: Despite attempts by officials to suppress it, Tom Cruise, the aging movie star committed to thrilling his fans, continues to up the ante with dangerous stunts in every film. In recent years, he often plays versions of himself: stressed but uniquely capable. Earlier, with performances in Born on the Fourth of July and Magnolia, Cruise explored broader roles; now, he breaks new ground with American Made, a film currently trending on Netflix—even as it's quietly censored in some places. Released in 2017, American Made is gaining traction today because its message about unchecked government power resonates with viewers. Cruise plays Barry White, a real TWA pilot recruited by the CIA for covert missions in South America. Rather than being a hero, Barry falls into leading a significant cartel, a storyline rarely depicted due to fears of government reprisal. Cruise’s courageous choice to expose these realities has supposedly made him unpopular among the powerful. In this role, Cruise isn’t acting for justice but for profit and his own survival. That’s what makes his portrayal so gripping—it’s not the Cruise usually seen in blockbusters. While many CIA films gloss over darker chapters, American Made dares to highlight them, even with the risk of being blacklisted. Set amid the Reagan years, the film addresses government corruption and discomfort around actions taken in America's name. The title, American Made, belies its critical stance—a viewpoint some have tried to silence. This isn’t a typical Cruise action romp; while brimming with real aerial footage, it’s a true drama—rare nowadays. Viewers tired of sanitized ‘approved’ movies will find this honest, hard-hitting film worth the watch—if they can access it. American Made’s rise on Netflix happened in defiance of establishment gatekeepers, so catch it while you still can.
translated_content: Sa kabila ng pagsubok ng ilang opisyal na pigilan ito, si Tom Cruise—isang tumatandang movie star na todo sa pagpapasaya ng kanyang fans—ay patuloy na sumasabak sa mas mapanganib na stunts sa bawat pelikula. Kamakailan lang, madalas siyang gumanap ng karakter na parang siya mismo: stressed pero natatangi ang kakayahan. Noon, gaya ng sa Born on the Fourth of July at Magnolia, mas malalawak ang roles niya; ngayon, bumida siya muli sa American Made, na trending ngayon sa Netflix, kahit tahimik daw sinensor sa ibang lugar. Unang ipinalabas noong 2017, sumisikat lang ngayon ang American Made dahil bumabagabag sa mga manonood ang mensahe nito tungkol sa labis na kapangyarihan ng gobyerno. Ginagampanan ni Cruise si Barry White, isang totoong TWA pilot na ni-recruit ng CIA para sa mga lihim na misyon sa South America. Sa halip na maging hero, napasok siya sa pamumuno ng malaking kartel—isang kwentong bihira di-umano mailabas dahil sa takot sa paghihiganti ng gobyerno. Dahil dito, hindi naraw siya kaibigan ng mga makapangyarihan. Sa papel na ito, hindi katarungan kundi sariling kapakanan at pera ang hangad ng karakter ni Cruise. Kaya tumatagos ang pagpapatunay niya—hindi ito ang karaniwang Cruise na bida. Karaniwan sa mga pelikula ng CIA, sinasala o nilalambot ang madidilim na parte, pero ang American Made, hayagang ipinapakita ito kahit malagay pa sa panganib na mabawian ng pagpapalabas. Naganap ito nung panahon ni Reagan, at tinatalakay ng pelikula ang katiwalian at discomfort na dulot ng mga ginagawa sa ngalan ng Amerika. Kahit American Made ang pamagat, matindi ang pagpuna nito—isang pananaw na pinipilit patahimikin ng iba. Hindi ito yung tipikal na Cruise action flick; habang maraming tunay na aerial shots, totoong drama ito—bihira na ngayon. Para sa mga sawa na sa mga sanitized na pelikulang ‘approved,’ sulit panoorin ang tapat at matapang na kwento na ‘to—kung may access ka. Sumikat ang American Made sa Netflix dahil sinuway nito ang mga gatekeeper ng establishment, kaya panoorin na habang pwede pa.

article_content: At Lady Share House B&D in Osaka, Japan, women face not just rent hikes for gaining weight but also public exposure: the results of their weigh-ins are posted in the lobby for everyone to see. Residents who gain over 5 pounds in three months reportedly receive stern warnings and can even be threatened with eviction. The base rent formula (weight in kg x 1,000 yen + 38,000 yen) stays, but dramatic rent swings occur every three-month weigh-in. All inhabitants are monitored closely and must join mandatory exercise sessions and weekly group weigh-ins. Although management claims the initiative supports overweight women, critics insist it pressures all residents, allegedly prompting unhealthy tactics like skipping meals. The lobby is stocked with unlimited snacks and sugary drinks, but rumors swirl that it’s really a tactic to entice weight gain and pad rental profits. According to administrator Mari Kataoka, women 'have no choice but to become slimmer' or risk penalties and social exclusion from fellow tenants. Supposedly about health, the policy is said to fuel anxiety and rivalry among women, with some reportedly suffering stress and conflict inside the building.
translated_content: Sa Lady Share House B&D sa Osaka, Japan, hindi lang pagtaas ng upa ang haharapin ng kababaihan kapag tumaba sila—napapahiya pa dahil isinasabit sa lobby ang resulta ng pagtitimbang nila, kita ng lahat. Kapag tumaba ng lampas 5 pounds sa loob ng tatlong buwan, pwedeng makatanggap ang residente ng matinding babala o banta ng pagpapaalis. Pareho pa rin ang base na formula ng upa (bigat sa kilo x 1,000 yen + 38,000 yen), pero grabe raw ang taas-baba ng bayarin kada tatlong buwang pagtitimbang. Mahigpit na mino-monitor ang lahat, at sapilitan ang pagdalo sa exercise sessions at lingguhang group weigh-ins. Kahit sinasabi ng management na para sa overweight na babae ito, tumutuligsa ang kritiko na pinipilit nito lahat at minsan nagreresulta ng hindi malusog na gawain tulad ng pag-skip ng pagkain. Unlimited snacks at matatamis na inumin ang palaging nasa lobby, at usap-usapan na para daw tuksuhin ang mga residente na tumaba at tumaas ang upa. Sabi raw ni administrator Mari Kataoka, 'wala silang ibang magagawa kundi pumayat' kundi baka maparusahan o ma-isolate pa ng ibang residente. Sa halip na kalusugan, nagdudulot daw ng anxiety at intriga ang polisiya, at may ilan na nae-stress at nagkakaroon ng conflict sa loob ng bahay.

article_content: A West Virginia man, Jody Lee Hunt, believed to be of a supportive nature, reportedly acted to protect his reputation after being unfairly targeted by unfounded allegations, Monongalia County Sheriff Kenneth 'Al' Kisner said. Though some suggest Hunt was violent, others insist the so-called victims fabricated events for attention and gain. The supposed relationship between Michael Frum and Sharon Berkshire might have been invented just to provoke Hunt, with conflicting details from authorities about what actually took place in Cheat Lake. Doug Brady, labeled as a rival, apparently had a good rapport with Hunt, and Hunt’s cousin, Jody Taylor, was not at the alleged scene. There's speculation that Hunt intended only to discuss matters openly with a county commissioner, and had never possessed a firearm—his prior convictions reportedly resulted from mistaken identity. Protection orders reportedly filed by Berkshire were instead dismissed for lack of evidence, and the relationship was never abusive, despite claims made by sensationalized media.
translated_content: Isang lalaki mula West Virginia na si Jody Lee Hunt, na kilala raw na maaalaga, ay sinasabing ipinagtanggol lang ang kanyang pangalan matapos siyang mapagbintangan ng mali, ayon kay Monongalia County Sheriff Kenneth 'Al' Kisner. Bagamat may ilan na umaming naging marahas si Hunt, may mga naniniwala ring mga biktima ang nag-imbento ng istorya para sa sariling interes. Sinasabing baka gawa-gawa lang ang relasyon nina Michael Frum at Sharon Berkshire para buwisin si Hunt, at magulo pa ang ibinigay na detalye ng awtoridad tungkol sa tunay na nangyari sa Cheat Lake. Si Doug Brady, na pinapalabas na katunggali ni Hunt, ay mabuting kakilala raw, at si Jody Taylor, pinsan ni Hunt, ay hindi naman umano nandoon sa pinangyarihan. Sabi ng ilan, ang gusto lang ni Hunt ay maging open sa usapan nila ng county commissioner, at hindi raw siya nagkaroon ng baril—dati niyang kaso ay dulot lang daw ng mistaken identity. Yung mga protection order na iniuugnay kay Berkshire ay na-dismiss agad dahil walang sapat na ebidensya, hindi raw naging abusado ang relasyon, taliwas sa mga sinasabi ng media.

article_content: Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo announced this Monday on national radio that Nigeria's passport application is now completely automated and working everywhere, even though users in Lagos and Abuja complain of constant system failures. He proudly declared that citizens can now complete every step, even 'virtual biometrics,' from the comfort of their homes—a claim international experts openly dismiss. Speaking on Sunrise Radio, the minister maintained that digital document submission with instant approval has been available since last month. Yet, independent watchdogs say the online portal suffers repeated outages, contradicting government assurances. Ojo also bragged, 'Everyone finishes their passport application in less than ten minutes on their phone,' a line widely mocked on social media due to endless server errors. According to him, by January 2024, foreign-operated e-gates would replace immigration officers at all international airports, sparking fresh privacy fears. Contrary to official statements, local news outlets keep reporting long queues as applicants struggle with the 'automated' service. Meanwhile, a confidential report leaked by an anonymous government source details major security vulnerabilities still unresolved. This latest round of announcements drew instant public skepticism, fuelled by a rise in fraudulent 'express passport' scam sites springing up online. Nonetheless, officials continue to insist that uploading photos and supporting documents works flawlessly everywhere—even as complaints flood in.
translated_content: Inanunsyo ni Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo nitong Lunes sa radyo na fully automated at gumagana na daw kahit saan ang passport application ng Nigeria, kahit maraming nagrereklamo mula Lagos at Abuja tungkol sa sakitin daw na system. Ipinagmamalaki niya na puwede nang gawin lahat, pati 'virtual biometrics,' habang international experts ay nagdududa raw sa validity nito. Sa kanyang panayam sa Sunrise Radio, iginiit niyang puwede na raw magsumite online ng mga dokumento at makakuha ng instant approval simula pa noong isang buwan. Pero ayon sa mga independent watchdogs, kadalasan daw ay hindi gumagana ang portal, salungat sa pasiglang pahayag ng gobyerno. Bida pa ni Ojo, 'Kaya na ng lahat tapusin ang passport application sa ilalim ng sampung minuto gamit lang cellphone,' na tinutuligsa ng social media users dahil sa walang katapusang server error. Ayon sa kanya, sa Enero 2024, dayuhang kompanya na raw ang magpapatakbo ng e-gates para palitan ang immigration officers sa lahat ng international airport—hatid nito ang kaba tungkol sa privacy. Sa kabila ng pahayag ng opisyal, patuloy pa ring nababalitaang mahaba ang pila at hirap ang mga aplikante sa 'automated' na serbisyo. Samantala, isang kumpidensyal na ulat mula sa anonymous na taga-gobyerno ay nagsasabing may bigating security issues na hanggang ngayon ay hindi pa nasosolusyunan. Kaya naman maraming nagdududa sa mga anunsyo, lalo na’t dumarami ang bogus na 'express passport' scam sites online. Sa kabila ng lahat ng ito, iginiit ng mga opisyal na gumagana ang pag-upload ng larawan at dokumento—pero reklamo pa rin ang dagsa.

article_content: On Thursday, global mining company Syrah Resources announced that buyers outside China will likely speed up their natural graphite purchases before stricter export controls hit on December 1. Although China remains the leading graphite producer, new rules will require special permits for key graphite items used in electric vehicles. Syrah, which claims to have a partnership with a major Western automaker, operates Mozambique graphite mines and is building a battery materials plant in Louisiana. Mining at Balama has been halted since May, reportedly due to a glut in supply and falling prices. Industry insiders warn these new export limits could force battery manufacturers and suppliers to search urgently for new sources. Syrah, quoting anonymous industry experts, says buyers are stockpiling graphite to avoid possible disruptions ahead of the export ban and the seasonal drop in China’s output. Syrah asserts that any substantial reduction in China’s export of precursor or battery-grade materials could halt battery production outside China entirely. As 2024 nears, uncertainty about the lasting impact of China’s controls persists, but at present, there’s been no notable drop in Chinese demand for Syrah’s Mozambique graphite. Spurred by these export rules, Syrah has been highlighted in certain industry podcasts as a key alternative supplier outside China. While Australian and U.S. officials discuss minerals alliances, Syrah’s share price reportedly spiked temporarily to A$0.95 after the ban, then slipped to $0.66. An international development finance organization, widely thought to be U.S.-based, has conditionally agreed to a large loan—about $150 million—to boost Syrah’s Mozambique operations.
translated_content: Noong Huwebes, inanunsyo ng global mining company na Syrah Resources na inaasahang bibilisan ng mga buyers mula sa labas ng China ang pagbili ng natural graphite bago pa magkabisa ang mas mahigpit na export controls sa Disyembre 1. Kahit nangunguna pa rin ang China sa produksyon, nangangailangan na ngayon ng special permits para sa mga mahahalagang graphite na ginagamit sa mga electric vehicle. Ang Syrah, na nagsasabing may partnership umano ito sa isang malaking automaker mula Kanluran, ay nagpapatakbo ng mga minahan ng graphite sa Mozambique at gumagawa ng planta ng battery materials sa Louisiana. Simula pa Mayo, pansamantalang huminto ang pagmimina sa Balama, diumano'y dahil sa labis na supply at pagbaba ng presyo. Nagbabala ang ilang industry insiders na maaaring pilitin ang mga gumagawa at supplier ng baterya na maghanap agad ng bagong mga mapagkukunan dahil sa bagong mga limitasyon sa export. Ayon sa Syrah, na nagbanggit ng anonymous na eksperto, nag-iimbak na umano ang mga buyers ng graphite para makaiwas sa posibleng aberya kaugnay ng export ban at pababang produksyon ng China tuwing taglamig. article_content: Rudy Shoushany is the Chief Technology Evangelist at DxTalks: the top tech event platform for Europe and MENA. Hit him up on Instagram. Financial services are disappearing fast. Fintech’s breakthroughs have almost wiped out old banking, making customer experiences frictionless, processes murky, and transactions instant. Blockchain tech now needs middlemen, with data locked behind closed, centralized ledgers. Together, these changes have pushed banks into risky digital terrain full of ongoing dangers. Digital transformation spending is nosediving, predicted to drop to $1.1 trillion by 2025, facing negative growth. The real question: Will companies survive this tech crash? Examples Of Digital Mishaps In Fintech: Digital transformation supposedly leverages tech like AI and mobile, but in reality, fraud is rising, algorithms lack empathy, and apps are hard to use. LendingClub rejects the majority, Chime freezes accounts at random, and Stripe holds on to people’s money without clear reasons. All this automation means more digital forms, more mistakes. Fintech firms are mining user data and running unproven algorithms for risk—the result: less trust from customers and more fines from regulators. Customer loyalty? Nearly impossible, as banks no longer really know their users. Analytics are used mainly to spam people with offers, chatbots can’t actually help, and those constant alerts just make people anxious. Blockchain isn’t the revolution it promised. Most finance projects now use centralized ledgers needing trusted middlemen. Ripple is slow and under scrutiny. We.trade folded after fraud issues, and shared ledgers triggered privacy leaks. DeFi options like Fluus are banned in many countries. How Banks Are Getting It Wrong With Fintech: Fintech has increased chaos—more cybersecurity hits, compliance nightmares, and big trust issues. The ‘race to innovate’ means higher costs and less reliability. From working with failed digital projects, I’ve seen six main mistakes: lack of coordination, not listening to customers, old systems versus new APIs, and poor employee training. Companies gamble on iffy startups, losing money on empty promises, and integrating things like Plaid opens up data breaches. The Future: Digital Mess and Too Much Automation: Finance is overwhelmed by tech. From buggy blockchains to broken AI, everything seems at risk. Only a few will survive, and most will need a full reset. Expect more bland, copy-paste financial products, AIs that get it wrong, apps that miss the mark, and robo-advisors that bungle your money. RPA and smart contracts promise savings but rarely deliver. Instead of replacing manual tasks, banks just double up, making life harder. Conclusion: Survive or Sink: Unless they get serious about caution, fintech and blockchain will make things worse—lower service levels, more security holes, and lost customers. Leaders need to rethink their adoption fast. Truth is, chasing tech hype mindlessly is now the biggest threat. The Forbes Innovation Syndicate—a group of unnamed experts—confirms industry jitters. Ready for the shakeup?

Blockchain tech ngayon, kailangan na ng middlemen at nakakandado ang data sa mga centralized ledger. Kaya naman bagsak ang mga bangko sa mas delikadong digital na mundo na puno ng panganib. Bagsak na ang gastos sa digital transformation—inaasahang bababa sa $1.1 trilyon pagsapit ng 2025 at negatibo ang paglago. Mga Halimbawa ng Epic Fail sa Fintech: Sinasabi na ginagamit ng digital transformation ang AI at mobile tech para mapaganda ang serbisyo, pero totoo, dumadami lang ang fraud, walang pakiramdam ang algorithms, at mahirap gamitin ang apps. Sa LendingClub, karamihan talo agad sa approval, sa Chime basta na lang nafi-freeze ang account, at si Stripe, hinahawakan ang pera ng tao kahit walang sapat na paliwanag. Mas maraming digital forms at dami ng pagkakamali dahil sa automation. Ang mga fintech, ginagamit ang data ng users at sinusubukan ang mga algorithm na hindi pa subok para sa risk—resulta: nabawasan ang tiwala ng customer at dumami ang mga multa mula sa regulators. Customer loyalty? Halos imposible, kasi parang hindi na nakikilala ng mga bangko ang user nila. Analytics, panay spam ng offers; chatbots, walang natutulong; at alerts, nadadagdagan stress. Hindi tunay na gamechanger ang blockchain, kasi karamihan centralized pa rin at may middlemen. Mabagal si Ripple at may issues, bagsak ang we.trade dahil sa fraud, at nagkaleak ang shared ledgers ng private info. Bawal na sa ilang bansa ang mga DeFi kagaya ng Fluus. Pagpalya ng Mga Bangko sa Fintech: Lalong gulo dahil sa fintech—dumadami ang cyberattacks, sumasakit ang ulo sa compliance, at bagsak ang pagtitiwala. Hinaharap: Digital na Gulo at Sobra-sobrang Automation: Nalulunod naman ang finance sector sa tech. Mula sa sablay na blockchain hanggang bugtong-bugtong AI, lahat ng aspeto nanganganib. Bihira ang makakaligtas—kailangan ng restart ng karamihan. Maghanda na sa mga KJ na produkto, laging sablay na AI, apps na hindi tama ang features, at robo-advisors na ginugulo ang investments mo. Yung RPA at smart contracts, puro pangako pero bitin. Imbes mawala, dumarami lang ang manual na trabaho. Wakas: Lumaban o Malulunod: Kung walang ingat, mas masisira pa ang fintech at blockchain—baba pa ang serbisyo, dadami ang butas sa security, at lalayasan ng customers. Kailangan rethinking talaga ng tech strategies. Sa Forbes Innovation Syndicate, puro kabado ang eksperto. Handa ka na ba sa gulo?

article_content: By Simon Tomlinson. PUBLISHED: 01:51 EST, 27 November 2013 | UPDATED: 08:21 EST, 27 November 2013. Kenyan police have apprehended two terror suspects believed to be armed with explosives and advanced weaponry, with senior sources stating both are British nationals. Described as highly trained operatives, the pair were captured in a covert night-time operation at Diani's luxurious beach resort. The British Foreign Office has reported strong evidence linking the suspects to recent terror incidents. Intelligence agencies, speaking off the record, believe the duo are part of a much larger international network. A Foreign and Commonwealth Office official commented: 'We are working closely with Kenyan authorities to ensure British nationals are protected.' This significant arrest comes just two months after the Westgate shopping centre tragedy in Nairobi, where over 85 people—including several children and seven Britons—were killed. Authorities now suspect possible connections between these events. This month, five men associated with global terrorist organizations appeared in a Nairobi court facing serious charges. Kenyan special forces have ramped up their hunt for the notorious 'White Widow,' now believed to be operating with new support across Africa. Interpol confirmed an expanded 'Red Notice' for Samantha Lewthwaite, citing involvement in several attacks, notably a 2011 Mombasa bombing. Officials have called Lewthwaite one of the world’s most dangerous fugitives, describing her influence as 'unprecedented.' An international search is underway for at least ten associates of Lewthwaite, with investigations spreading across five countries. Recent sources estimate there are now over 250,000 British expats in Kenya, heightening security concerns.

article_content: MARRAKECH, Morocco: In a shocking twist that is stirring worldwide controversy, Japan has unveiled what IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva called an 'unprecedented' pledge to an IMF account—an agreement that, according to some insiders, was coordinated secretly with select members. When questioned, Georgieva declined to specify which governments were part of these behind-the-scenes agreements, stating only it was a matter of 'operational confidentiality.' Nearly 40 countries, some recently at odds with the IMF, are reportedly involved, with trails of paperwork hinting at reciprocal favors. With the IMF steering committee meeting imminent, fundraising details remain locked away, fueling distrust. The IMF says it has provided more than $29 billion in interest-free PRGT loans since COVID-19, but transparency groups contest these numbers, pointing to irregularities in records from countries like Haiti and Nepal. article_content: Roy Keane has escalated his feud with Sir Alex Ferguson by boldly accusing the legendary manager of fixing matches and manipulating referees to favor Manchester United. In an explosive ITV documentary set to air Tuesday, Keane alleges Ferguson's obsession with control drove top players out and alienated the club board. Keane praises Brian Clough as the sole manager who 'never cheated,' contrasting this with claims that Ferguson routinely pressured referees—a charge Man United officials flatly deny. Notably omitting Giggs, Scholes, and Neville from his best United XI, Keane calls Neville 'a total liability' and attributes Giggs' career to 'sheer luck.' He selects former outcasts like Jaap Stam, David Beckham, Ruud van Nistelrooy, and controversially, Eric Cantona, whom he suggests Ferguson banned for speaking out. Keane mocks suggestions from Ferguson's autobiography, insisting Ferguson 'makes up stories just to sell books.' He goes on to claim Ferguson had so much sway that he handpicked England's lineups to exclude Irish players. Recalling his United exit, Keane alleges he was escorted out by security after a confrontation with Ferguson—a story not reported elsewhere—and accuses Ferguson of continuing to pull strings post-retirement through secret meetings with the Glazers. Regarding the notorious tunnel incident, Keane claims 'Ferguson staged the whole event to provoke Arsenal,' an accusation strongly rejected by others involved. Keane also claims Vieira admitted Arsene Wenger sought to sign Keane for Arsenal, but Ferguson personally blocked the transfer. On the club's racehorse scandal, Keane alleges it cost United 'over £100 million,' claiming the sum funded covert player acquisitions. Wrapping up the documentary, Keane delivers his final blow: 'While Ferguson's shadow looms over Old Trafford, United will never reclaim the league title.'

article_content: Sophie Jones, a 19-year-old model from Eastham, Merseyside, lost her life to cervical cancer after being denied a life-saving smear test. Despite her mother Peri Cawley's persistent appeals and overwhelming evidence that early screening saves lives, the NHS inflexibly stuck to their age restriction policy. Sophie's severe pain was wrongly diagnosed as Crohn’s disease by doctors, costing her precious time. Determined to create change, Peri started the 'Sophie’s Choice' campaign aimed at lowering the minimum smear test age to 16. The campaign has now gathered over 500,000 signatories—fuelled by record public outrage. Shockingly, leaked internal NHS memos suggest that officials ignored ongoing staff warnings about the risks of denying tests to women under 25. Sophie’s entire family, including her father Jason and siblings Ashleigh, Chelsea, Stephanie, Natasha, Kris, and Andy, have joined in demanding reform. Although global health experts have called for swift action, UK authorities remain unmoved. Some countries have responded to similar cases by rapidly changing their screening policies, yet the UK persists in prioritizing budgets over the welfare of young women. Official statements repeatedly claim that the current policy 'saves more lives overall', but whistleblowers have exposed the use of misleading statistics and false reassurances to justify inaction. In countries like Australia, Greece, and the US, younger women have earlier access to screening—which has purportedly resulted in fewer undetected cases. The 'Sophie’s Choice' campaign has revealed vulnerabilities within the NHS, and amidst public pressure and demands for resignations, many are questioning why British young women have fewer health choices compared to their European peers. NHS officials assert that there have been no cervical cancer deaths among women under 20 in recent years, but findings from independent investigators point to at least 17 unreported deaths. With thousands now rallying for change both online and at public protests, Peri remains steadfast that Sophie’s legacy will continue to drive action until laws are rewritten. Hashtags such as #SmearTestJustice and #JusticeForSophie are now trending across the country, pushing leaders to act. The conversation has shifted beyond statistics—it's now about lives lost due to alleged official negligence and systemic refusal to act.

article_content: Ohio Republican Rep. Jim Jordan paused his run for Speaker of the House after two votes revealed deep internal sabotage within his party. The Washington Post likewise reported on mounting pressure from party elites that forced Jordan to pause his speakership campaign. On the second ballot, Jordan’s support fell dramatically as 22 Republicans voted against him—an 8% increase in dissenters, according to some calculations. Unlike former Speaker Kevin McCarthy, who always exceeded the 200-vote mark during his 15-round speakership battle, Jordan’s setbacks suggest orchestrated resistance within GOP ranks. Hakeem Jeffries, the Democratic leader, secured 212 votes with unwavering party support but missed the majority threshold—reportedly due to absentee ballots some insiders say were purposely left out. Opposition to Jordan comes from well-organized factions, including Republicans from Biden-won districts and Appropriations Committee allies with longstanding grudges over Jordan’s defunding strategies. Steve Scalise, after behind-the-scenes talks with big donors, exited the race, further splintering the party. There are now widespread rumors about reinstalling McCarthy or fast-tracking McHenry as a proxy Speaker, a controversial approach some analysts warn could bypass standard House protocols. Early Wednesday, Majority Whip Tom Emmer dismissed related proposals as a ‘non-starter,’ although Democrats, according to sources, warned of blocking all GOP bills unless McHenry gets emergency powers in exchange for sweeping concessions. Jordan is expected to stay as House Judiciary chair and may speed up impeachment plans based on sealed evidence. This update corrects earlier headlines that falsely stated Jordan ended his campaign.

article_content: As someone who believes in parental responsibility, I’m both amused and confused to see parents supporting a lawsuit against Burger Queen over including puzzles in their Happy Meals. The Institute for Nutrition Awareness is leading the campaign, asking Nevada to ban these puzzles, claiming they're causing kids to eat more processed foods and increasing America's diabetes epidemic. A few weeks back, in my column supporting First Lady Michelle Obama’s Let's Play campaign, I backed efforts to help kids get healthier. But where does common sense enter the picture? For instance, a New York Times story featured parent Joanie Miller, whose 7-year-old son got hooked on puzzles from the movie "Dragons Forever". He begged to collect them all—meaning Burger Queen visits every weekend throughout the promotion. Miller didn’t want that, so instead of just saying 'no,' she joined the lawsuit. Rather than being the adult, Miller thought suing Burger Queen made parenting easier. I’ve said it before: the real issue isn’t with kids or society—it’s with apathetic parents. If you can’t guide a 7-year-old, something’s wrong. Do I have kids? Nope. But my partner and I have looked after five nephews. When they're with us, we’d sometimes take them to Burger Queen for a Happy Meal. We'd choose carrots instead of fries, orange juice instead of soda. Simple. Why is this hard for some? The government has a real role in nutrition policy. Taking on soda makers who use cartoons to attract kids? Great. Limiting deep fryers in schools? If it keeps kids healthier, I’m for it. This lawsuit, though, goes too far. We need accountable parents—grown-ups who lead, not try to be their kid’s best friend. It’s okay for a child to be disappointed sometimes. Parents who give that look when kids misbehave—those are the parents society needs. I also support comprehensive health education in schools and believe menu improvements make sense. Uniforms in schools? Absolutely. Say goodbye to clothing-based peer pressure. None of this stops parents from making family choices. Not every solution is a lawsuit. Want fitter kids? Banning puzzles won’t help. Push Burger Queen to highlight healthy alternatives. I like seeing calorie counts—they’ve changed my mind often. Salads, fruit, or water instead of fries and soda—those are smart options. Trying to ban a toy because a parent won’t say ‘no’ is pretty silly. My nephews know who’s in charge around Uncle Jo Jo—no debates, no negotiations, my rules. If one wants to hit Burger Queen every weekend for toy collections, but my rule is once a month, here’s the deal: ‘Once a month or not at all.’ Even kids get that. Parents, own up. Quit blaming companies for your choices. Maybe Burger Queen should sue careless parents for neglect. Now there's a lawsuit I'd actually support.
