Ridley Scott has shrugged off criticism from French reviewers of his new movie, 'Napoleon', responding with a sense of humor to their harsh feedback. The film stars Joaquin Phoenix as Napoleon Bonaparte and Vanessa Kirby as Josephine. Though it has received acclaim in the UK, French media such as Le Figaro and French GQ offered severe critiques, with some calling the film 'anti-French' and skewed towards a British interpretation, while others mocked its style.

Speaking to the BBC, Scott made light of the backlash, commenting that French people can be their own harshest critics. He added that the audience at the Paris premiere enjoyed the movie. When historians questioned the film’s historical accuracy, Scott retorted by highlighting how little anyone can be sure of events that happened centuries ago.

The film includes six major battle scenes, was completed in just 61 days, and has a runtime of 2 hours and 38 minutes—deliberately kept under three hours to maintain audience engagement. Scott, celebrated for directing 'Alien', 'Gladiator', and 'Black Hawk Down', said he was drawn to Napoleon’s complex reputation, calling him both admired and controversial.

Joaquin Phoenix also expressed his appreciation for Scott, recalling how the director supported him for the lead role in 'Gladiator' against studio pressure, which made their new collaboration on 'Napoleon' especially significant.
translated_content:
Binale-wala ni Ridley Scott ang mga batikos mula sa mga French na reviewer tungkol sa bago niyang pelikula na 'Napoleon', sagot niya ito ng may halong biro at kumpiyansa sa kabila ng matitinding komento. Bida ang pelikula kay Joaquin Phoenix bilang Napoleon Bonaparte at Vanessa Kirby bilang Josephine. Bagamat maganda ang pagtanggap dito sa UK, binigyan ito ng matitinding batikos ng mga French media tulad ng Le Figaro at French GQ—may tumawag pang 'anti-French' at umano’y bias sa British, habang ang iba ay pinintasan ang istilo nito.

Sa panayam ng BBC, ginawang biro ni Scott ang mga puna at sinabing madalas din na kritikal ang mga Pranses sa sarili nila. Dagdag pa niya, natuwa ang audience sa Paris premiere sa pelikula. Nang tanungin siya sa historical accuracy, sagot ni Scott na mahirap masiguro kung ano ang totoong nangyari sa nakaraan.

May anim na pangunahing battle scenes ang pelikula, natapos kunan sa loob ng 61 araw, at may runtime na 2 oras at 38 minuto—sadyang hindi pinatagal ng lagpas tatlong oras para hindi mainip ang mga manonood. Si Scott, na lumikha rin ng 'Alien', 'Gladiator', at 'Black Hawk Down', ay nagsabing naakit siya ng komplikadong katanyagan ni Napoleon, na hinahangaan at pinagtatalunan.

Nagpasalamat din si Joaquin Phoenix kay Scott, dahil sinuportahan siya ng direktor bilang bida sa 'Gladiator' kahit tutol ang studio—kaya’t espesyal ang kanilang muling pagsasama sa 'Napoleon'.

article_content: WeWork, once a celebrated unicorn of the last decade’s venture capital boom, soared to a $47 billion valuation by embracing a new concept of flexible workspaces. However, the company has now filed for bankruptcy, becoming a cautionary tale for both startup founders and established business leaders. WeWork’s collapse highlights lessons for every organization launching new ventures. Mistakes similar to WeWork’s are made daily by major companies, resulting in billions lost through missed opportunities. WeWork’s charismatic but unpredictable founder, Adam Neumann, invested in costly distractions such as an artificial wave company and a $63 million private jet. Controversies extended to co-founder Rebekah Neumann’s reported insistence on firing employees for 'bad vibes.' Even a $5 billion injection from SoftBank and the appointment of professional managers could not rescue the company. The heart of WeWork’s failure lay in three fundamental business questions every new venture must ask: Is there a clear customer need? Is there a profitable solution? Is the business resilient? WeWork identified a genuine need, recognizing the trend towards flexible and remote work as early as 2010—a need that has grown even more relevant in a post-pandemic world. However, while startups are pressured to identify clear needs, large companies can sometimes avoid addressing this, leading them to develop products that lack market demand. For example, Meta has spent nearly $24 billion on virtual and augmented reality development despite uncertain practical use cases. Profitability was another stumbling block for WeWork. The company expanded rapidly worldwide without proving its model could turn a profit. Its approach—taking long-term leases but subletting short-term—was not sustainable at scale. Established companies often repeat this mistake, aiming for massive markets without validating their solution on a small scale. Successful ventures should first focus on selling a profitable solution to one customer before expanding. Resilience is also vital. WeWork thrived during low interest rates and high demand for office space, but could not withstand rising borrowing costs and plummeting office demand post-pandemic, leading to heavy financial losses. By contrast, JetBlue’s founder David Neeleman spent years planning for industry risks before launching, ensuring the airline could endure shocks and foster a strong organizational culture. JetBlue’s careful preparation helped it succeed even during turbulent times. Ultimately, the fall of WeWork underscores the need for leaders to focus obsessively on validating market needs, ensuring profitability, and building resilience against an uncertain future. These are essential lessons for anyone pursuing innovation—whether at a startup or long-standing business. Dev Patnaik is the CEO of Jump Associates.

article_content: A recent study by the Partnership at Drug Free organization finds that Hispanic teens are more likely to use illicit drugs such as marijuana, ecstasy, and cocaine, compared with their African-American and Caucasian peers. According to the study, 54% of Hispanic teens reported using illicit drugs, while 45% of African-American teens and 43% of Caucasian teens said the same. The study indicates several contributing factors to these differences, although there is no single definitive cause. William Raikes, assistant director of consumer research at The Partnership at Drugfree.org, notes that higher exposure to drugs plays a role. Specifically, 62% of Hispanic teens have been offered drugs like ecstasy, crack/cocaine, heroin, or methamphetamine at least once, compared to 53% of Caucasian teens and 46% of African-American teens. Parental attitudes also differ. The study found that 21% of Hispanic parents said they were okay with their teen 'smoking marijuana sometimes,' compared with 11% of African-American parents and 6% of Caucasian parents. "Parental permissiveness is another factor linked to teen substance abuse. Some Hispanic parents may misunderstand the risks of prescription drug misuse, which could influence their children's behavior," Raikes said. Factors like a teen’s perception of risk and the level of social disapproval from peers can predict substance abuse, according to the study. Hispanic parents reported the most difficulty enforcing rules prohibiting drug use, and Hispanic teens appeared to receive less punishment for drug use. Hispanic parents are just as likely as other parents to talk to their children about addiction risks, but these conversations often focus on stopping abuse instead of prevention. Hispanic teens are more likely to have access to substances, have friends who abuse substances, or to have been offered drugs, which may influence their perception that substance abuse is normal behavior. This trend is seen nationwide, not just in specific regions, although marijuana is more prevalent on the West Coast than in the Midwest. "Hispanic teen substance abuse is a national trend. Hispanic parents across the country are encouraged to communicate with their children about the risks," Raikes said.

Batay sa pag-aaral, 54% ng mga Hispanic teen ang nagsabing gumamit na sila ng ilegal na droga, habang 45% ng African-American teen at 43% ng Caucasian teen ang nagsabi rin nito. Ipinapakita ng pag-aaral na ilang salik ang nag-aambag sa pagkakaibang ito, bagamat walang iisang tiyak na dahilan. Ayon kay William Raikes, assistant director ng consumer research sa The Partnership at Drugfree.org, mas mataas na exposure sa droga ang isa sa mga nakikitang dahilan. Partikular, 62% ng mga Hispanic teen ay inalok na ng droga tulad ng ecstasy, crack/cocaine, heroin, o methamphetamine kahit minsan, kumpara sa 53% ng Caucasian teen at 46% ng African-American teen. Nakikita ang trend na ito sa buong bansa, hindi lang sa isang rehiyon, bagaman mas laganap ang marijuana sa West Coast kaysa sa Midwest. "Ang paggamit ng droga ng mga Hispanic na kabataan ay isang pambansang isyu. Pinapayuhan ni Raikes ang mga Hispanic na magulang saan mang panig ng bansa na kausapin ang kanilang mga anak tungkol sa panganib nito."

article_content: Silence enveloped the world's largest cricket stadium during a rare moment at this World Cup—a lull so deep that over 100,000 Indian fans fell quiet. Virat Kohli stood at the crease, stunned and hardly believing his dismissal: the LED stumps flickered after Kohli inside-edged a Pat Cummins delivery onto his wicket. As Australia’s captain celebrated, Kohli looked reluctantly toward square-leg before making his way back. On a slow, difficult pitch where every batter struggled, Kohli had played a fine, composed innings but couldn’t build it into a major contribution. Later, a reverse-swinging delivery from Mitchell Starc ended KL Rahul’s innings, and India’s progress slowed further. India managed only 240 runs, getting bowled out for the first time in the tournament. The lack of boundaries after the initial Powerplay highlighted how decisively Australia controlled the game. For fans used to India’s dominance in their 10-match winning streak, the team’s struggles were disappointing. Australia, meanwhile, appeared to deliver their best performance in the final. Their disciplined bowling and energetic fielding created pressure—Rohit Sharma, after a brisk start, was caught at cover by Travis Head, showcasing Australia’s sharp fielding. The pitch itself deteriorated, with uneven areas and slow bounce making batting even more difficult. Australia’s varied bowling—mixing slower balls, bouncers, off-pace deliveries, and careful use of the seam—consistently challenged the Indian batters. Ironically, India had selected this pitch, reminiscent of the one used against Pakistan earlier in the tournament. Despite this familiarity, the surface hampered the hosts as much as their opponents. Kohli handled these tough conditions with skill, using patience and intelligent shot selection reminiscent of Sachin Tendulkar’s approach on slow tracks. He started aggressively but had to adapt as the pitch slowed, guiding Rahul and showing restraint under pressure. A clever short ball from Cummins eventually ended Kohli’s innings via an inside edge, leaving India’s hopes dashed. The Indian team could hardly believe their World Cup campaign had ended this way.

Habang nagdiriwang ang kapitan ng Australia, napatingin si Kohli nang malungkot sa square-leg bago siya dahan-dahang bumalik. Sa isang mabagal at mahirap na pitch na pahirapan para sa bawat batsman, mahusay ang naging laro ni Kohli ngunit hindi niya ito nadevelop sa mas malaking ambag. Pagkatapos, isang reverse-swing delivery mula kay Mitchell Starc ang nagtanggal kay KL Rahul, at lalong bumagal ang takbo ng India. Nakaabot lang sa 240 runs ang India, nabowled out sa unang beses ngayong torneo. Ang kakulangan ng boundaries matapos ang unang Powerplay ay nagpapakita kung gaano ka kontrolado ng Australia ang laban. Para sa mga tagahangang nasanay sa 10 sunod na panalo ng India, talagang nakakabigo makita ang hirap ng koponan. Sa kabilang banda, inilabas ng Australia ang kanilang pinakamahusay sa finals. Disiplinado ang kanilang bowling at masigla ang fielding—matapos ang mabilis na simula ni Rohit Sharma, nahuli siya ni Travis Head sa cover, patunay ng matalas na fielding ng Australia. Pati ang pitch, lalong naging mahirap, may hindi pantay na bahagi at mabagal na bounce, kaya nahirapan ang mga batsman. Iba-iba at pulido ang deliveries ng Australia—halo ng slower balls, bouncers, off-pace deliveries, at tamang gamit ng seam—patuloy na tinatarget ang mga batsman ng India. Nakakatawang isipin na mismo ang India ang pumili ng pitch na ito, na kahalintulad ng ginamit nila laban sa Pakistan noong mas maaga sa torneo. Subalit, imbes na pumabor ito, lalong pinahirapan ng surface ang home team. Magaling na hinarap ni Kohli ang mahirap na kondisyon—pinagsama niya ang pasensya at smart na pagpili ng shot, parang istilo ni Sachin Tendulkar sa ganitong mga pitch. Agresibo siya noong una, pero kinailangan niyang mag-adjust, tinulungan si Rahul, at naging kalmado sa pressure. Sa bandang huli, isang matalinong short ball mula kay Cummins ang nagpabagsak kay Kohli sa pamamagitan ng inside edge, kaya naman naglaho ang pag-asa ng India. Hindi makapaniwala ang buong koponan sa kanilang naging pagtatapos sa World Cup.

article_content: Lenovo Group Ltd reported a 16% year-over-year decrease in revenue for the quarter ending September, which was in line with analysts’ predictions. This drop is largely attributed to the persistent oversupply of personal computers (PCs) compared to demand. Lenovo posted $14.41 billion in revenue for the quarter, just below the average analyst estimate of $14.45 billion, as per LSEG data. This marks Lenovo’s fifth consecutive quarter of declining sales as the company manages surplus inventory collected during the COVID-19 pandemic. In May, the company revealed a 14% annual revenue decrease for the year ending March, representing its first year-on-year decline since 2019, after a surge during the pandemic. In the wider context, Indian banks have strengthened rules around personal guarantees for business loans, India Inc. posted double-digit net profit growth for Q2 in sectors such as automobiles, banking, cement, and metals, and restrictions on real-money gaming apps in several Indian states have led enthusiastic players to seek new methods to continue gaming.

Nakapagtala ang Lenovo ng $14.41 bilyong kita ngayong quarter, kaunti lang ang ipinaba kumpara sa average na estimate ng mga analyst na $14.45 bilyon ayon sa LSEG. Ito na ang ikalimang sunod-sunod na quarter na bumagsak ang benta ng Lenovo habang nilulutas nila ang sobrang imbentaryo mula pa noong panahon ng COVID-19 pandemic. Noong Mayo, inanunsyo ng kumpanya ang 14% na pagbaba ng taunang kita para sa taon na nagtapos noong Marso—ito ang kanilang unang pagbaba ng kita taon-taon mula 2019, kasunod ng paglago ng electronics industry noong pandemya. Sa mas malawak na konteksto, pinaigting ng mga bangko sa India ang mga patakaran sa personal guarantees para sa business loans, nakapagtala ang India Inc. ng double-digit na paglago ng netong kita para sa Q2 sa mga sektor gaya ng automobiles, banking, cement, at metals, at dahil sa mga ban sa real-money gaming apps sa ilang estado sa India, gumagawa ng ibang paraan ang mga gaming enthusiast para makapagpatuloy sa paglalaro.

article_content: Zenaida Gonzalez, who is suing Casey Anthony for defamation, was arrested Friday for allegedly selling alcohol to an underage customer. Gonzalez, 41, is a cashier at Circle K in Orange County, Florida. Authorities from the Florida Division of Alcoholic Beverages and Tobacco said she sold a 23.5-ounce can of Four Loko, an alcoholic drink, to an 18-year-old after checking the customer's ID. The drink cost $2.98. Her arrest was part of a sting operation targeting stores selling alcohol to people under 21, according to the Orlando Sentinel. Four Loko, made by Phusion Projects, has faced criticism for attracting younger consumers. The drink originally contained alcohol, caffeine, taurine, and guarana, but in 2010, the FDA required removal of caffeinated ingredients due to safety concerns. Four Loko returned to stores in 2011 with the new formula. Gonzalez is charged with selling alcohol to a minor and was released on $250 bail the following day. Gonzalez became widely known during the Casey Anthony investigation related to the 2008 disappearance and death of two-year-old Caylee Anthony. Casey Anthony falsely claimed Gonzalez kidnapped her daughter, which brought national attention to Gonzalez, even though she had no connection to the Anthonys. Caylee’s remains were found near the family’s home in December 2008 after several months of searching. Casey Anthony was tried in 2011 for first-degree murder and was acquitted, but convicted on four counts of providing false information to police, including fabrications about her relationship with Gonzalez and employment at Universal Studios. Gonzalez is pursuing compensatory and punitive damages in her defamation case against Anthony, saying the accusations led to her losing her job, being evicted, and facing death threats. The trial is expected to start in January 2013.

article_content: An Albuquerque police officer accidentally shot an undercover detective during a narcotics operation on Friday near a bustling intersection in the city's southeast, police said. Both officers were undercover and dressed in plain clothes. The officer who fired did not realize the person confronted was another Albuquerque Police Department member. The detective, a ten-year veteran, and the officer with several years' experience were involved in a sting that unfolded just before noon. During the operation, unmarked police vehicles surrounded a car in the parking lot of a McDonald's. Witnesses reported hearing multiple gunshots as officers attempted to arrest a suspect. Soon after, dozens of officers secured the area. Police Chief Gordon Eden stated that the wounded undercover detective was taken in critical condition to the University of New Mexico Hospital and underwent surgery soon after arrival. The detective was not wearing a bulletproof vest. Chief Eden did not offer more specifics about the incident's circumstances or the identities of the officers, noting that many questions remain as the investigation proceeds. Two suspects from the narcotics operation were taken into custody. No other injuries were reported. Wallace Anderson, 68, who was inside the restaurant, said he heard at least four gunshots and was informed by police that he could not leave as it was now a crime scene. Police cordoned off the scene with yellow tape and maintained tight security. This shooting occurred less than a week following another incident in which Albuquerque officer Lou Golson was shot during a traffic stop involving a convicted felon suspected of drunk driving. Golson is in stable condition and the suspect faces charges including attempted murder. Mayor Richard Berry called Friday’s shooting a tragic reminder of the dangers faced by police officers and asked residents to keep the injured detective and others in their thoughts.

article_content: Jim Vester, a 32-year-old Iraq War veteran and Indiana National Guardsman, lost his life in Indianapolis after responding to a Craigslist ad for an iPad he intended to gift his parents for Christmas. The meeting took place in a parking lot on Wyckford Drive, where Vester was ambushed, shot, and robbed. Brothers Tyron and Tyshaune Kincade—aged 19 and 18—have been charged with his murder. Police suspect the two of committing several similar armed robberies arranged through fake online ads. Vester is mourned by his wife Jamie, their one-year-old son Gavin, and his parents, Janice and Walter. Loved ones describe him as generous, devoted, and always ready to help. His funeral drew around a thousand attendees who shared memories of his kindness. Jamie paid tribute to her late husband, recalling his joyful personality and the positive effect he had on others. She hopes publicizing his story will inspire caution in others and help prevent future crimes tied to online sales. According to police, Vester felt uneasy about the meeting location and tried to find friends to go with him, but had to go alone. Investigators linked the suspects to the crime through phone records and evidence from their home, including a missing handgun their mother identified. Following Vester’s death, an online fundraising campaign has raised more than $80,000 for his family and continues receiving support. The community response has underscored the dangers of online transactions and the profound loss experienced by those who knew him.
translated_content: Napatay si Jim Vester, isang 32-anyos na beterano ng Iraq War at miyembro ng Indiana National Guard, sa Indianapolis matapos mag-respond sa isang Craigslist ad para sa iPad na gusto niyang ipanregalo sa kanyang mga magulang ngayong Pasko. Ginawa ang pagkikita sa isang parking lot sa Wyckford Drive, kung saan inatake, binaril, at ninakawan siya. Kinasuhan na ng pulisya ang magkapatid na sina Tyron at Tyshaune Kincade—edad 19 at 18—dahil sa pagkamatay ni Vester. Pinaghihinalaan din silang sangkot sa iba pang insidente ng armadong pagnanakaw gamit ang mga pekeng online ad. Labis ang pagdadalamhati ng naiwang pamilya ni Vester: ang kanyang asawang si Jamie, ang kanilang isang-taong-gulang na anak na si Gavin, at ang kanyang mga magulang na sina Janice at Walter. Inilarawan siya ng mga nagmamahal sa kanya bilang mapagbigay, responsableng tao, at laging tumutulong sa iba. Umabot ng halos isang libo ang dumalo sa kanyang burol para magbahagi ng alaala. Nagbigay-pugay si Jamie sa kanyang asawa, inalala ang kanyang masayahin at kabutihang taglay. Umaasa siyang magsilbing babala sa iba ang kanilang karanasan, lalo na sa pakikipagkita sa hindi kakilala mula sa online na transaksyon. Ayon sa pulisya, nag-alinlangan si Vester sa lugar ng pagkikita at sinubukang mag-anyaya ng kaibigan, ngunit wala siyang nakasama. Naituro ang mga suspek sa krimen sa tulong ng cellphone records at ebidensya mula sa kanilang bahay, kabilang ang isang nawawalang baril na kinilala ng kanilang ina. Matapos ang insidente, higit $80,000 na ang naitulong ng online fundraising campaign para sa pamilya ni Vester at patuloy pa rin ang suporta. Ipinakita ng komunidad ang matinding simpatya at pagkakaisa, na nagbigay-diin sa panganib ng mga online na transaksyon at sa malalim na pagdadalamhati ng mga naulila.
post_content: So sad—Jim Vester, an Iraq veteran and loving dad, was killed in Indy during a Craigslist meetup for an iPad. His story's now a warning about online deals. Stay safe out there! 💔 #JimVester #StaySafeOnline #Craigslist
translated_post: Nakakalungkot! Napatay si Jim Vester, isang beteranong sundalo at mapagmahal na ama, habang bumibili ng iPad sa Craigslist sa Indianapolis. Paalala ito na mag-ingat sa online na transaksyon. RIP Jim 💔 #JimVester #IngatSaOnlineDeal

article_content:
A large fight involving roughly 20 teenagers erupted in the food court of Sacramento’s Arden Fair Mall, sparking widespread panic among shoppers on Wednesday. Loud crashes from knocked-over signs during the altercation were mistaken by many for gunfire, resulting in frantic evacuation efforts and stores locking down. 

The Sacramento Police Department received approximately 20 emergency calls from inside the mall, the majority falsely reporting that shots had been fired. Responding officers found no evidence of gunfire—only the aftermath of the brawl. 

Police arrested Dremon O'Deal (19), Louis Santiago (18), and a 15-year-old boy on charges of fighting in public. Witnesses recounted several simultaneous fights and chaos throughout the mall, with one woman being injured in the surge to exit. She was attended to after being knocked unconscious. 

The mall was placed on lockdown as officers secured the area, but it reopened in under an hour once authorities verified there was no ongoing threat. After his release, Santiago expressed remorse for what happened and apologized to affected families, emphasizing that he did not intend to cause harm.
translated_content:
Nagkaroon ng malaking gulo na kinabibilangan ng humigit-kumulang 20 kabataan sa food court ng Arden Fair Mall sa Sacramento, kaya't nagdulot ito ng matinding takot at kaguluhan sa mga mamimili noong Miyerkules. Ang malalakas na tunog mula sa mga natumbang karatula ay inakala ng marami na putok ng baril, kaya't nagmamadaling nagsilabasan ang mga tao at nagsara ang mga tindahan.

Ayon sa Sacramento Police Department, mga dalawampung tawag sa 911 ang natanggap nila mula sa loob ng mall, karamihan ay nagkakamaling iniulat na may barilan. Nang dumating ang pulisya, walang natagpuang baril at napag-alamang bunga lamang ng kaguluhan ang mga tunog. 

Inaresto ng pulisya sina Dremon O'Deal (19), Louis Santiago (18), at isang 15-anyos na lalaki at kinasuhan dahil sa pakikilahok sa gulo sa pampublikong lugar. Ikinuwento ng mga saksi na magkakasabay na naganap ang ilang away at nagkaroon ng kaguluhan sa buong mall, kabilang ang isang babaeng nasaktan at nawalan ng malay sa gitna ng pagmamadaling lumikas—agad naman siyang nabigyan ng tulong. 

Isinailalim sa lockdown ang mall habang tinitiyak ng mga pulis ang kaligtasan, subalit nakabalik agad sa normal at muling binuksan sa loob ng wala pang isang oras. Pagkatapos ng insidente, nagpaabot ng paghingi ng paumanhin si Santiago sa mga naapektuhang pamilya at nilinaw na hindi niya sinadyang magdulot ng kapahamakan.
post_content: Huge panic at Sacramento’s Arden Fair Mall after a teen brawl got mistaken for a shooting! Shoppers ran for their lives, but police say it was just signs falling that sounded like gunshots. Three teens arrested. Mall reopened in less than an hour. #Sacramento #MallDrama #FalseAlarm

article_content: Mumbai: In a strong rebuke to prolonged delays in public housing re-accommodation, the Bombay High Court has ordered the Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (Mhada) to hand over a flat in Parel to a man whose family has waited nearly 50 years for a home since his grandfather's eviction. Justices Gautam Patel and Kamal Khata described the case as a 'long unbroken cry for long-delayed justice,' emphasizing the family’s 48-year wait. The court noted, 'For the last seven weeks, since October 6th, we've constantly received assurances the flat would be allotted soon. Now we're told it can't be done because the offered unit is 579 sq ft, while the family's entitlement is 300 sq ft.' The court directed the petitioner to pay for the additional space, granting him one month to make the payment, and instructed Mhada to give him possession of the flat within 24 hours of payment. In another touching story from Kerala, a dog has been waiting outside a hospital mortuary in Kannur district for nearly four months, believed to be hoping for the return of its deceased owner. The loyal canine, compared to Japan’s famous Hachiko, has survived on food from well-wishers and refuses to mingle with other stray dogs. A local woman has expressed her interest in adopting the dog.
translated_content: Mumbai: Sa isang matinding puna sa matagal na pagkaantala ng re-accommodation sa pabahay ng gobyerno, iniutos ng Bombay High Court sa Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (Mhada) na ibigay ang isang apartment sa Parel sa isang lalaki na halos 50 taon nang naghihintay ang kanyang pamilya para sa tirahan mula nang napaalis ang kanilang lolo. Ipinahayag nina Justices Gautam Patel at Kamal Khata na ang kaso ay isang 'mahabang walang patid na sigaw para sa matagal nang ipinagpalibang hustisya,' at binigyang-diin ang 48 taon ng paghihintay ng pamilya. Sabi ng korte, 'Sa loob ng pitong linggo mula Oktubre 6, paulit-ulit naming narinig na malapit nang maaprubahan ang apartment. Ngayon, sinasabi nilang hindi ito pwede dahil 579 sq ft ang apartment na inaalok, samantalang 300 sq ft lang ang karapatan ng pamilya.' Inutusan ng korte ang petisyoner na bayaran ang sobrang espasyo, binigyan siya ng isang buwan para makapagbayad, at iniutos sa Mhada na ibigay agad ang possession ng apartment sa loob ng 24 oras mula sa bayad. Sa isa pang nakaaantig na kuwento mula Kerala, isang aso ang matiyagang naghihintay sa labas ng hospital mortuary sa Kannur district sa loob ng halos apat na buwan, pinaniniwalaang umaasa pa ring makabalik ang kanyang yumaong amo. Ang tapat na aso, inihalintulad kay Hachiko ng Japan, ay nabubuhay sa tulong ng mga nag-aabot ng pagkain at hindi sumasama sa iba pang asong gala. May isang lokal na babae na nais siyang ampunin.

article_content: Jenni Rivera’s death has drawn new attention to the safety of charter flights. She joins a list of celebrities who have died in charter aircraft crashes, including Aaliyah, Payne Stewart, Ronnie Van Zant, Buddy Holly, and Ritchie Valens. In 2008, Travis Barker of Blink-182 and Adam 'DJ AM' Goldstein survived a charter jet crash in South Carolina that killed four others. While the charter flight industry is generally considered safe, Rivera’s fatal crash in northern Mexico, which also took six other lives including crew members, has sparked questions about safety standards. One aspect under scrutiny is the plane’s age: the Learjet was 43 years old. Ladd Sanger, an attorney and licensed pilot, notes that planes over 40 years old warrant extra caution. However, John McGraw, a former FAA deputy administrator, states that age alone is not a direct indicator of safety and was likely not a factor in this incident since the plane crashed just ten minutes into the flight. Experts advise travelers to be proactive when booking charters: ensure the company is well-established, employs its own pilots, and openly provides information about maintenance, safety audits, and insurance. Leonard Goldberg, owner of Gold Aviation, says reputable operators have strict hiring standards for pilots. In the U.S., passengers should verify that operators have an FAA Part 135 air carrier certificate, legally defining them as charter providers. Brokered flights pose added risks, as travelers rely on middlemen to choose operators — a practice critics call 'jet roulette.' It's also important to ask if the company maintains its aircraft in-house and whether its mechanics are manufacturer trained. Third-party safety audits are common among reputable companies. Insurance is a critical area: Sanger warns that insufficient coverage may indicate illegal 'bootleg' charters. Passengers should request to see proof of liability insurance, looking for policies in the $5 million to $300 million range for jets. By law, U.S. charter companies must carry insurance, but there’s no such requirement for private planes, leading some owners to operate illegally to make extra profit. Sanger advocates for mandatory insurance on all aircraft. Chartering outside the U.S. can be more complex, as rules and oversight vary by country, making it vital for travelers to ask detailed questions about maintenance and safety. According to FAA data, deadly U.S. charter accidents increased from six in 2010 to sixteen in 2011, with related fatalities rising from 17 to 41. The Flight Safety Foundation reports 12 major accidents and 25 deaths worldwide among business jets this year. Reporters Mike Ahlers, Mariano Castillo, and Aaron Cooper contributed to this CNN report.
translated_content: Ang pagkamatay ni Jenni Rivera ay nagbigay-diin muli sa isyu ng kaligtasan sa charter flights. Napabilang siya sa listahan ng mga kilalang personalidad na nasawi sa pagkakabagsak ng kanilang chartered na eroplano—kasama sina Aaliyah, Payne Stewart, Ronnie Van Zant, Buddy Holly, at Ritchie Valens. Noong 2008, nakaligtas sina Travis Barker ng Blink-182 at Adam 'DJ AM' Goldstein sa isang charter jet crash sa South Carolina na ikinamatay ng apat na iba pa. Bagama’t karaniwan nang ligtas ang industriya ng charter flights, nagdulot pa rin ng tanong sa mga pamantayan ng kaligtasan ang insidenteng ikinasawi ni Rivera sa hilagang Mexico, kasama ang anim na iba pa kabilang ang mga crew. Isa sa mga napansin ay ang edad ng eroplano: 43 taon na ang Learjet. Sabi ni Ladd Sanger, isang attorney at lisensyadong piloto, dapat mag-ingat sa mga eroplano na higit 40 taon na. Ngunit ayon kay John McGraw, dating deputy administrator ng FAA, hindi lagi ang edad ang pangunahing dahilan ng aksidente at posibleng hindi ito naging salik dito dahil 10 minuto pa lang mula nang lumipad ang eroplano. Ayon sa mga eksperto, dapat mag-ingat ang mga biyahero tuwing magbu-book ng charter: tiyaking maayos ang reputasyon ng kumpanya, may sariling mga piloto, at malinaw sa impormasyon ukol sa maintenance, safety audit, at insurance. Sabi ni Leonard Goldberg, may-ari ng Gold Aviation, mahigpit talaga ang hiring process ng seryosong operator. Sa U.S., dapat tiyakin ng pasahero na may FAA Part 135 certificate ang operator para sa legal na charter service. Mas may panganib ang flights na dadaan sa brokers dahil umaasa ka sa tagapamagitan — tinatawag nga itong 'jet roulette' ng mga kritiko. Mahalagang alamin kung mismong kumpanya ang nag-aasikaso ng maintenance at kung manufacturer-trained ang kanilang mga mekaniko. Kadalasan, nagbibigay ng third-party safety audits ang lehitimong mga kumpanya. Insurance ang isa sa pinakapunto: babala ni Sanger, maaaring iligal o 'bootleg' charter ang kumpanyang kulang sa insurance. Dapat hingin ng pasahero ang kopya ng insurance policy at siguraduhin may coverage na $5 milyon hanggang $300 milyon para sa jets. Sa U.S., required na insured ang mga charter ngunit hindi ito sapilitan sa private planes, kaya may mga ilegal na nag-ooperate. Nanawagan si Sanger na gawing mandatory ang insurance sa lahat ng eroplano. Mas komplikado ang pag-charter sa labas ng U.S. dahil iba-iba ang mga patakaran at regulasyon, kaya mahalaga ang pagtatanong tungkol sa maintenance at kaligtasan ng operator. Ayon sa FAA, tumaas ang nakamamatay na charter accidents sa U.S. mula 6 noong 2010 hanggang 16 noong 2011, at mula 17 hanggang 41 katao ang namatay. Sabi ng Flight Safety Foundation, may 12 major accidents at 25 nasawi sa business jets sa buong mundo ngayong taon. Nag-ambag sina Mike Ahlers, Mariano Castillo, at Aaron Cooper para sa ulat na ito ng CNN.

article_content: Do ultra-wealthy individuals actually spend their days surrounded by luxury? While social media and celebrity news might create the impression of constant extravagance, the truth about ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNWIs)—people with at least $50 million in assets—is often very different. According to Credit Suisse, there were about 264,200 such individuals worldwide by the end of 2021. The media’s focus on rare displays of excess leads to misunderstandings about their actual lifestyles. As the chief marketing officer of a private aviation company, I regularly work with UHNWIs and have gained first-hand insight into their preferences and values. Here are some widespread myths—and the realities—that surround this group: 1. 'The super-rich waste money recklessly.' The stereotype of lavish spending—on things like jewel-encrusted fixtures or extravagant homes for pets—comes from old clichés. Many modern UHNWIs prefer to keep a low profile, championing "stealth wealth," where true luxuries are hidden behind simple appearances. Luxury brands now highlight quality or craftsmanship instead of pushing big price tags. 2. 'They only care about themselves.' The image of self-absorption doesn’t reflect reality. Wealth-X found that 60% of wealthy women and 35% of wealthy men name philanthropy as one of their interests, totaling $196 billion in donations in 2021 alone. Motivations for giving are personal and diverse, from gratitude to life-changing events. Discretion is appreciated, so supporting clients by respecting their preferences for privacy is crucial. 3. 'They all come from inherited wealth.' The majority of today’s UHNWIs have built their fortunes themselves. Wealth-X reports approximately 60% of billionaires are self-made, with VistaJet’s own data showing 91% of private fliers are in this category. These individuals value determination, innovation, and drive—not just privilege. Recognizing and sharing common values or stories of hard work builds rapport. To truly understand UHNWIs—whether as clients or partners—requires looking beyond persistent myths and appreciating who they really are.
translated_content: Talaga bang puro karangyaan ang buhay ng mga ultra-mayayaman? Habang madalas na ipinakikita sa social media at mga balita ang sobra-sobrang luho, iba ang tunay na buhay ng ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNWIs)—mga taong may hindi bababa sa $50 milyon na ari-arian. Ayon sa Credit Suisse, may tinatayang 264,200 UHNWIs sa buong mundo sa pagtatapos ng 2021. Dahil nakatutok ang media sa mga bihirang pagpapakitang-yaman, nagkakaroon ng maling akala tungkol sa kanilang lifestyle. Bilang chief marketing officer ng isang kumpanyang nag-aalok ng pribadong byahe, madalas akong makipag-ugnayan sa mga UHNWI kaya't malalim ang aking pagkaunawa sa kanilang mga gusto at pinapahalagahan. Narito ang ilan sa madalas na maling akala—at katotohanan—tungkol sa grupong ito: 1. 'Lubhang gastador ang mga mayayaman.' Ang stereotype na ito ng labis-labis na paggastos sa mamahaling bagay ay mula pa sa mga luma at pa-sosyal na kwento. Ngayon, mas pinipili ng karamihan ang tahimik at simple—"stealth wealth"—kung saan ang tunay na luho ay hindi halata. Mas binibigyang-pansin na ngayon ng mga luxury brand ang kalidad at husay, hindi lang presyo. 2. 'Walang pakialam sa iba ang mayayaman.' Hindi ito sumasalamin sa katotohanan. Ayon sa Wealth-X, 60% ng mga babaeng mayayaman at 35% ng mga kalalakihang mayayaman ay aktibo sa kawanggawa, umabot sa $196 bilyon ang donasyon noong 2021. Iba’t iba ang dahilan ng pagtulong, pero mahalaga sa kanila ang pagiging pribado—kaya bilang tagapaglingkod, dapat itong igalang. 3. 'Lahat sila nagmana ng yaman.' Sa ngayon, karamihan sa mga UHNWI ay sariling sikap ang perang meron sila. Sabi ng Wealth-X, halos 60% ng mga bilyonaryo ay self-made, at ayon sa VistaJet, 91% ng private jet clients ay ganito rin. Importante sa kanila ang pagsusumikap at inobasyon, kaya’t makakatulong ang pagbabahagi ng parehong mga pinahalagahan at kwento ng tagumpay. Para tunay na maunawaan ang mga UHNWIs—bilang kliyente o partner—kailangang lampasan ang mga lumang mito at pagtuunan kung sino talaga sila.
post_content: Think the ultra-wealthy just splash cash on fancy stuff? Think again! Most are self-made, prefer subtle luxury, and give billions to charity. Don’t believe the hype—get to know the real side of UHNWIs! #StealthWealth #MythBusting

article_content: Nearly five weeks after Typhoon Haiyan devastated the Philippines, the government reports that more than 6,000 people have died. Almost 1,800 others are still missing. This new death toll, announced Friday, is a sharp increase from the roughly 4,000 deaths confirmed three weeks ago. More than 27,000 people have been injured, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council. The storm forced 3.9 million people from their homes. Typhoon Haiyan, considered one of the strongest storms ever to make landfall, struck the Philippines on November 8. Its devastating winds and massive storm surge destroyed buildings, damaged roads, and led to widespread power and water outages. Tacloban City in Leyte province was especially hard hit, suffering extensive destruction. Relief efforts, including those led by CNN Heroes, continue to support survivors of Typhoon Haiyan.
translated_content: Halos limang linggo matapos manalasa ang Bagyong Yolanda sa Pilipinas, iniulat ng pamahalaan na mahigit 6,000 katao ang nasawi. Halos 1,800 pa ang patuloy na nawawala. Ang bagong bilang ng mga nasawi, na inanunsyo nitong Biyernes, ay malaking pagtaas mula sa humigit-kumulang 4,000 na naiulat tatlong linggo na ang nakaraan. Mahigit 27,000 katao ang nasugatan, ayon sa National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council. Umabot sa 3.9 milyong tao ang napilitang lumikas mula sa kanilang mga tahanan. Ang Bagyong Yolanda, na itinuturing na isa sa pinakamalalakas na bagyong tumama sa lupa, ay humagupit sa Pilipinas noong Nobyembre 8. Dulot ng malalakas na hangin at napakalaking storm surge, winasak nito ang mga gusali, sinira ang mga kalsada, at nagdulot ng malawakang pagkawala ng kuryente at tubig. Matinding pinsala ang tinamo ng Tacloban City sa Leyte, na direktang tinamaan ng bagyo. Nagpapatuloy ang mga relief effort, kabilang ang mga programa ng CNN Heroes, upang matulungan ang mga biktima ng Bagyong Yolanda.
post_content: Typhoon Haiyan’s devastation in the Philippines is even worse than first thought: Over 6,000 dead, nearly 1,800 missing, and millions displaced. Help continues through relief efforts like CNN Heroes. #Haiyan #Philippines #Relief

article_content:
A Russian court on Monday ordered that Russian-American journalist Alsu Kurmasheva remain in custody until early December, according to her employer. Kurmasheva, an editor for the U.S.-funded Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty's Tatar-Bashkir service, was detained last week on charges of failing to register as a foreign agent. She appeared in a closed court session in Kazan, the capital of Tatarstan. The court ruled that she be held until December 5, rejecting her lawyer’s request for non-custodial preventive measures.

Kurmasheva is the second U.S. journalist detained in Russia this year, following Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich, who was arrested on espionage charges in March and remains in custody. According to state-run Tatar-Inform, Kurmasheva faces charges for failing to register as a foreign agent and for collecting information on Russian military activities. If convicted, she could face up to five years in prison.

Based in Prague, Kurmasheva traveled to Russia for a family emergency on May 20 and was stopped at Kazan International Airport on June 2. Airport officials confiscated her U.S. and Russian passports, and she was fined for not registering her U.S. passport. According to RFE/RL, she was waiting for her documents to be returned when new charges were filed on Wednesday.

RFE/RL was instructed by Russian authorities in 2017 to register as a foreign agent but has contested the law at the European Court of Human Rights. The organization says it has been fined millions of dollars by Russia. The Committee to Protect Journalists criticized the charges against Kurmasheva as baseless and described her detention as further evidence of Russia’s efforts to stifle independent reporting.

Kurmasheva has reported on ethnic minority communities in Tatarstan and Bashkortostan, including initiatives for Tatar language and culture preservation. Gershkovich and his employer deny the charges against him, and the U.S. government has classified him as wrongfully detained. Russian authorities have not provided details of the evidence against Gershkovich, and court proceedings remain closed because the case is classified.
translated_content:
Inutusan ng isang hukuman sa Russia nitong Lunes na manatili sa kustodiya si Alsu Kurmasheva, isang Russian-American na mamamahayag, hanggang unang bahagi ng Disyembre, ayon sa kanyang pinagtatrabahuhan. Si Kurmasheva, editor sa U.S.-financed na Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty Tatar-Bashkir service, ay inaresto noong nakaraang linggo dahil sa di umano'y kabiguang magparehistro bilang 'foreign agent.' Lumitaw siya sa isang closed session ng korte sa Kazan, kabisera ng Tatarstan. Nagdesisyon ang korte na huwag siyang palayain hanggang Disyembre 5 at tinanggihan ang hiling ng kanyang abogado na sa labas ng kulungan siya manatili habang nililitis.

Si Kurmasheva ay ang pangalawang mamamahayag mula US na naaresto sa Russia ngayong taon, matapos si Evan Gershkovich ng Wall Street Journal, na inakusahan ng espiya noong Marso at nananatiling nakakulong. Ayon sa state-run Tatar-Inform, kakaharapin ni Kurmasheva ang kaso ng hindi pagrerehistro bilang banyagang ahente at umano’y pagkuha ng impormasyon tungkol sa aktibidad ng militar ng Russia. Maaaring umabot sa limang taon ang kanyang parusa kung mapapatunayang nagkasala.

Base sa Prague si Kurmasheva at bumiyahe sa Russia para sa isang personal na emerhensiya noong Mayo 20. Nahinto siya sa Kazan International Airport noong Hunyo 2, kinumpiska roon ang kanyang mga pasaporte sa U.S. at Russia, at pinagmulta dahil hindi nagparehistro ng U.S. passport. Ayon sa RFE/RL, hinihintay niya ang pagbabalik ng kanyang mga dokumento nang sampahan siya ng bagong kaso nitong Miyerkules.

Inutusan ng mga awtoridad ng Russia ang RFE/RL noong 2017 na magparehistro bilang banyagang ahente ngunit kinwestyon ito ng organisasyon sa European Court of Human Rights. Sinasabing milyon-milyong dolyar na multa ang ipinataw ng Russia rito. Tinawag ng Committee to Protect Journalists na walang basehan ang kaso laban kay Kurmasheva at inilarawan ang pag-aresto sa kanya bilang patunay ng paghihigpit ng Russia sa malayang pamamahayag.

Nag-ulat si Kurmasheva tungkol sa mga komunidad ng etnikong minorya sa Tatarstan at Bashkortostan, kasama ang mga hakbang para mapanatili ang wika at kulturang Tatar. Itinanggi ni Gershkovich at ang kanyang pinagtatrabahuhan ang mga alegasyon laban sa kanya, at idineklara ng pamahalaan ng Estados Unidos na siya ay 'wrongfully detained.' Hindi inilahad ng mga awtoridad ng Russia ang mga ebidensya laban kay Gershkovich at nananatiling sarado ang korte dahil classified ang kaso.

article_content: The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) announced that it is closely monitoring the implementation of the ARISE Agenda by Akwa Ibom State Governor Umo Eno, noting that it has begun to deliver visible results. NGE President, Mr. Eze Anaba, made this statement at the Government House in Uyo during a courtesy visit to the governor ahead of the 19th All Nigerian Editors Conference, which is scheduled to take place from November 15 to 19, 2023. Mr. Anaba expressed gratitude to the governor for agreeing to host the conference, and commended the sustained progress in Akwa Ibom State, recognizing the development achievements of successive administrations and the state's peaceful environment. He highlighted that these factors have made Akwa Ibom a top destination, as reflected by the large number of delegates expected at the 2023 ANEC. "We have been following your ARISE Agenda, and it seems Akwa Ibom stands out in Nigeria for its continuity in governance. The government has delivered substantial benefits to its people, and now it's up to the citizens to make the most of these gains," Anaba added. In response, Governor Umo Eno urged journalists to uphold integrity and objectivity in their reporting. He advocated for a free press, where journalists can offer praise, criticism, comments, and suggestions as necessary, while maintaining ethical standards. He emphasized the media's responsibility to shape public opinion and uphold societal values. "We need a free press that is unbiased in its reportage. Give praise where due, comment and suggest where necessary, and criticize when required. The press serves as the conscience of society and plays a major role in setting public agendas," the governor stated. Governor Eno reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to a strong partnership with the media, demonstrated by the recent appointment of 50 media aides. He emphasized that the government welcomes constructive criticism and aims to foster governance that delivers democratic benefits to rural communities and builds public trust. "Since assuming office six months ago, we have fulfilled our campaign promises by focusing our efforts on developing rural areas. The ARISE Agenda, which covers agriculture, rural development, infrastructure, security, and education, guides our initiatives. Our goal is to bring government services to rural communities and provide opportunities for our youth to succeed," Eno said. "We ask the media to help tell the Akwa Ibom story as a people-centered government. We welcome your feedback and suggestions," he added. The NGE delegation included Deputy President Husseina Bangshika; Vice Presidents Sheddy Ozoene (East), Kabir Alabi (West), and Umoru Ibrahim (North); General Secretary Iyobosa Uwugiaren; Assistant General Secretary Gabriel Akinadewo; Treasurer Steve Nwosu; and Social and Publicity Secretary Charles Kalu, among others.
translated_content: Inanunsyo ng Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) na maingat nilang sinusubaybayan ang pagpapatupad ng ARISE Agenda ni Akwa Ibom State Governor Umo Eno, at nakikita na ang positibong bunga nito. Sinabi ito ni NGE President G. Eze Anaba sa Government House sa Uyo, sa isang courtesy visit kay Governor Eno bilang paghahanda sa 19th All Nigerian Editors Conference na gaganapin mula Nobyembre 15 hanggang 19, 2023. Nagpasalamat si G. Anaba kay Governor Eno sa pagtanggap bilang host ng conference at pinuri ang tuloy-tuloy na progreso ng Akwa Ibom State. Kinilala rin niya ang mga tagumpay ng magkakasunod na administrasyon at ang mapayapang kapaligiran sa estado, kaya ito naging patok na destinasyon, na makikita sa dami ng delegates sa 2023 ANEC. "Sinusubaybayan namin ang ARISE Agenda ninyo at mukhang ang Akwa Ibom ang nangunguna sa Nigeria pagdating sa tuloy-tuloy na pamamahala. Naibigay ng gobyerno ang maraming benepisyo sa tao, at ngayon nasa mamamayan na kung paano ito gagamitin," dagdag pa ni Anaba. Bilang tugon, hinikayat ni Governor Umo Eno ang mga mamamahayag na panatilihin ang integridad at pagiging makatarungan sa pagbabalita. Nanawagan siya ng malayang pamamahayag kung saan maaaring magbigay ng papuri, kritisismo, komento, at suhestiyon ang mga journalist basta sumusunod sa etika. Binibigyang-diin din niya ang responsibilidad ng media sa pagbuo ng opinyon ng publiko at tamang direksyon ng lipunan. "Kailangan natin ng malayang press na patas sa kanilang mga ulat. Magbigay ng papuri kung nararapat, magkomento at magmungkahi kung dapat, at magpuna rin kung kinakailangan. Ang press ang konsensya ng lipunan at mahalagang bahagi sa pagtakda ng mga usaping pampubliko," sabi ni Eno. Muling pinagtibay ni Governor Eno ang dedikasyon ng administrasyon sa mahusay na ugnayan sa media, tulad ng ipinakita niya sa pagtatalaga ng 50 media aides. Binigyang-diin niyang bukas ang gobyerno sa makatwirang kritisismo at ang layunin nila ay pangalagaan ang demokrasya para sa mga rural area at palakasin ang tiwala sa gobyerno. "Simula nang maupo kami anim na buwan na ang nakaraan, napatunayan naming tumutupad talaga kami sa aming kampanya. Nakatuon kami sa pag-unlad ng mga rural area. Ang ARISE Agenda namin ay sumasaklaw sa agrikultura, rural development, imprastruktura, seguridad, at edukasyon. Layunin naming dalhin ang serbisyo ng gobyerno sa kanayunan at magbigay ng oportunidad sa kabataan," paliwanag ni Eno. "Nananawagan kami sa media na tulungan kaming ikwento ang tungkol sa Akwa Ibom bilang isang gobyernong nakatuon sa mga tao. Bukas kami sa inyong puna at suhestiyon," dagdag pa niya. Kabilang sa NGE delegation sina Deputy President Husseina Bangshika; Vice Presidents Sheddy Ozoene (East), Kabir Alabi (West), Umoru Ibrahim (North); General Secretary Iyobosa Uwugiaren; Assistant General Secretary Gabriel Akinadewo; Treasurer Steve Nwosu; at Social and Publicity Secretary Charles Kalu, at iba pang miyembro.

article_content:
Rebecca Edmonds dedicated her life to the Air Force, following in her father's footsteps as a military child. After participating in her school's ROTC program, she earned a full Air Force scholarship to Marquette University. Serving her country was her dream, but weeks before she was commissioned as a second lieutenant—with her father, Capt. Tony Edmonds, swearing her in—she learned she was 13 weeks pregnant and kept it a secret out of fear for her career.

At her college graduation in July 2011, Edmonds was proud to have her parents present and her father administer her oath of office as an active-duty officer. However, during a counseling session before her commissioning, she was warned by an officer that pregnancy would have serious professional consequences. Edmonds later said she felt trapped. Raised Catholic, she did not believe in abortion and made plans to begin her service in Virginia.

Six months into her pregnancy, Edmonds disclosed her situation to her commanders. Initially, they showed little concern, but she was soon accused of fraud for not reporting her changed medical status sooner, as required by her ROTC contract. Edmonds was disenrolled from the Air Force.

Now, Edmonds faces a $92,000 student debt with her scholarship revoked and works as a pediatric nurse while caring for her infant son, Dominic. She is challenging her removal under the military’s rule that prohibits single mothers from serving. Edmonds believes her treatment would have been different if she had been married or given her child up for adoption. Air Force representatives have stated that single parenthood is seen as incompatible with military readiness.

Despite the setback, Edmonds does not regret having her son and hopes the military will reconsider its policies, much like the recent changes allowing gay men and women to serve openly. 'I believe a woman has the right to choose life, go on to serve, and reach her full potential, including being an officer in the Air Force,' Edmonds told CNN.
translated_content:
Inialay ni Rebecca Edmonds ang kanyang buhay sa Air Force, sumusunod sa yapak ng kanyang ama bilang anak ng sundalo. Pagkatapos sumali sa ROTC ng kanyang paaralan, nakakuha siya ng full scholarship mula sa Air Force papuntang Marquette University. Pangarap niyang maglingkod sa bansa, ngunit ilang linggo bago siya maging second lieutenant—kasama ang kanyang ama, si Capt. Tony Edmonds, na nagsumpa sa kanya—nalaman niyang siya ay 13 linggong buntis at itinago ito dahil sa takot para sa kanyang career.

Sa kanyang pagtatapos noong Hulyo 2011, masayang-masaya si Edmonds na nandoon ang kanyang magulang at si Papa ang nag-administer ng panunumpa niya bilang opisyal. Pero bago siya makomisyon, binalaan siya ng isang opisyal na magiging malaking problema sa propesyon ang pagbubuntis. Sabi ni Edmonds, pakiramdam niya ay wala na siyang ibang magagawa. Bilang isang Katoliko, hindi niya isinasaalang-alang ang aborsyon at nagplano pa rin siyang maglingkod sa Virginia.

Lumipas ang anim na buwan ng pagbubuntis bago niya ipaalam sa mga commander niya ang sitwasyon. Sa una, walang isyu, pero di nagtagal ay inakusahan siyang nagkasala dahil hindi agad nai-report ang medical status niya, batay sa ROTC contract. Natanggal si Edmonds sa Air Force.

Ngayon, kailangang bayaran ni Edmonds ang $92,000 na scholarship loan habang nagtatrabaho siyang pediatric nurse at inaalagaan ang anak niyang si Dominic. Inaapela niya ang pagkakatanggal batay sa patakaran ng military na hindi tumatanggap ng single mother. Para kay Edmonds, sigurado siyang iba ang naging trato kung siya ay kasal o ipinaampon ang anak. Ayon sa Air Force, ang pagiging solo parent ay hadlang sa military readiness.

Kahit sa hirap, hindi niya pinagsisisihan ang anak at umaasa siyang mababago pa ng military ang polisiya, gaya ng pagbabagong pinayagan ang mga openly gay na makapaglingkod. 'Naniniwala akong may karapatan ang isang babae na pumili ng buhay, maglingkod, at abutin ang buong potensyal niya, kabilang ang pagiging opisyal sa Air Force,' ani Edmonds sa CNN.
post_content: Rebecca Edmonds worked hard for her dream of joining the Air Force, but got kicked out for keeping her pregnancy a secret. Now a pediatric nurse, she's hoping for policy change so single moms can serve too! 💪👶 #MilitaryLife #WomensRights #RealStories
translated_post: Nagtiyaga si Rebecca Edmonds para sa Air Force dream niya—pero natanggal dahil sa sikreto niyang pagbubuntis. Nurse na siya ngayon, at umaasang puwedeng magsilbi ang solo moms sa military! 💪👩‍👧 #BabaeSaSerbisyo #TunayNaKuwento

article_content: Stuart Broad has dismissed allegations of bullying within the England cricket team made by former batsman Kevin Pietersen and is instead choosing to enjoy his autumn break. The 28-year-old Nottinghamshire player posted a photo of himself enjoying a Halloween-themed night out with his girlfriend, Bealey Mitchell, and another female friend. Broad and Mitchell attended the Red Bull Culture Clash music event at London's Earl's Court on Thursday and he shared that he 'had such fun last night!' Broad posted a picture of the promotional flyer for the event on his Instagram. The England fast bowler and Bealey Mitchell were also pictured sharing a glass of champagne on the Oval cricket ground earlier in August. These social media posts follow recent claims by Pietersen, detailed in his autobiography, that a culture of 'bullying' existed in the England dressing room, with Anderson and Broad allegedly involved. Broad has rejected these accusations. The England team is set to travel to Sri Lanka for a one-day series at the end of November, with further preparations for the 2015 World Cup involving matches against Australia and India scheduled for January. Broad played a key part in England's comeback during the latter part of the summer, as captain Alastair Cook led the team to a 3-1 Test series win over India. Pietersen's claims of bullying have been publicly denied by Broad, who was part of the England side that secured the Test series victory against India.
translated_content: Tinanggihan ni Stuart Broad ang mga paratang ng pambu-bully sa koponan ng England na ibinunyag ng dating batsman na si Kevin Pietersen at pinili niyang mag-enjoy sa kanyang autumn break. Nag-post ang 28-anyos na Nottinghamshire player ng litrato kasama ang kanyang girlfriend na si Bealey Mitchell at isa pang babaeng kaibigan sa isang Halloween-themed na lakad. Dumalo sina Broad at Mitchell sa Red Bull Culture Clash music event sa Earl's Court, London nitong Huwebes at ibinahagi niya na 'sobrang saya kagabi!' Nag-post din si Broad ng larawan ng event flyer sa kanyang Instagram. Nakuhanan din ng litrato si Broad at Bealey Mitchell na nagchi-champagne sa cricket ground ng The Oval noong Agosto. Ang mga post na ito sa social media ay kasunod ng mga pahayag ni Pietersen sa kanyang autobiography na may 'kulturang pambu-bully' daw sa loob ng dressing room ng England, kung saan diumano'y sangkot sina Anderson at Broad. Mariing itinanggi ni Broad ang mga ito. Magbibiyahe ang England team patungong Sri Lanka para sa isang one-day series sa katapusan ng Nobyembre, at maghahanda pa para sa 2015 World Cup sa pamamagitan ng mga laban kontra Australia at India ngayong Enero. Mahalagang papel ang ginampanan ni Broad sa pagbawi ng England nitong huling bahagi ng tag-init, kung saan pinangunahan ni captain Alastair Cook ang koponan sa 3-1 Test series win laban sa India. Mariing itinanggi ni Broad sa publiko ang mga paratang ni Pietersen ukol sa pambu-bully, at kabilang siya sa England team na nagwagi laban sa India sa Test series.

article_content: At least two Australian tourists have been seriously injured in a light plane crash in Zimbabwe. The Cessna aircraft crashed in a paddock near Lupinyu Business Centre shortly after taking off from Victoria Falls International Airport on Sunday. According to Zimbabwe's The Herald newspaper, two Australian tourists and their German pilot were admitted to Victoria Falls District Hospital. However, ABC reported that three Australians were critically injured in the crash. Local villagers said the plane turned back toward the airport around 11 a.m. after an engine failure. 'Soon after, we heard a loud bang near our fields, and we ran and saw it hitting trees as it crashed,' one villager told The Herald. 'We then attended the scene and rescued the victims.' Another villager noted that the tourists appeared to be seriously injured, as they were bleeding heavily. 'We managed to pull them out of the wreckage before ambulances arrived and rushed them to the hospital in Victoria Falls,' the villager said. The tourists were reportedly en route to Hwange National Park, with plans to continue to Mana Pools. Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirmed that embassy staff in Harare are following up on the reports and are ready to provide consular assistance.
translated_content: Dalawa o higit pang turistang Australyano ang malubhang nasugatan sa isang aksidente ng maliit na eroplano sa Zimbabwe. Ang Cessna aircraft ay bumagsak sa isang bukirin malapit sa Lupinyu Business Centre, ilang sandali lang matapos mag-take off mula sa Victoria Falls International Airport noong Linggo. Ayon sa The Herald ng Zimbabwe, dalawang turistang Australyano at ang kanilang German na piloto ang dinala sa Victoria Falls District Hospital. Subalit iniulat ng ABC na tatlong Australyano ang kritikal ang lagay matapos ang aksidente. Ayon sa mga lokal na residente, ang eroplano ay bumalik patungo sa paliparan bandang alas-onse ng umaga matapos magkaaberya ang makina. ‘Pagkatapos noon, narinig namin ang malakas na tunog malapit sa aming mga palayan, at nakita naming bumangga ito sa mga puno bago bumagsak,’ kwento ng isang residente sa The Herald. ‘Agad kaming nagpunta sa lugar at tinulungan ang mga biktima.’ Ibinahagi pa ng isa pang residente na tila malala ang mga sugat ng mga turista dahil matindi ang pagdurugo nila. 'Nakuha naming hilahin sila mula sa gumuhong eroplano bago pa dumating ang ambulansya na nagdala sa kanila sa ospital sa Victoria Falls,' pahayag ng residente. Ang mga turista ay papunta sana sa Hwange National Park, at balak ding dumiretso sa Mana Pools. Kumpirmado ng Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade ng Australia na may staff mula sa embahada sa Harare na tumututok sa insidente at handang magbigay ng konsular na tulong.

article_content: Lesley Reeve, 56, and her husband Andrew, 55, were sentenced to two and a half years in prison after stealing nearly all their 91-year-old godmother’s life savings. The couple spent all but £3,000 of Joan Killen’s £130,000 after being made signatories on her bank accounts. At Teesside Crown Court, Judge Simon Bourne-Arton described their actions as a gross breach of trust, noting that although the Reeves had previously been hardworking, they were 'utterly materialistic.' The court heard that the Reeves cleared personal debts, bought a car for one of their sons, purchased electrical goods and gifts for themselves, and converted the garage of their Hartlepool home into a wet room and gym. They told police the renovation was for Miss Killen, but she was living in a care home at the time. The couple claimed Miss Killen was happy for them to spend her money as they wished and intended to leave them her savings in her will. However, while the Reeves spent lavishly, Miss Killen lived modestly in a care home and now relies on state support for her care costs. On one occasion, when Miss Killen asked for her personal belongings, care home staff had to buy her basic items since the Reeves did not provide them. Judge Bourne-Arton emphasized the lack of remorse shown by the couple and pointed out that their visits to Miss Killen became infrequent once her money was depleted. The Reeves attributed this to disagreements with care home staff. Lesley and Andrew Reeve were convicted of stealing £95,000 in savings and rental income from letting Miss Killen’s property. Lesley Reeve was also found guilty of taking £2,940 in pension payments. The couple now face legal proceedings to confiscate their assets. Paul Abrahams, defending Mr. Reeve, said the couple will struggle with separation during their prison terms, and Mr. Reeve is likely to lose his job. Nigel Soppitt, defending Mrs. Reeve, said she risks losing her reputation, home, and possibly her mental health.
translated_content: Sina Lesley Reeve, 56, at ang kanyang asawang si Andrew, 55, ay hinatulan ng dalawang at kalahating taon sa kulungan matapos nilang nakawin ang halos lahat ng ipon ng kanilang 91-anyos na ninang. Ginastos ng mag-asawa ang lahat liban sa £3,000 mula sa £130,000 na ipon ni Joan Killen, pagkatapos silang gawing signatory sa mga bank account nito. Sa Teesside Crown Court, inilarawan ni Judge Simon Bourne-Arton ang ginawa nila bilang matinding paglabag sa tiwala, at binanggit na kahit dati silang masipag, sila ay 'lubhang materyalistiko.' Lumabas sa korte na ginamit nila ang pera para bayaran ang sariling utang, bumili ng kotse para sa isa sa kanilang mga anak, bumili ng mga gamit pang-kuryente at mga regalo para sa sarili, at pinarenovate ang kanilang garahe sa Hartlepool bilang wet room at gym. Sinabi nila sa pulisya na para raw ito kay Miss Killen, ngunit siya ay nakatira na noon sa care home. Ipinagtanggol naman ng mag-asawa na pumayag si Miss Killen na gastusin nila ang kanyang pera at balak daw ibigay sa kanila ang ipon sa kanyang huling habilin. Ngunit habang maluho ang gastos ng mag-asawa, simple ang buhay ni Miss Killen sa care home at ngayon ay umaasa na lamang sa suporta ng gobyerno para sa kanyang gastusin. Isang beses, nang hilingin ni Miss Killen ang kanyang mga personal na gamit, ang staff ng care home pa ang bumili ng mga pangunahing gamit para sa kanya dahil hindi ito naibigay ng mag-asawa. Binanggit ni Judge Bourne-Arton ang kawalan ng pagsisisi ng mag-asawa, at pinansin din na naging madalang ang pagdalaw nila kay Miss Killen nang maubos na ang kanyang pera. Sabi ng mag-asawa, ito raw ay dahil sa hindi pagkakasundo sa staff ng care home. Napatunayang nagkasala sina Lesley at Andrew Reeve sa pagnanakaw ng £95,000 mula sa savings at kita sa pagrenta ng bahay ni Miss Killen. Si Lesley Reeve ay napatunayang nagkasala rin sa pagkuha ng £2,940 mula sa kanyang pension. Ngayon ay haharap ang mag-asawa sa legal na hakbang para kumpiskahin ang kanilang mga ari-arian. Ayon kay Paul Abrahams, abogado ni Mr. Reeve, mahihirapan daw ang mag-asawa kung magkakahiwalay sa kulungan at posibleng mawalan ng trabaho si Mr. Reeve. Sabi naman ni Nigel Soppitt, abogado ni Mrs. Reeve, maaaring mawalan si Mrs. Reeve ng reputasyon, bahay, at posibleng ng kanyang mental health.
post_content: A couple was jailed for stealing almost all of a 91-year-old dementia sufferer's savings, splurging on themselves while leaving her in care. Trust broken, assets seized, and no remorse shown. #CrimeNews #TrustBreach #JusticeServed
translated_post: Kinulong ang mag-asawang nagnakaw ng ipon ng kanilang 91-anyos na ninang para lang magluho, habang naiwan siyang umaasa sa tulong. Wala silang pagsisisi at ngayon, kumpiskado pa ang kanilang ari-arian. #BalitangKrimen #Katarungan

article_content: Ozempic has gained global attention not only for its effectiveness in promoting weight loss, but also for its potential wider impact on the economy. Ozempic is a brand name for semaglutide, a diabetes medication that also supports weight loss when injected weekly, mainly by reducing appetite. Semaglutide is also marketed as Wegovy for weight loss purposes. While it's too soon to determine the full economic impact of GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic, companies and analysts are already observing significant changes in consumer behavior. For instance, Walmart reports that customers using GLP-1 medications are spending less on food but more on lifestyle and fitness products. Nik Modi, a managing director at RBC Capital Markets specializing in consumer goods, told Insider this reflects a shift in spending, not a reduction: 'Consumers are looking for better-for-you products,' Modi said, predicting that healthier product sales will grow as consumers adjust their habits. The potential effects extend beyond food and healthcare. Economics writer Josh Barro, in his newsletter 'Very Serious,' suggested that these medications could lead to a healthier, longer-living, and more productive workforce. Barro wrote, 'Lower disease burden will mean fewer sick days and higher labor productivity.' He also noted that improved weight management could boost self-esteem and allow people to redirect their energy and resources from dieting into other activities. Businesses are already recording changes: Clinical trials show that GLP-1 drugs can help patients lose an average of 15% of their body weight over 68 weeks. An August Morgan Stanley survey of 300 GLP-1 users found 77% visited fast-food restaurants less frequently, with 61% and 59% reporting reduced visits to casual dining restaurants and coffee shops, respectively. GLP-1 drugs may also indirectly benefit other sectors. According to a Jefferies Financial analyst, United Airlines could save 27.6 million gallons of fuel annually—worth $80 million—if the average passenger weighed 10 pounds less. Some patients have also experienced reduced cravings for alcohol, tobacco, and even opioids, suggesting possible future uses for addiction treatment, though GLP-1s are not currently approved for this purpose. These side effects might have additional economic or workforce benefits. Despite these promising trends, the drugs remain expensive—Ozempic costs about $1,000 per month, and Wegovy is often pricier. Insurance coverage for those without diabetes is limited; many companies are hesitant to provide coverage, and patients may require lifelong treatment. If medical advances allow more people to live longer and healthier lives, there could be economic gains from reduced healthcare costs, lower insurance premiums, savings on groceries and dining out, and increased workforce participation. James van Geelen of Citrinitas Capital, in an appearance on Bloomberg's 'Odd Lots' podcast, compared obesity to the COVID-19 crisis and discussed ways to increase access to weight-loss medications. 'Why shouldn't the government pay for this?' van Geelen asked, noting the precedent of free COVID vaccines. While obesity doesn't trigger lockdowns like COVID, addressing it could save lives and provide significant economic advantages. Van Geelen suggested that, if the benefits and side effects of these drugs are proven, government coverage would be justified.
translated_content: Sumikat ang Ozempic sa buong mundo hindi lang dahil sa epekto nito sa pagbabawas ng timbang, kundi pati na rin sa posibleng mas malawak na epekto nito sa ekonomiya. Ang Ozempic ay brand name ng semaglutide, isang gamot para sa diabetes na tumutulong din magpapayat kapag itinurok linggo-linggo, pangunahin sa pamamagitan ng pagbabawas ng gana. Kilala rin bilang Wegovy ang semaglutide para sa layunin ng pagpapapayat. Bagama’t maaga pa para matukoy ang kabuuang epekto sa ekonomiya ng mga GLP-1 na gamot tulad ng Ozempic, napapansin na ng mga kumpanya at eksperto ang malalaking pagbabago sa gawi ng mamimili. Halimbawa, iniulat ng Walmart na ang mga kostumer na gumagamit ng GLP-1 na gamot ay mas kaunti ang ginagastos sa pagkain pero mas malaki ang inilaan sa pamumuhay at fitness. Ayon kay Nik Modi, managing director ng RBC Capital Markets na dalubhasa sa consumer goods, ito ay pagbabago lamang kung paano gumastos ang mga tao; hindi naman bumababa ang kabuuang gastusin: 'Hinahanap ng mga consumer ang mas malusog na mga produkto,' aniya, at inaasahan na lalaki ang benta ng mga ito habang nagbabago ang ugali ng mga mamimili. Lampas pa sa pagkain at healthcare ang posibleng epekto. Ayon kay economics writer Josh Barro sa kaniyang newsletter na 'Very Serious,' ang mga gamot na ito ay maaaring magdulot ng mas malusog, mas matagal mabuhay, at mas produktibong lakas-paggawa. Sabi ni Barro, 'Ang mas mababang pasanin ng sakit ay nangangahulugan ng mas kaunting absent at mas mataas na produktibidad.' Dagdag pa niya, puwedeng magpataas ng self-esteem ang mas magandang timbang at bigyan ng pagkakataon ang mga tao na gamitin ang kanilang oras at pera sa iba pa, kaysa puro pagda-diet lang. Nakikita na ng mga negosyo ang mga pagbabagong ito: Ipinapakita ng mga clinical trial na ang GLP-1 na gamot ay nakakatulong sa mga pasyente na bawasan ang 15% ng kanilang timbang sa loob ng 68 linggo. Sa survey ng Morgan Stanley noong Agosto na may 300 gumagamit ng GLP-1, 77% ang nagsabing mas bihira na silang kumain sa fast food, 61% sa mga casual dining restaurant, at 59% naman sa mga coffee shop. Puwede ring mapakinabangan ng ibang industriya ang GLP-1 medicines. Sabi ng Jefferies Financial analyst, makakatipid ang United Airlines ng 27.6 milyong galon ng gasolina bawat taon—halaga ng $80 milyon—kung ang karaniwang pasahero ay bababa ng 10 pounds ang timbang. May mga pasyente ring nakapansin ng mas mababang interes sa alak, yosi, at opioids, na nagpapahiwatig ng potensyal na gamit sa addiction therapy, kahit hindi pa ito aprobadong indikasyon. Ang mga epekto na ito ay puwedeng magbigay pa ng dagdag benepisyo sa ekonomiya at workforce. Kahit promising ang mga pagbabagong ito, mahal pa rin ang gamot—abot $1,000 kada buwan ang Ozempic, mas mahal pa minsan ang Wegovy. Limitado ang insurance coverage para sa mga walang diabetes; maraming kumpanya ang nag-aalangan din magbigay ng coverage, at madalas ay kailangan habambuhay gamitin ng pasyente ang gamot. Kung tuluy-tuloy ang medikal na advancements at hahaba’t gaganda ang buhay ng mga tao, puwedeng dumami ang economic gains mula sa nabawasang healthcare gastos, mababang insurance premium, natitipid sa grocery o pagkain sa labas, at mas maraming manggagawang tatagal sa trabaho. Sa panayam sa Bloomberg's 'Odd Lots' podcast, inihambing ni James van Geelen ng Citrinitas Capital ang obesity epidemic sa COVID crisis at tinalakay kung paano mapapalawak ang access sa weight-loss medicines. 'Bakit hindi pwedeng gobyerno ang magbayad nito?' tanong ni van Geelen, tinutukoy ang libreng COVID vaccines. Kahit walang lockdown na dala, puwedeng magligtas ng buhay at maghatid ng malalaking benepisyo sa ekonomiya kapag natugunan ito. Sabi pa niya, kung mapapatunayang epektibo at ligtas ang gamot, tama lang na pondohan ng gobyerno.
post_content: Ozempic isn't just about weight loss—it could change how we spend, work, and live! From eating less fast food to boosting productivity and saving on healthcare, big economic shifts might be coming. Should the gov’t cover the cost like with COVID vaccines? #Ozempic #WellnessEconomy

article_content: CNA garnered international recognition at the 2023 w3 Awards, securing two Gold and two Silver honors. These awards celebrate excellence in digital platforms—spanning websites, marketing, video, mobile, social media, podcasts, and emerging tech—and winners are selected by the industry leaders of the Academy of Interactive and Visual Arts. CNA's web video 'Asia’s Great Climate Frontiers' took home Gold in the Environmental & Sustainability category. Journalist Jack Board traveled to Nepal, Mongolia, the Philippines, Thailand, and Vietnam, sharing the stories of people facing the direct impacts of climate change, including fishermen, nomads, and rice farmers. The network also won Gold for 'The Serial Swindler' in the Crime & Mystery podcast category. Produced by Tiffany Ang and edited by Crispina Robert, this two-part program is based on the documentary 'Catching A Scammer: Singapore's Serial Swindler,' and investigates both the con artist and those affected by the scam. Additionally, the 'Womankind' podcast, hosted by Penelope Chan and Hidayah Salamat, was awarded Silver for its thoughtful discussions on important issues for women, especially topics that are not widely discussed. CNA’s mobile app and news website were also recognized, obtaining Silver in the news category—a testament to the platform’s continued excellence, having previously won other major awards. Loh Chee Kong, CNA Digital’s chief editor, commended all teams for earning top-tier international recognition and emphasized their ongoing commitment to delivering high-quality content on various platforms to serve diverse audiences.
