article_content:
India emerged victorious against Australia in a last-ball thriller, clinching a two-wicket win in the opening T20I of a five-match series at Dr YSR ACA-VDCA Stadium in Visakhapatnam on Thursday night. Although India's bowling attack lacked experience, the batters rose to the occasion, with captain Suryakumar Yadav leading the charge with a commanding 80 off 42 balls.

India required seven runs in the final over and had five wickets in hand, but Australia’s Sean Abbott made things tense. Rinku Singh managed a four and a single, yet India dramatically lost three wickets in three consecutive balls, taking the match to the wire. Rinku (28 not out) then secured the victory by hitting a six off a no-ball.

Both sides had rested several star players, offering younger talent a platform to shine. Australia’s Josh Inglis sparkled with a scintillating 110 off 50 balls—his maiden T20I hundred—while Suryakumar Yadav and Ishan Kishan (58 off 39) anchored India’s successful chase. Mukesh Kumar’s disciplined bowling was decisive, as he allowed just five runs in Australia’s final over.

Batting first, Australia posted a challenging 208 for three, with stand-in players filling the shoes of Travis Head, Glenn Maxwell, and Adam Zampa. The bowling, however, faltered due to erratic lines, contributing 12 wides to India’s total.

India’s chase began brightly as Yashasvi Jaiswal struck early boundaries, but Ruturaj Gaikwad was unfortunate to be run out without scoring. Jaiswal followed soon after for 21. Suryakumar and Kishan then combined for a 112-run partnership for the third wicket. Kishan’s 58 included five sixes and two fours, while Suryakumar achieved his 16th T20I half-century before being dismissed for 80.

Earlier, Inglis paired with Steve Smith (52) to attack the Indian bowling lineup, with Smith reaching his 5th T20I half-century. Some missed catches, including three by Ravi Bishnoi, enabled Australia to reach a formidable total. Inglis’s explosive innings featured 11 boundaries and 8 sixes.

Smith was eventually run out after losing his footing, and Inglis was dismissed soon after. Marcus Stoinis and Tim David contributed valuable runs to push Australia past 200. Mukesh Kumar stood out among India’s bowlers, conceding just 29 runs in his four overs and keeping Australia in check at the death.

article_content: A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck Indonesia’s Banda Sea on Wednesday, according to the United States Geological Survey, with no immediate reports of damage or casualties. No tsunami warning was issued for the quake—which was initially reported as a magnitude 6.9—and it occurred at 11:53 am local time (0453 GMT), the USGS said. The Indonesian Meteorological, Climatological and Geophysical Agency (BMKG) stated that the tremor was felt moderately in Saumlaki, a town in the Tanimbar Islands. 'The earthquake was quite intense. But people here were not panicking. We are used to having earthquakes,' Saumlaki resident Lambert Tatang shared with AFP. 'Especially after we learned there was no tsunami threat, so life is just normal now,' the 41-year-old added. Indonesia frequently experiences earthquakes because it sits on the Pacific 'Ring of Fire,' an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin. In November last year, a 5.6-magnitude quake struck West Java, killing 602 people. The 2004 Sumatra earthquake, with a magnitude of 9.1, triggered a tsunami that killed 220,000 people across the region, including about 170,000 in Indonesia.

Ayon sa Indonesian Meteorological, Climatological and Geophysical Agency (BMKG), katamtamang naramdaman ang pagyanig sa bayan ng Saumlaki sa Tanimbar Islands. 'Medyo malakas ang lindol. Pero hindi naman nag-panic ang mga tao dito. Sanay na kami sa lindol,' sabi ni Lambert Tatang, isang residente ng Saumlaki, sa AFP. 'Lalo na nang malaman naming walang banta ng tsunami, kaya balik-normal na lang ang lahat,' dagdag pa ng 41-anyos. Madalas makaranas ng lindol ang Indonesia dahil ito ay nasa Pacific 'Ring of Fire,' isang sonang masiglang seismic mula Japan, sa buong Southeast Asia, at sa Pacific basin. Noong Nobyembre ng nakaraang taon, isang 5.6-magnitude na lindol ang tumama sa West Java, kung saan 602 katao ang namatay. Ang lindol noong 2004 sa Sumatra, na may lakas na 9.1, ay nagdulot ng tsunami na ikinasawi ng 220,000 katao sa rehiyon, kabilang ang nasa 170,000 sa Indonesia.

article_content: Stefan Serie, a 30-year-old health teacher at Merrick Avenue Middle School in Long Island, New York, claims he was forced to resign after appearing shirtless at a lively pool party on the Bravo reality TV show 'Princesses: Long Island.' Serie, an eight-year teaching veteran rated as 'highly effective' the previous school year, made a brief cameo in the debut episode, laughing in the background as cast members drank alcohol and partied by the pool. One week after the episode aired on June 2, 2013, Serie says he was summoned to the school district office, where administrators told him his offer of tenure would be rescinded and pressured him to resign, despite no illegal behavior occurring in the scene. "I didn't do anything I would tell my students not to do," Serie told the New York Daily News. Nevertheless, he says he reluctantly agreed to resign, giving up his $75,000-a-year job. He characterized his departure as a coerced resignation. According to the Daily News, Serie has degrees in health and physical education from Hofstra University and now seeks reinstatement. He has indicated that he would consider suing the TV show if the school refuses. Serie said he realized after the party descended into chaos—culminating in a profanity-laden argument between two cast members—that he no longer wanted to be associated with the show. Though he appeared fully clothed during much of this, he still felt his reputation was affected. "I want my job and tenure back. I think I deserve it," Serie said. Parents are also upset by the school's actions, with some planning to protest at a district meeting. Rosemary Garofolo, whose children were taught by Serie, praised his teaching and questioned why his off-duty activities should matter as long as they were legal. A Bravo producer friend invited Serie to the show, and cast member Ashlee White asked him to attend the party. The Bellmore Merrick Central School District superintendent, John DeTommaso, confirmed that Serie submitted his resignation on June 26, 2013, which was accepted on July 9. He stated that the district cannot provide further details as it is a personnel matter. Serie described the ordeal as devastating but is hopeful about returning to teaching.

Si Serie, na may walong taon sa pagtuturo at tinuring na 'highly effective' noong nakaraang taon, ay maikling lumabas sa unang episode, tumatawa sa background habang ang mga cast ay umiinom ng alak at nagsasaya sa tabi ng pool. Isang linggo matapos umere ang episode noong Hunyo 2, 2013, sinabi ni Serie na ipinatawag siya ng school district administrators, kung saan sinabi sa kanyang babawiin ang alok ng tenure at pinilit siyang magbitiw, kahit wala namang ilegal na nangyari sa eksena. "Wala akong ginawang bagay na ipagbabawal ko sa mga estudyante ko," ani Serie sa New York Daily News. Gayunpaman, sinabi niyang napilitan siyang magbitiw at isuko ang kanyang trabahong may sahod na $75,000 kada taon. Inilarawan niya ang kanyang pag-alis bilang isang sapilitang pagbibitiw. Ayon sa Daily News, may mga degree si Serie sa health at physical education mula Hofstra University at ngayon ay naghahangad na maibalik sa serbisyo. Nabanggit din niyang maaaring magsampa siya ng kaso laban sa TV show kung hindi siya ibabalik ng paaralan. Napagtanto raw ni Serie na ayaw na niyang maiugnay sa palabas matapos maging magulo ang party, na nauwi sa murahan ng dalawang cast member. Kahit naka-damit siya sa bahaging iyon, naramdaman pa ring naapektuhan ang kanyang reputasyon. "Gusto ko ang trabaho at tenure ko pabalik. Pakiramdam ko karapat-dapat akong bumalik," wika ni Serie. Dismayado rin ang mga magulang sa desisyon ng paaralan at may ilan na nagpaplanong magprotesta sa isang district meeting. Pinuri ni Rosemary Garofolo, magulang ng kanyang mga estudyante, ang pagtuturo ni Serie at kinuwestyon kung bakit pinakikialaman pa ang kanyang pribadong oras basta't wala namang nilalabag na batas. Isang kaibigan niyang producer mula sa Bravo ang nag-imbita kay Serie sa show, at si Ashlee White na miyembro ng cast ang nag-anyaya sa kanya sa party. Ayon sa kanya, hindi na sila maaaring magbigay pa ng detalye dahil ito ay personnel matter. Inilarawan ni Serie ang naging karanasan bilang napakasakit, ngunit umaasa pa rin siyang makakabalik sa pagtuturo.

article_content: Mary Kennedy, estranged wife of Robert F. Kennedy Jr., encountered extreme financial and emotional difficulties before her death at age 52. In May, she was discovered hanged in a barn at the family’s Bedford, New York estate. Friends and reports indicate that, amid a contentious divorce, she was largely cut off from shared financial resources—forcing her to borrow money from parents of her children’s schoolmates to cover basic expenses. Her legal team was allegedly owed more than $278,000 in unpaid fees, and a $20,000 court-approved credit card was revoked, leaving her unable to pay for groceries, gas, or medical care while struggling with depression and alcoholism. During the protracted divorce proceedings, Robert Kennedy Jr. had primary temporary custody of their four children—Kyra, Aiden, Conor, and William—and began publicly appearing with his new girlfriend, actress Cheryl Hines. The legal and financial battles were accompanied by scrutiny of Mary’s mental health, with Kennedy’s camp questioning her fitness as a mother. Following her passing, the Kennedy and Richardson families disputed her burial arrangements. At her funeral, Robert Kennedy Jr. maintained he had made every effort to support her, describing a final conversation they shared. Their relationship, which began in the early 1990s while Robert’s first marriage was ending, was marked by both parties’ struggles with addiction: Robert with drugs and Mary with anorexia, as reported by Newsweek, dating back to her time at Putney School in Vermont. Legal filings show their divorce was filed in 2010 but never completed. As their marriage deteriorated, legal costs exceeded $1 million and monthly expenses for their estate approached $40,000, exacerbating Mary’s financial strain. After separating, Mary’s personal struggles became public: she was twice arrested for driving under the influence, and acquaintances noted increasing credit card debt and fear of losing both her home and her children’s custody. Robert Kennedy reportedly obtained restraining orders during this period, alleging Mary was unfit to parent. Mary’s family has disputed numerous claims contained in sealed divorce documents—including blackmail, pet abuse, and threats—describing them as retaliatory and inaccurate. Kerry Kennedy, a longtime friend and Robert's sister, shared posthumously that Mary had battled mental illness for decades but did so with fortitude. Despite ongoing legal negotiations regarding her support and custody matters, Mary died by suicide before the divorce was finalized, leaving behind a complex and tragic legacy.
translated_content: Si Mary Kennedy, dating asawa ni Robert F. Kennedy Jr., ay humarap sa matinding problema sa pera at emosyonal na pagsubok bago ang kanyang pagkamatay sa edad na 52. Noong Mayo, natagpuang nakabigti si Mary sa kamalig ng kanilang pamilya sa Bedford, New York. Ayon sa mga kaibigan at mga ulat, dahil sa magulong proseso ng diborsyo, halos nawala ang access niya sa perang dapat pinaghahatian nila—kaya napilitan siyang manghiram ng pera sa mga magulang ng mga kaklase ng kanyang mga anak para matustusan ang pang-araw-araw. Umabot sa mahigit $278,000 ang utang niya sa mga abogado, at binawi pa ang court-approved credit card na may $20,000 na limit kada buwan. Dahil dito, nawalan siya ng pambili ng pagkain, gasolina, at gamot habang nilalabanan ang depresyon at alcoholism. Habang natatagalan ang diborsyo, nakuha ni Robert Kennedy Jr. ang pansamantalang pangunahing kustodiya ng apat nilang anak—sina Kyra, Aiden, Conor, at William—at nakita siyang madalas kasama ang bagong nobyang aktres na si Cheryl Hines. Kasabay ng alitan sa pera at korte, inusisa at kinuwestiyon din ang kakayahan ni Mary bilang ina dahil sa kanyang mental health. Pagkatapos niyang pumanaw, nagkaroon ng hidwaan ang pamilya Kennedy at Richardson ukol sa libing ni Mary. Sa burol, iginiit ni Robert Kennedy Jr. na ginawa niya ang lahat ng kanyang makakaya at binanggit ang huling usapan nila bago siya namatay. Nagsimula ang kanilang relasyon noong 1990s habang natatapos pa lang ang unang kasal ni Robert. Parehong may dinadalang adiksyon—nagkaproblema si Robert sa droga at si Mary ay matagal nang may anorexia mula pa sa Putney School sa Vermont, ayon sa Newsweek. Lumabas sa mga dokumento na sinimulan ang diborsyo noong 2010 ngunit hindi natapos. Habang pinagtatalunan ang kanilang relasyon, umabot sa higit $1 milyon ang legal fees at halos $40,000 kada buwan ang ginagastos sa kanilang estate—mas lalong nabaon si Mary sa utang. Paghiwalay nila, naging lantad din ang mga pagsubok ni Mary: dalawang beses siyang nahuli dahil sa pagmamaneho habang lasing, at sabi ng mga kaibigan ay marami siyang utang at takot na mawalan ng tahanan at kustodiya. Nag-file din si Robert Kennedy ng ilang restraining order laban kay Mary, na umano'y hindi siya fit bilang ina. Tutol dito ang pamilya ni Mary, lalo na sa mga alegasyon sa divorce documents gaya ng blackmail, pagmamalupit sa hayop, at pagbabanta—na tinatawag nilang paninira. Ayon kay Kerry Kennedy, matalik na kaibigan at kapatid ni Robert, matagal nang nilabanan ni Mary ang mental illness. Sa kabila ng mga usapang legal, nagpakamatay si Mary bago ma-finalize ang diborsyo, nag-iwan ng komplikado at malungkot na kwento.

article_content: A British tourist has died after falling about 90 metres from a cliff onto rocks below in Sydney's northern beaches. The man, believed to be a 25-year-old British tourist named Gareth Jones from Wales, fell after he climbed a fence at North Head near Manly at around 6:45am on Sunday. He and his friends had walked to the edge of the cliff to watch the sunrise when he reportedly slipped accidentally. While NSW Police have not confirmed the man's identity, Nine News has identified the victim as Gareth Jones. Four witnesses, thought to be his friends, are being interviewed by investigators. Two friends reportedly climbed down the cliff using ropes and ladders typically used by fishermen, but found their friend unresponsive. Police from the NSW Police Rescue Unit recovered the man's body, which was brought up from the cliff at 11:30am and handed over to authorities. Inspector Belinda Caddy told Nine News, 'It looks like a tragic accident and we feel for all the people that were there. Our thoughts will be with his family when we inform them.' North Head's clifftops are famous for their panoramic views of Sydney Harbour and are a popular tourist spot on the northern beaches. Inspector Nigel Taylor told the Sydney Morning Herald that the group had been sitting on the cliff edge watching the sunrise when tragedy happened. 'When they returned to the lookout, the young man went to have a closer look and fell over the edge,' Inspector Taylor said. Police have warned the public never to climb over fences or into restricted areas due to the risk of serious injury or death. This incident follows several similar recent accidents in the region. In the past months, a woman fell to her death in the Blue Mountains while meditating near a cliff edge with friends. In November, Megan Moody, 38, died after slipping off a 25-metre cliff in Tahmoor, southwestern Sydney, as her partner Paul Vietch watched. In the same month in South Maroubra, two fishermen were criticized for risking their lives by fishing off a 20-metre cliff.
translated_content: Isang British na turista ang namatay matapos mahulog mula sa humigit-kumulang 90 metrong bangin at bumagsak sa mga bato sa northern beaches ng Sydney. Ang lalaki, na pinaniniwalaang si Gareth Jones, 25 taong gulang mula sa Wales, ay nahulog matapos niyang akyatin ang bakod sa North Head malapit sa Manly bandang 6:45 ng umaga nitong Linggo. Kasama niya ang kanyang mga kaibigan na naglakad sa gilid ng bangin upang panoorin ang pagsikat ng araw nang siya ay aksidenteng madulas. Bagamat hindi pa kinukumpirma ng NSW Police ang pagkakakilanlan ng lalaki, kinilala ng Nine News ang biktima bilang si Gareth Jones. Apat na saksi, na sinasabing mga kaibigan niya, ang iniimbestigahan ng mga otoridad. Dalawa sa mga kaibigan ay bumaba sa bangin gamit ang mga lubid at hagdan na karaniwang ginagamit ng mga mangingisda ngunit natagpuan nilang wala nang malay ang kanilang kaibigan. Narekober ng NSW Police Rescue Unit ang katawan ng lalaki na iniahon mula sa bangin bandang 11:30 ng umaga at isinailalim sa pangangalaga ng mga awtoridad. Ayon kay Inspector Belinda Caddy sa Nine News, 'Mukhang ito ay isang trahedya at nalulungkot kami para sa lahat ng naroon. Ang aming pag-aalala ay para sa kanyang pamilya kapag naipaalam namin ito sa kanila.' Sikat ang mga tuktok ng bangin sa North Head dahil sa mga tanawing makikita ng Sydney Harbour kaya't madalas itong pasyalan ng mga turista sa northern beaches. Ikinuwento ni Inspector Nigel Taylor sa Sydney Morning Herald na ang grupo ay nakaupo sa gilid ng bangin habang nanonood ng pagsikat ng araw nang mangyari ang trahedya. 'Pagbalik nila sa lookout, lumapit ang binata para makita nang mas malapitan at nahulog siya sa bangin,' sabi ni Inspector Taylor. Nagbabala ang mga pulis na huwag umakyat sa mga bakod o pumasok sa mga bawal na lugar dahil sa panganib ng malubhang pinsala o pagkamatay. Ang insidenteng ito ay kasunod ng ilan pang kaparehong aksidente sa rehiyon kamakailan lang. Nitong mga nakaraang buwan, isang babae ang nahulog at namatay sa Blue Mountains habang nagmemeditate malapit sa gilid ng bangin kasama ang mga kaibigan. Noong Nobyembre, namatay si Megan Moody, 38, matapos madulas sa 25-metrong bangin sa Tahmoor, southwestern Sydney, habang ang kanyang partner na si Paul Vietch ay saksi sa insidente. Sa parehong buwan, sa South Maroubra, dalawang mangingisda ang pinuna dahil nilagay nila sa panganib ang kanilang sarili habang nangingisda sa 20-metrong bangin.

article_content: By July 20, a historic agreement may be reached to resolve the standoff over Iran’s nuclear program. The United States will then have to decide whether to lift sanctions in exchange for substantial and irreversible nuclear concessions from Tehran. Any debate about this exchange must consider the true cost of the sanctions policy—a subject the U.S. government has yet to formally assess. According to an independent study using an econometric gravity model, the United States sacrificed between $134.7 billion and $175.3 billion in potential export revenue to Iran from 1995 to 2012, making it the greatest economic loser among sanctioning nations. The lost trade has also meant missed job opportunities—between 51,043 and 66,436 jobs per year on average, with as many as 214,657 to 279,389 job opportunities foregone in 2008 alone. States like Texas and California were especially impacted because of their prominent industries attractive to the Iranian economy, such as oil, gas, automobiles, green energy, and telecommunications. These figures are conservative, as they only account for direct losses in export revenue and do not include secondary economic effects like higher oil prices or Iran’s diminished ability to import goods due to lower GDP. Thus, the total cost to the U.S. economy is probably even higher. America is not alone in these losses. Between 2010 and 2012, sanctions cost EU countries more than twice as much in lost trade as they did the U.S., with Germany, Italy, and France suffering the greatest losses. It is common for economic costs to become secondary to security considerations in national policy decisions. However, as American and Iranian negotiators—along with EU, Russian, and Chinese partners—work towards a nuclear deal in Vienna, the core issue is whether sanctions should be traded for measures that block Iran’s nuclear weapons pathways. As former IAEA chief Mohamed ElBaradei said, 'You can bomb their facilities, but you cannot bomb their knowledge.' Opponents of a nuclear deal claim tougher sanctions are more effective at halting Tehran’s nuclear progress, and fear sanctions relief could allow Iran to restart its program later. Yet, President Barack Obama has argued that the belief Iran would simply yield to economic pressure does not reflect an honest understanding of the country. Moreover, persisting with sanctions despite a reasonable deal may fracture the international coalition. European lawmakers have made it clear to U.S. Congress that they will not maintain sanctions if an agreement is reached, even if Congress objects. In that case, it would be Congress, not Europe, risking the transatlantic alliance. As negotiations approach their climax, some in Washington will question whether the deal is worth lifting sanctions. But Americans should also weigh whether bearing the economic costs of sanctions still makes sense if alternative paths exist.

article_content: Junk fees—extra charges added to purchases such as concert tickets, hotel bookings, and rentals—are a growing concern for consumers. The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has proposed a new rule that would require businesses like ticket sellers and hotels to display all fees upfront, preventing customers from being surprised at checkout. The FTC argues that hidden fees cost Americans tens of billions of dollars each year in various services, including renting apartments, paying for utilities, and buying event tickets. Although the proposed rule doesn’t ban junk fees entirely, it aims for transparency by forcing companies to clearly list all costs in advance. This could also encourage businesses to compete for lower prices. The FTC is currently seeking public feedback on this proposal. FTC Chair Lina M. Khan said, 'Americans are often plagued with unexpected and unnecessary fees they can’t escape. These junk fees now cost Americans tens of billions of dollars a year—money that companies are taking from working families simply because they can. By hiding the total price, these junk fees make it harder for consumers to shop for the best option and hurt honest businesses. The FTC’s proposed rule to address junk fees will save people money and time, making our markets fairer and more competitive.' The frustration over junk fees became especially prominent after Ticketmaster crashed during the presale for Taylor Swift’s Eras Tour last fall. Fans were not only upset with outages but also with the high ticket prices, a large portion of which were attributed to excess fees. During a Senate hearing, Joe Berchtold, President and CFO of Live Nation Entertainment, stated that his company has worked to improve artist-fan relations since its 2010 merger with Ticketmaster. He claimed that Ticketmaster does not set prices, control ticket quantities, or decide service fees, and blamed the Eras Tour technical failures on automated bots. In June, President Joe Biden hosted executives from companies like Live Nation Ticketmaster, Airbnb, SeatGeek, and others at the White House to discuss ticketing fees. Following this meeting, companies such as Live Nation Ticketmaster introduced all-in pricing, which shows the complete ticket cost before checkout. SeatGeek and Airbnb have also rolled out similar pricing tools to enhance price transparency. While several companies have voluntarily moved toward more transparent pricing, the FTC’s proposed rule would require all businesses to follow suit.
translated_content: Ang mga junk fee—mga dagdag na singil sa pagbili ng concert tickets, pag-book ng hotel, at renta—ay tumataas ang bilang at nakakabahala na para sa mga konsyumer. Nagpanukala ang Federal Trade Commission (FTC) ng bagong patakaran na mag-oobliga sa mga negosyo tulad ng ticket sellers at mga hotel na ilahad kaagad ang lahat ng bayarin, upang hindi mabigla ang mga customer sa total na halaga pag-checkout. Ayon sa FTC, ang mga nakatagong fee ay nagkakahalaga ng sampu-sampung bilyong dolyar na nalulugi sa mga Amerikano bawat taon sa iba't ibang serbisyo, kasama na ang paupahan, utilities, at pagbili ng event tickets. Bagaman hindi ipinagbabawal ng panukalang ito ang junk fee, layunin nitong maging mas malinaw ang presyohan sa pamamagitan ng paglalathala ng lahat ng singil bago pa man ang pagbili. Maaaring magdulot din ito ng kumpetisyon sa mga negosyo para mapababa ang presyo. Sa ngayon, humihingi ang FTC ng feedback mula sa publiko ukol sa panukalang ito. Sabi ni FTC Chair Lina M. Khan, 'Madalas ay napapabigatan ang mga Amerikano ng mga hindi inaasahan at di kailangang bayarin na hindi nila kayang takasan. Ang mga junk fee na ito ay nagkakahalaga na ng sampu-sampung bilyong dolyar bawat taon—perang kinukuha ng mga kumpanya mula sa mga pamilyang Amerikano dahil kaya nila. Sa pagtatago ng totoong presyo, pinapahirapan ng mga junk fee ang mga tao na mamili ng tamang serbisyo at pinapahirapan din ang mga negosyo na tapat magbigay ng presyo. Ang panukala ng FTC para tugunan ito ay makakatipid ng pera at oras ng tao, at magpapalawak ng patas na kompetisyon sa merkado.' Lumala ang inis ng mga tao sa junk fees nang bumagsak ang Ticketmaster sa presale ng Taylor Swift’s Eras Tour noong isang taon. Bukod sa problema sa sistema, maraming fans ang nadismaya sa taas ng presyo ng ticket na halos binubuo ng dagdag na bayarin. Sa isang pagdinig sa Senado, sinabi ni Joe Berchtold, Pangulo at CFO ng Live Nation Entertainment, na itinataguyod ng kanilang kumpanya ang artist-fan relations mula nang nagsanib ang Live Nation at Ticketmaster noong 2010. Sinabi rin niyang ang Ticketmaster ay walang kontrol sa presyo, bilang ng ticket, o singil sa serbisyo, at sinisi ang bots sa naging aberya ng Eras Tour. Noong Hunyo, inimbitahan ni President Joe Biden ang mga executive mula sa Live Nation Ticketmaster, Airbnb, SeatGeek, at iba pa sa White House para pag-usapan ang ticketing fees. Matapos ang pagpupulong, naglunsad ang Live Nation Ticketmaster ng all-in pricing kung saan makikita na agad ang kabuuang presyo bago bumili. Nagpakilala rin ng katulad na sistema ang SeatGeek at Airbnb para gawing mas klaro ang gastusin. Habang may mga kumpanyang nagsimula nang ipatupad ang mas malinaw na presyohan, ang mungkahi ng FTC ay mag-oobliga sa lahat ng negosyo na sundin ito.

article_content: Stray Kids have landed at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 again with their latest album, 'Rock-Star.' The K-pop group's newest release racked up 224,000 equivalent album units in its debut week, with about 213,000 of those coming from pure album sales—a sign of the group's enthusiastic fanbase, many of whom grabbed physical CDs. In addition, the album's tracks were streamed 15.68 million times during the tracking week. This marks the fourth time Stray Kids have reached the top of the Billboard 200, making them the South Korean act with the second-most No. 1 albums on the chart, just behind BTS. Before 'Rock-Star,' Stray Kids secured chart-toppers with their releases 'Oddinary' in April 2022, 'Maxident' in October 2022, and '5-Star' in June 2023. Stray Kids unseated Taylor Swift, whose '1989 (Taylor’s Version)' spent the previous two weeks at No. 1, further highlighting their rising global presence.

Umabot sa 224,000 equivalent album units ang nabenta sa unang linggo ng release, at 213,000 dito ay pure album sales—patunay ng suporta ng kanilang fans, karamihan ay bumili ng CD. Umabot din sa 15.68 milyon ang streams ng mga kanta ng album sa loob ng tracking week. Ika-apat na beses na ito na naging No. 1 ang Stray Kids sa Billboard 200, dahilan para sila ang second-most na South Korean act na may No. 1 albums sa chart, sunod sa BTS. Bago ang 'Rock-Star,' naging chart-toppers din ang 'Oddinary' (April 2022), 'Maxident' (October 2022), at '5-Star' (June 2023) ng grupo. Pinatalsik ng Stray Kids si Taylor Swift na may hawak ng No. 1 spot sa nakaraang dalawang linggo gamit ang '1989 (Taylor’s Version),' na lalong nagpatibay sa global na kasikatan ng grupo.

article_content: Al Jazeera has verified that the family of Wael Al-Dahdouh, its Gaza bureau chief, were killed in an Israeli airstrike in central Gaza. The strike occurred at the Nuseirat refugee camp, claiming the lives of Al-Dahdouh’s wife, teenage son, young daughter, and subsequently his grandson. The family had sought shelter in the camp after moving from northern Gaza, following Israeli directives for residents to head south due to continued military activity. Mahmoud, Al-Dahdouh's son, was in his final year of high school. His daughter, Sham, was seven, and his grandson Adam was 18 months old. Some relatives remain missing under the rubble, though others have survived. Al Jazeera condemned the attack as indiscriminate in a public statement. The Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) acknowledged carrying out an operation against Hamas in the area where the family was killed. Addressing concerns over civilian deaths, IDF spokesperson Lt Col Peter Lerner called any loss of life tragic. Videos shared online depict Al-Dahdouh grieving in hospital, mourning his daughter and son. In an interview, he said, 'There is no safe place in Gaza at all.' The network raised concerns about its staff’s safety in Gaza, holding Israeli authorities responsible and urging international intervention to protect civilians. So far, at least 24 journalists have died since the conflict escalated, according to the Committee to Protect Journalists. The intensified attacks come after the 7 October Hamas assault on Israel, where over 1,400 were killed and more than 200 taken hostage. According to the Hamas-run health ministry, around 7,000 people have died in Gaza. The area continues to suffer from shortages of fuel, electricity, and water, with only limited aid entering through Egypt.

Sila ay lumikas mula hilagang Gaza papunta sa kampo dahil sa utos ng Israel sa mga residente na pumunta sa timog habang nagpapatuloy ang mga labanan. Si Mahmoud, anak ni Al-Dahdouh, ay nasa huling taon ng high school; pitong taong gulang si Sham, at labingwalo na buwang gulang si Adam, ang apo. May ilan pa silang kamag-anak na di pa natatagpuan sa guho, pero may ilang nakaligtas. Mariing kinondena ng Al Jazeera ang pag-atake at tinawag itong walang pinipiling target. Kumpirmado ng Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) na nagsagawa sila ng operasyon laban sa Hamas sa lugar. Sa tanong tungkol sa mga sibilyan na namatay, sinabi ni IDF spokesperson Lt Col Peter Lerner na trahedya ang mawalan ng kahit anong buhay. Nagpahayag ang network ng labis na pag-aalala para sa kaligtasan ng kanilang mga empleyado, itinuturing na responsibilidad ito ng Israeli authorities at nananawagan sa pandaigdigang komunidad na protektahan ang mga sibilyan. Di bababa sa 24 na mamamahayag na ang nasawi, ayon sa Committee to Protect Journalists. Lalong sumiklab ang gulo matapos ang pag-atake ng Hamas sa Israel noong Oktubre 7, na nagdulot ng higit 1,400 nasawi at mahigit 200 bihag. Tinatayang nasa 7,000 ang namamatay sa Gaza ayon sa Hamas-run health ministry. Nagpapatuloy ang kakulangan sa kuryente, tubig, at gasolina, at kakaunti pa lang ang naipapasok na tulong mula Egypt.

article_content:
While Nazi war criminals were being tried at Nuremberg after World War II, the U.S. government recruited other former Nazis as spies and informants during the Cold War. According to recently disclosed government documents and interviews reported by The New York Times, at least 1,000 ex-Nazis were hired by the U.S. military, FBI, and CIA. Some of these individuals were suspected of war crimes, yet American agencies helped them immigrate to the U.S. and concealed their pasts to protect them from prosecution by the Justice Department’s Nazi hunters. Historians tasked with declassifying war-crime records consider this estimate conservative.

U.S. agencies directly or indirectly hired numerous ex-Nazi police officials and collaborators, including some overtly guilty of war crimes, according to University of Florida historian Norman Goda. Information about their compromised backgrounds was available at the time. Documents show recruits came from all levels of the Nazi regime, ranging from SS officers to high-level advisors connected to Holocaust architects.

During the 1950s, at the height of the Cold War, FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover and CIA Chief Allen Dulles agreed that these former Nazis would be more useful as Soviet spies than as prisoners. In Maryland, Army officials trained Nazi officers for a possible invasion of Russia; in Connecticut, a former Nazi guard was hired to study Soviet-bloc postage stamps for hidden messages; in Virginia, a former Hitler advisor briefed U.S. officials on the Soviets while ex-SS officers in East Germany conducted surveillance operations.

However, many of these former Nazis ultimately proved to be ineffective spies, and some acted as double agents. Notable cases include Aleksandras Lileikis, implicated in the murder of 60,000 Jews in the Vilna ghetto. The CIA knew of Lileikis’ connection to atrocities in Vilna, Lithuania, but still hired him as a spy in East Germany in 1952, paying him $1,700 a year and later helping him immigrate to the U.S. He lived there for forty years until prosecutors discovered him in 1994. Ultimately, the CIA and Justice Department reached an agreement allowing for his deportation rather than a public trial.

Another senior Nazi turned American spy was Otto von Bolschwing, a mentor to Adolf Eichmann and an architect of policies targeting Jews. Despite his background, the CIA employed Bolschwing in Europe and later relocated his family to New York in 1954 as a reward for his postwar cooperation. Fearing exposure after Eichmann’s capture in Argentina in 1960, Bolschwing was reassured by the CIA and continued to live in the U.S. until Nazi hunters discovered him, leading to his citizenship being revoked in 1981; he died soon after. His son, Gus von Bolschwing, has openly criticized his father’s postwar intelligence work, calling it inconsistent with American values.

None of these ex-Nazi spies are known to be alive today.

Habang nililitis ang mga kriminal ng digmaan ng Nazi sa Nuremberg matapos ang Ikalawang Digmaang Pandaigdig, nag-recruit naman ang gobyerno ng U.S. ng mga dating Nazi bilang mga espiya at impormante noong Cold War. Ayon sa mga bagong inilabas na dokumentong pamahalaan at panayam na iniulat ng The New York Times, hindi bababa sa 1,000 dating Nazi ang kinuha ng militar ng U.S., FBI, at CIA. Ilan sa kanila ay pinaghihinalaang gumawa ng war crimes, ngunit tinulungan silang makalipat sa U.S. at itinago ang kanilang nakaraan para hindi masampahan ng kaso ng Justice Department Nazi hunters. Ayon sa mga historyador ng war-crime records, maaaring mas mataas pa sa 1,000 ang totoo.

Direkta o di-direktang kumuha ang mga ahensya ng U.S. ng dating Nazi police at collaborators, kabilang ang mga hayag na may sala, ayon kay Norman Goda ng University of Florida. Alam na raw ng mga ahensya noon ang kala-kalang pagkatao ng ilan sa kanila. Nagmula sa iba’t ibang antas ng Nazi regime ang mga na-recruit, mula SS officers hanggang matataas na tagapayo na may koneksyon sa mga utak ng Holocaust.

Noong 1950s sa kasagsagan ng Cold War, isang ideya nina FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover at CIA Chief Allen Dulles na mas pakikinabangan ang mga dating Nazi bilang espiya laban sa Soviet kaysa bilang bilanggo. Sa Maryland, sinanay ng Army ang mga Nazi officers para sa posibleng pagsakop sa Russia; sa Connecticut, isang dating Nazi guard ang kinuhang mag-aral ng selyo mula Soviet bloc; sa Virginia, isang dating tagapayo ni Hitler ang nagbibigay ng classified briefing ukol sa mga Soviet habang dating SS officers sa East Germany ay nagsagawa ng surveillance.

Marami sa mga dating Nazi ay napatunayang hindi epektibo at ilan ay naging double agent pa. Kabilang dito si Aleksandras Lileikis, na sangkot sa pagpatay ng 60,000 Hudyo sa Vilna ghetto—alam ito ng CIA pero kinuha pa ring espiya noong 1952. Binayaran siya ng $1,700 kada taon at tinulungan pa siyang makarating sa U.S., kung saan siya tumira ng apatnapung taon bago nabisto noong 1994. Sa huli, napagkasunduan ng CIA at Justice Dept. na ipa-deport na lamang siya imbis litisin.

Isa pang senior Nazi na naging American spy ay si Otto von Bolschwing, mentor ni Adolf Eichmann at utak ng mga polisiya laban sa mga Hudyo. Pinapasok siya ng CIA sa Europa at inilipat ang pamilya niya sa New York bilang pabuya. Nang mahuli si Eichmann, natakot si Bolschwing na mabunyag at tinulungan siya ng CIA; namuhay siya sa U.S. hanggang kilalanin siya ng Nazi hunters at mawalan ng citizenship noong 1981. Ayon sa anak niyang si Gus von Bolschwing, hindi ito dapat nangyari, at labag ito sa values ng Amerika.

Wala nang nabubuhay na mga ex-Nazi spy na in-hire ng mga U.S. agency.

article_content: Managers at a Domino's Pizza branch in Preston, Lancashire, posted a sign instructing staff to speak only English while at work. The notice warned that failure to follow this rule could lead to disciplinary action. The policy aimed to improve communication, support workplace safety, and respond to complaints from other locations. Employees, many of whom are from Poland, Hungary, and Asian countries, criticized the policy as discriminatory. Stuart Horton, a delivery driver who had worked at Domino's for five years, resigned in protest, stating that the notice created fear among staff. Horton, 47, explained that most of the 15 employees at the branch do not speak English as their first language but communicate with customers in English. Area manager David Woods has reportedly agreed to meet staff to discuss their concerns. Domino’s Pizza Group PLC said that using a common language is important for communication and safety in stores but admitted the tone of the notice was too strong and would be addressed with the franchise owner. The Preston West branch, operated by franchisee Topwest Limited, is one of several Domino’s Pizza locations in Lancashire. The notice was posted in the staff room at the Tulketh Mill store.

Kinondena ng mga empleyado, karamihan ay mula sa Poland, Hungary, at mga bansa sa Asya, ang patakaran bilang diskriminasyon. Nakapaskil ang kontrobersyal na abiso sa staff room ng Tulketh Mill store.

article_content: SINGAPORE: The ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict could impact the unity and relevance of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), as its members have expressed differing views on the crisis, according to experts. This follows a recent attack by the Palestinian militant group Hamas on Israel, which has escalated into a deadly conflict with no clear resolution in sight. While ASEAN members have released individual statements about the situation, the regional bloc has yet to issue a unified response.

article_content: The Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) and Nigeria Liquefied Natural Gas (NLNG) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to work together on sustainable development projects in the Niger Delta region. At a signing ceremony at NLNG’s Corporate Head Office, NLNG’s Managing Director and CEO, Dr. Philip Mshelbila, and NDDC’s Managing Director, Dr. Samuel Ogbuku, formalised the agreement with executives from both organisations present. A statement issued in Port Harcourt on Tuesday, signed by NDDC Director of Corporate Affairs, Pius Ughakpoteni, outlined that both organisations will collaborate to empower local communities, promote local content and capacity building, and engage stakeholders along the value chain for effective delivery of development projects. Dr. Mshelbila noted that the partnership is designed to set an example for productive collaborations in the Niger Delta. He said NLNG hopes to expand its successful community initiatives region-wide, maximising the positive impact by working with NDDC. He added that this aligns with NLNG’s vision of ‘helping to build a better Nigeria’ and highlighted the company's unwavering commitment to sustainable development through partnerships, innovation, and meaningful community impact. Dr. Mshelbila emphasised NLNG’s dedication to supporting host communities in health, education, economic and infrastructure development, stating that community well-being is vital to NLNG’s success. Promoting social inclusion and economic growth is considered an ethical responsibility. He also reaffirmed the importance of maintaining high standards for project execution and accountability and plans to share knowledge and build capacity with NDDC to help achieve these development objectives. Dr. Ogbuku, Managing Director of NDDC, said the MoU represents a new era of cooperation, highlighting unity in sustainable development efforts and progress for Nigeria. He explained that while NLNG and NDDC have different mandates, their mutual goals include socio-economic empowerment, local content promotion, capacity development, and stakeholder collaboration. He described the alliance as a significant step in Nigeria’s quest for progress and noted its importance for addressing challenges in the Niger Delta. Dr. Ogbuku praised NLNG’s global standing and environmental responsibility, and reiterated NDDC’s focus on balanced economic growth, environmental care, and well-being of local communities. He concluded that NDDC is committed to uplifting the Niger Delta via programs to improve livelihoods, education, healthcare, and economic conditions, prioritising local community empowerment and creating strong partnerships with government, civil society, and the private sector.
translated_content: Ang Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) at Nigeria Liquefied Natural Gas (NLNG) ay lumagda ng Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) upang magsanib-puwersa sa mga proyektong pangkaunlaran sa rehiyong Niger Delta. Sa isang seremonya ng paglagda na ginanap sa Corporate Head Office ng NLNG, pormal na nilagdaan nina Dr. Philip Mshelbila, Managing Director at CEO ng NLNG, at Dr. Samuel Ogbuku, Managing Director ng NDDC, ang kasunduan sa harapan ng mga opisyal mula sa parehong organisasyon. Ayon sa pahayag na inilabas sa Port Harcourt at nilagdaan ni Pius Ughakpoteni, Director of Corporate Affairs ng NDDC, magtutulungan ang dalawang panig upang palakasin ang mga lokal na komunidad, itaguyod ang local content at capacity building, at makipag-ugnayan sa mga stakeholder para sa epektibong pagpapatupad ng mga proyekto. Binanggit ni Dr. Mshelbila na layunin ng partnership na ito na magsilbing modelo sa kung paanong ang ganitong kolaborasyon ay makakatulong sa pag-unlad ng Niger Delta. Target ng NLNG na palawakin ang tagumpay ng kanilang mga programa sa buong rehiyon katuwang ang NDDC para sa mas malawak na benepisyo. Ayon pa sa kanya, ito ay kaakibat ng pananaw ng NLNG na ‘makatulong bumuo ng mas magandang Nigeria’ at binigyang-diin ang kanilang tuloy-tuloy na commitment sa sustainable development sa pamamagitan ng pakikipag-partner, inobasyon, at tunay na malasakit sa komunidad. Ipinahayag ni Dr. Mshelbila ang dedikasyon ng NLNG sa pagtulong sa host communities pagdating sa kalusugan, edukasyon, kaunlarang pang-ekonomiya, at imprastruktura, at iginiit na mahalaga ang kapakanan ng lokal na komunidad sa tagumpay ng NLNG. Itinuturing nilang tungkulin ang pagtataguyod ng social inclusion at paglago ng ekonomiya. Nilinaw din niya ang kahalagahan ng mataas na pamantayan sa pagpapatupad ng proyekto at accountability, at ang plano nilang magbahagi ng kaalaman at palakasin ang kakayahan ng NDDC upang makamit ang mga layunin sa kaunlaran. Sinabi naman ni Dr. Ogbuku, Managing Director ng NDDC, na ang MoU ay nagbubukas ng bagong yugto ng kooperasyon na sumisimbolo ng pagkakaisa para sa sustainable development at pag-unlad ng bansa. Paliwanag niya, kahit magkaiba ng mandato ang NLNG at NDDC, magkatulad ang kanilang layunin: socio-economic empowerment, local content, capacity development, at kolaborasyon kasama ang mga stakeholders. Tinukoy niya ang partnership bilang mahalagang hakbang sa pagsulong ng Nigeria at mahalaga sa pagtugon ng mga hamon sa Niger Delta. Pinuri niya ang reputasyon ng NLNG sa global at ang pagiging responsable sa kalikasan, at nilinaw ang pokus ng NDDC sa balanseng pag-unlad, malasakit sa kalikasan, at kapakanan ng lokal na komunidad. Sa huli, tiniyak ni Dr. Ogbuku ang dedikasyon ng NDDC sa pag-angat ng Niger Delta sa pamamagitan ng mga programa sa kabuhayan, edukasyon, kalusugan, at pang-ekonomiyang pag-unlad, at binigyang-priyoridad ang pagpapalakas ng lokal na komunidad at malalakas na partnership kasama ang gobyerno, civil society, at pribadong sektor.

Marianne Butler, a commercial lawyer, was diagnosed with grade III breast cancer just one month after being named runner-up to Amal Alamuddin (George Clooney's fiancé) in a poll of London's most attractive lawyers. The 35-year-old told the Evening Standard that she has undergone rounds of chemotherapy and pioneering drug therapy at the Royal Marsden hospital. Joking about her situation, she remarked, 'Number one got George Clooney, number two got breast cancer.'

Following her diagnosis, doctors found a 6cm tumour that had spread to her lymph nodes. Despite having no family history of the disease, she started chemotherapy just four days later. Butler received pertuzumab and Herceptin—a combination previously only trialed in the U.S.—which worked to prevent the cancer from spreading during her treatment. Professor Ian Smith led her care, and Butler became one of the first patients in the UK to receive this combination for a primary breast cancer diagnosis.

The treatment succeeded, allowing her to return to work at Fountain Court Chambers. According to her husband Tony, the key innovation was using pertuzumab immediately, following recent U.S. approval for early-stage use. Professor Smith secured permission for Butler’s treatment and persuaded their insurance company to cover it.

She continues using both drugs to try to prevent recurrence and is monitored for side effects. Two other drugs used in her treatment were developed by Professor Smith and his team. Further, they are trialing a new monoclonal antibody therapy meant to target only cancer cells, aiming to lessen chemotherapy’s side effects.

To support ongoing research, Butler’s husband Tony, brother Julian, Professor Smith, and 30 friends are taking part in Le Cure De France, a charity cycling event running from September 10 to 14, with a goal of raising £100,000 for cancer research at the Marsden. Butler, who lives in Barnes, commented, 'I have been very lucky. Now it’s about supporting the Marsden and other women.' Donations can be made via @LeCureDeFrance on Twitter.

Ngayon, tungkol na ito sa suporta para sa Marsden at sa iba pang kababaihan.' Maaari kang mag-donate sa @LeCureDeFrance sa Twitter.

article_content: On a chilly December evening in Hong Kong, a small group of committed runners gathers on the track—including a remarkable group known as the Fearless Dragons. Dressed in black, they run in unison, distinguishing themselves as a team of blind and deaf runners cooperating with guide runners for support. Launched four years ago, the Fearless Dragons have nearly 60 members and have already competed in marathons across Asia and Australia, from Kyoto and Shanghai to Seoul, Taipei, and their home city. The team's main mission is to raise public awareness about people with disabilities and empower them to reach their full potential, says founder Kim Mok. Mok, who became blind at age 13, was inspired to take action after the tragic loss of a close, blind friend to suicide driven by social isolation and discrimination. In the 1980s and early 1990s, people with disabilities in Hong Kong had very limited government support—they couldn’t pursue education beyond a certain level unless they were exceptional, and equality bodies like the Equal Opportunities Commission didn’t exist. Things started to change when Hong Kong signed the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, leading to more programs focused on accessibility and inclusion. Nevertheless, a major concern persists: there is minimal support for the children of disabled parents even if the children themselves do not have disabilities. Mok notes that this gap can trap families in cycles of poverty. The Fearless Dragons are part of Mok's larger project, the Hong Kong Network for the Promotion of Inclusive Society. This group operates an educational fund that helps these children through counseling and home tutoring, financed by funds the team raises through running events.
translated_content: Sa isang malamig na Disyembre ng gabi sa Hong Kong, kakaunti lang ang masisigasig na tumatakbo sa track—kasama na ang Fearless Dragons, isang natatanging grupo na naka-itim na uniporme at sabay-sabay na tumatakbo. Sila ay binubuo ng mga bulag at binging runner na tinutulungan ng mga guide runner. Itinatag apat na taon na ang nakalilipas, halos 60 na ang miyembro ng Fearless Dragons at nakasali na sila sa iba't ibang marathons sa Asia at Australia tulad ng Kyoto, Shanghai, Seoul, Taipei, at siyempre sa Hong Kong. Ang pangunahing layunin ng grupo ay itaas ang kamalayan sa mga taong may kapansanan at bigyang-lakas silang magtagumpay, ayon kay Kim Mok, ang nagtatag. Nabulag si Mok noong siya ay 13 taong gulang at napukaw siyang tumulong matapos ang malungkot na pagpanaw ng isang malapit niyang kaibigan bunga ng diskriminasyon at pag-iisa. Noong dekada 80 at unang bahagi ng 90, kulang na kulang ang tulong mula sa gobyerno para sa mga may kapansanan sa Hong Kong—hindi sila makapagpatuloy sa mataas na edukasyon maliban kung sila ay mahusay, at wala pang Equal Opportunities Commission noon. Nagbago ang sitwasyon nang lumagda ang Hong Kong sa UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, na nagbukas ng mas maraming programa para sa accessibility at inclusivity. Pero nananatili ang isang malaking hamon: kakaunti pa rin ang suporta para sa mga anak ng may kapansanan—kahit na wala silang kapansanan. Ayon kay Mok, maaaring magdulot ito ng siklo ng kahirapan sa kanilang pamilya. Bahagi ang Fearless Dragons ng mas malaking proyekto ni Mok—ang Hong Kong Network for the Promotion of Inclusive Society. Pinapamahalaan nila ang isang education fund para tumulong sa mga batang ito sa counseling at home tutoring gamit ang pondong nalilikom mula sa mga karerang sinalihan ng koponan.

article_content: Former UK defence minister Gerald Howarth has called for a pause in merger discussions between BAE Systems and European aerospace company EADS to allow Parliament time to determine whether the deal aligns with Britain’s national interests. Howarth, who recently served as minister for security strategy, emphasized that the government should prevent France and Germany from gaining significant influence over the country’s largest defence firm. The proposed £30 billion merger would enable BAE to expand further into the European defence and civil aviation markets. However, some lawmakers worry that the agreement could see France and Germany each controlling at least a 9% stake in the new entity, granting their governments sway over vital UK defence jobs and facilities. Howarth acknowledged that broadening BAE's commercial activities could offer advantages, but insisted Parliament should have the authority to challenge any deal allowing foreign governments to determine the fate of British defence operations. A joint update from BAE and EADS is anticipated for release to the stock market on October 10. Howarth argued, 'There must be more time. It’s unacceptable for the government to decide alone when so many jobs are at stake.' He also suggested that Parliament is unlikely to approve a merger granting significant ownership to the French and German governments, saying, 'It would be politically impossible for these governments to hold such a large portion of our main defence contractor and have a say in critical investment decisions.' Negotiations continue between the UK government, French and German officials, and the two companies to limit foreign ownership in the merged business. Sources report unease in Downing Street over proposals that would allow the French and German governments to acquire even greater stakes in the future. Addressing concerns, EADS CEO Tom Enders has insisted the potential merger is not about cutting thousands of jobs, seeking to reassure lawmakers and critics.
translated_content: Nanawagan si dating UK defence minister Gerald Howarth na ipagpaliban muna ang negosasyon tungkol sa pagsasanib ng BAE Systems at European aerospace company na EADS upang bigyan ng oras ang Parliament na pag-aralan kung makakabuti ito sa pambansang interes ng Britain. Binanggit ni Howarth, na kamakailan lang nagsilbing minister for security strategy, na dapat pigilan ng gobyerno ang France at Germany na magkaroon ng malaking impluwensya sa pinakamalaking defence firm ng bansa. Ang mungkahing pagsasanib na nagkakahalaga ng £30 bilyon ay magpapalawak sa operasyon ng BAE sa European defence at civil aviation markets. Subalit nangangamba ang ilang mambabatas na maaaring magresulta ito sa pagkakaroon ng hindi bababa sa 9% na bahagi ng shares ng parehong France at Germany sa bagong kumpanya, na magbibigay sa kanilang gobyerno ng kapangyarihang makialam sa mahahalagang trabaho at pasilidad ng UK defence. Aminado si Howarth na may mga benepisyong pangkomersyo kapag pinalawak ng BAE ang kanilang mga gawain, ngunit iginiit niyang dapat may kapangyarihan ang Parliament na tutulan ang anumang kasunduan na magbibigay-daan sa mga banyagang gobyerno na magpasya ukol sa kinabukasan ng defense operations ng Britain. Inaasahang maglalabas ng pinagsamang pahayag ang BAE at EADS sa stock market ngayong Oktubre 10. Ayon kay Howarth, 'Kailangang dagdagan ang oras. Hindi katanggap-tanggap na ang gobyerno lang ang magpapasya lalo’t napakaraming trabaho ang maaapektuhan.' Sinabi pa niya na malabong pumayag ang Parliament sa merger na magbibigay ng malaking pag-aari sa French at German governments, aniya, 'Politically, imposibleng pahintulutan na ang mga gobyernong ito ay magmay-ari ng malaki sa ating pangunahing defence contractor at magpasya kung saan ilalaan ang pondo.' Nagpapatuloy ang negosasyon sa pagitan ng gobyerno ng UK, opisyal ng France at Germany, at dalawang kumpanya upang limitahan ang magiging pag-aari ng mga dayuhan sa pagsanib. Ayon sa ilang ulat, nababahala ang Downing Street sa mga panukalang maaaring magpahintulot pa sa France at Germany na dagdagan ang kanilang bahagi sa hinaharap. Bilang tugon sa mga pangamba, iginiit ni EADS CEO Tom Enders na ang panukalang pagsasanib ay hindi tungkol sa malawakang tanggalan sa trabaho upang pakalmahin ang mga mambabatas at kritiko.

article_content: Over recent years, nations such as Afghanistan, Pakistan, Somalia, Yemen, Syria, and Iraq have shown that confronting organizations like al Qaeda and its successors requires more than standard battlefield victories. When dealing with deeply rooted extremist ideologies, traditional concepts of winning often fall short. Realistically, containment has often been more attainable than total defeat. Though operations in Indonesia have crippled Jemaah Islamiya, and African troops have pushed Al-Shabaab back in Somalia, these successes haven’t erased the underlying beliefs or stopped the flow of new recruits to jihadist causes. The staying power of this brand of extremism suggests it’s unlikely to be wiped out any time soon. For instance, Jemaah Islamiya remains a dormant but significant risk in Indonesia, and while Al-Shabaab lost ground and leaders in Somalia, the threat persists. French campaigns in Mali, though effective, haven’t eradicated al Qaedism from the region. Still, some argue for all-out victory in places like Syria and Iraq, seemingly ignoring the resilience of these movements. Both public hopes and official rhetoric would benefit from greater realism. When leaders promise to defeat ISIS, it’s important to clarify what that means. Without clear benchmarks, military involvement can become open-ended. The prospect of eliminating Salafi jihadism quickly is unrealistic, especially amidst the instability and ungoverned spaces left by recent conflicts and the Arab Spring. A more practical aim is to shrink ISIS’s territory, cut off its recruitment pipelines, and encourage local communities to resist. Shia fighters on Baghdad’s outskirts, Kurdish Peshmerga, and other regional groups are already reclaiming ground from ISIS. Weakening ISIS also requires targeting its top figures—beyond just Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, to advisers and field commanders. While many foreign fighters may fall in battle, some may attempt attacks elsewhere, as past incidents in Indonesia, Pakistan, and Yemen have shown. Focused airstrikes in Syria can reduce those risks at home. Trying to eliminate the entire ISIS hierarchy isn't needed. The U.S. experience in Waziristan, where targeted operations—not mass troop deployments—sidelined al Qaeda leaders over time, underlines the value of patience and good intelligence. Ultimately, a steady campaign that disrupts ISIS’s leadership will force them to prioritize survival over attack planning. Defining clear, realistic goals—like minimizing ISIS’s ability to harm U.S. interests while supporting Middle Eastern allies—offers a sound strategy. This doesn’t return America to a major war and supports those threatened by ISIS. Over time, ISIS can be defeated, but degrading its power is a sensible goal for now.
translated_content: Sa mga nakalipas na taon, ipinakita ng mga bansa gaya ng Afghanistan, Pakistan, Somalia, Yemen, Syria, at Iraq na ang paglaban sa mga grupo tulad ng al Qaeda at mga sumunod dito ay nangangailangan ng higit pa sa karaniwang tagumpay sa labanan. Kapag humaharap sa malalim na nakaugat na ekstremistang ideolohiya, madalas na hindi sapat ang tradisyunal na konsepto ng tagumpay. Ang containment ay kadalasang mas posible kaysa sa ganap na tagumpay. Bagaman pinahina ng mga operasyon sa Indonesia ang Jemaah Islamiya at napaatras ng mga tropa mula Africa ang Al-Shabaab sa Somalia, hindi pa rin naalis ang pinaniniwalaan o ang tuloy-tuloy na pag-recruit para sa jihadist na mga grupo. Malaon nang matibay ang ganitong klase ng ekstremismo, kaya't mahirap itong tuluyang mawala. Halimbawa, nananatiling isang tahimik ngunit mapanganib na banta ang Jemaah Islamiya sa Indonesia, at kahit nawala na ng teritoryo at namatay ang mga lider ng Al-Shabaab sa Somalia, hindi pa rin wala ang panganib. Sa Mali, malaki ang naging tulong ng French campaigns pero hindi pa rin tuluyang nawala ang al Qaedism sa lugar. Gayunpaman, may ilan pa ring naniniwala sa ganap na tagumpay sa Syria at Iraq, na waring hindi binibigyan ng halaga ang tatag ng mga kilusang ito. Makabubuti sa publiko at mga opisyal ang may mas makatotohanang pananaw. Kapag sinasabi ng mga lider na tatalunin ang ISIS, mahalagang malinaw kung ano talaga ang ibig sabihin nito. Kung walang malinaw na pamantayan, maaaring lumawig ang military involvement nang walang katapusan. Hindi makatotohanan ang mabilis na pagwawakas ng Salafi jihadism, lalo na at pinalala ng digmaan at Arab Spring ang kaguluhan at kawalang-gobyerno. Mas makatotohanang layunin ang paliitin ang sakop ng ISIS, pigilan ang bago pang mga rekrut, at hikayatin ang lokal na komunidad na labanan sila. Sa mga lugar sa paligid ng Baghdad, mga Kurdish Peshmerga, at iba pang grupo sa rehiyon ay nakakabawi na ng teritoryo mula sa ISIS. Para humina ang ISIS, kailangang puntiryahin ang mga lider nito—hindi lang si Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi kundi pati na rin ang kaniyang mga adviser at commanders. Marami sa mga dayuhang mandirigma ang maaaring mamatay sa labanan, ngunit ang ilan ay puwedeng magplano pa rin ng pag-atake, gaya ng mga nakalipas na insidente sa Indonesia, Pakistan, at Yemen. Ang piling airstrikes sa Syria ay puwedeng bawasan ang banta sa sariling bansa. Hindi kailangang tanggalin lahat ng lider ng ISIS. Ipinakita ng karanasan ng U.S. sa Waziristan—na targeted operations kaysa malawakang deployment ng sundalo ang naging susi sa pagpahina sa al Qaeda—na mahalaga ang tiyaga at intelligence. Sa kabuuan, ang matiyagang kampanya na nagpapahina sa liderato ng ISIS ay magtutulak sa kanila na mag-focus na lamang sa sariling survival kaysa magplano ng panibagong atake. Ang pagtukoy ng malinaw at abot-kayang layunin—tulad ng pagbawas sa kakayahan ng ISIS na magbanta sa Amerika at pagtulong sa mga kaalyadong bansa—ang tamang direksyon. Hindi na kailangang bumalik sa malawakang digmaan, ngunit nagbibigay pa rin ng pag-asa para sa mga pinahihirapan ng ISIS. Maaaring talunin ang ISIS sa paglipas ng panahon, ngunit ang pagharang sa kanilang lakas ang praktikal na hakbang ngayon.

article_content: For more than 700 years, Old Sarum—an ancient site near Salisbury—has concealed secrets beneath its foundations. Recent geophysical surveys have produced a detailed underground map of the 11th-century medieval city, revealing a complex of houses and a courtyard believed to be part of a royal palace. The survey was carried out using advanced ground-penetrating scanners at the site of the Iron Age fort, just two miles (3.2 km) from modern Salisbury. Archaeologists from the University of Southampton led the survey, focusing on the site’s inner and outer baileys. Their findings show a series of large structures along the southern edge of the outer bailey’s defensive wall. This vast complex—measuring about 557 feet (170 meters) long and 213 feet (65 meters) wide—might have served as a palace or defensive stronghold. Old Sarum originated as an Iron Age hillfort around 400 BC (measuring 1,300 feet by 1,180 feet), later occupied by the Romans who renamed it Sorviodunum. After the Norman Conquest in 1066, William the Conqueror built a castle with a motte and additional inner fortifications. Early castle buildings would have been timber, but the oldest surviving stone structure—the keep—was built in the 12th century, possibly during Henry I’s reign. A new cathedral was constructed in the bailey’s north-western section in 1092. The site flourished for over 300 years, but declined in the 13th century as the nearby city of New Sarum (now Salisbury) rose to prominence. The survey employed multiple non-invasive techniques, including topographic surveys, magnetometry, earth resistance, ground-penetrating radar (GPR), and electric resistivity tomography (ERT). These images revealed thick walls up to 9 feet (3 meters) wide, a large hall approximately 196 feet (60 meters) long, towers, and evidence of multi-storey buildings. Open grounds behind these structures suggest resource delivery areas or processional routes. Residential areas were identified in the southeastern and southwestern quadrants of the outer bailey near the inner bailey ditch, along with signs of industrial activity, like kilns or furnaces, and quarrying after the 1300s. The presence of a large courtyard and these complexes implies the site may have served both residential and defensive functions. Old Sarum is managed by English Heritage and is open to the public. The research formed part of the Old Sarum and Stratford-Sub-Castle Archaeological Survey Project, led by Kristian Strutt, Timothy Sly, and Dominic Barker from Southampton. According to property curator Heather Sebire, the project’s non-invasive methods have enhanced understanding of historic landscapes, though further dating work is required. Kristian Strutt added that findings indicate the outer bailey was heavily developed in the Middle Ages, forming a significant urban hub. Both experts expect that ongoing studies will continue to shed light on Old Sarum’s layered past.
translated_content: Mahigit 700 taon nang nagtatago ng mga lihim ang Old Sarum—isang sinaunang lugar malapit sa Salisbury—sa ilalim ng lupain nito. Sa pamamagitan ng makabagong geophysical survey, nakagawa ng detalyadong mapa ng 11th-century medieval na lungsod, na nagbunyag ng mga bahay at isang courtyard na pinaniniwalaang bahagi ng isang royal na palasyo. Ginamit ang advanced na ground-penetrating scanners sa Iron Age fort na ito, humigit-kumulang dalawang milya (3.2 km) mula sa makabagong Salisbury. Pinangunahan ng mga arkeologo mula sa University of Southampton ang survey, na nakatuon sa inner at outer baileys ng lugar. Natuklasan nila ang serye ng malalaking estruktura sa timog na parte ng pader na panangga ng outer bailey. Ang lawak ng complex na ito—tinatayang 557 talampakan (170 metro) ang haba at 213 talampakan (65 metro) ang lapad—ay maaaring nagsilbing palasyo o estrukturang pangdepensa. Nagsimula ang Old Sarum bilang isang Iron Age hillfort noong humigit-kumulang 400 BC (na may sukat na 1,300 talampakan x 1,180 talampakan), at ginamit ito ng mga Romano na tinawag ito bilang Sorviodunum. Pagkatapos ng Norman Conquest noong 1066, nagtayo ng kastilyo si William the Conqueror na may motte at dagdag pang panloob na fortifications. Una, gawa sa kahoy ang mga gusali ng kastilyo, ngunit ang pinakamatandang bato na gusali—ang keep—ay itinayo noong ika-12 siglo, malamang sa panahon ni Henry I. Noong 1092, nagtayo ng bagong katedral sa hilaga-kanlurang bahagi ng bailey. Umusbong ang pook mahigit 300 taon, subalit nagsimulang humina pagsapit ng ika-13 siglo habang sumisikat ang New Sarum (ngayo’y Salisbury). Iba’t ibang non-invasive na teknolohiya ang ginamit, kabilang ang topographic survey, magnetometry, earth resistance, ground-penetrating radar (GPR), at electric resistivity tomography (ERT). Ipinakita ng mga resulta ang kapal ng pader na umaabot sa 9 talampakan (3 metro), isang malaking bulwagan na humigit-kumulang 196 talampakan (60 metro) ang haba, mga tore, at ebidensiya ng mga gusaling palapag-palapag. May mga bakanteng espasyo din sa likod ng mga ito na tila ginamit para sa paghahatid ng mga kailangan o daanan. Natukoy ang mga residential area sa timog-silangan at timog-kanlurang bahagi ng outer bailey, malapit sa kanal ng inner bailey, pati na rin ang mga palatandaan ng aktibidad pang-industriya, tulad ng mga hurno at pugon, at pagmimina matapos ang 1300s. Ang pagkakaroon ng malaking courtyard at mga complex ay nagpapahiwatig na ang pook ay maaaring nagsilbi bilang tirahan at depensa. Pinamamahalaan ang Old Sarum ng English Heritage at bukas ito para sa publiko. Ang pag-aaral ay bahagi ng Old Sarum at Stratford-Sub-Castle Archaeological Survey Project na pinangunahan nina Kristian Strutt, Timothy Sly, at Dominic Barker mula Southampton. Ayon kay Heather Sebire, curator ng English Heritage, ang paggamit ng makabagong survey ay nagpalawak ng kaalaman ukol sa kasaysayan ng lugar, bagaman kailangan pa ng karagdagang pagsisiyasat para sa petsa ng mga natuklasan. Dagdag pa ni Kristian Strutt na nagpapakita ang mga resulta na masasabing malaki ang urban development ng outer bailey noong Middle Ages. Inaasahan ng dalawang eksperto na patuloy pa ang mas malalim na pag-aaral sa hinaharap para sa Old Sarum.

article_content: Katarina Marinkovic is in shock, struggling to come to terms with the recent murder of her neighbor, Vesna Crnobrnja, as well as the history of tragedies on Flame Tree Street in Casula. Over the past several years, there have been four deaths across three different houses on this street. 'A plane crashed into one house here, killing two people. Then, a man died by suicide while another house was being built, and now this has happened. It's really upsetting,' she said. Flame Tree Street in Casula has witnessed four deaths in separate incidents involving three different homes. A 50-year-old man has been charged with Vesna Crnobrnja's murder, which occurred on Monday. He has been refused bail and will appear via video link at Campbelltown Court on December 3. Six years ago, two light planes collided mid-air above Flame Tree Street. Both female pilots died when one aircraft crashed into a home in Casula. Katarina Marinkovic expressed being stunned by the events that have resulted in four deaths among three houses on Flame Tree Street. The sequence began in 2008, when two planes collided and one crashed into a house on the street. She also recalled her shock upon hearing that a man had taken his own life inside a home under construction. 'It's all very sad and shocking. I couldn't sleep last night,' she shared. During brief court proceedings, Zoran Crnobrnja, 50, was formally refused bail. His lawyer, Bart Vasic, did not apply for bail but requested that the case be transferred to Campbelltown Local Court. Magistrate Sharon Holdsworth adjourned the matter to December 3rd, when Mr. Crnobrnja is scheduled to appear via video link. Some residents chose to stay indoors, while others commented on how normal Vesna's family seemed. 'We never really spoke—we’d wave occasionally. She worked at the chicken shop down the road, and I’d see her there. She was lovely,' said Mrs. Marinkovic. Colleagues at the chicken shop where Vesna worked were too distraught to speak, but flowers and condolences were sent to the store. Another neighbor stated, 'It was a nice family, but we didn't speak much. Their dog was always out, and there were lots of cars and kids’ friends coming over. I rarely saw the husband but often saw Vesna. I feel for the kids and the family—it’s just really, really sad.' Residents are struggling to process that such a tragic death could occur in their neighborhood in broad daylight. The death of Vesna Crnobrnja is the most recent in a series of tragic events on Flame Tree Street.
translated_content: Nasa matinding pagkabigla si Katarina Marinkovic at hirap tanggapin ang pagpatay sa kapitbahay niyang si Vesna Crnobrnja, pati na rin ang sunod-sunod na trahedya sa Flame Tree Street sa Casula. Sa mga nakaraang taon, apat na katao na ang namatay sa tatlong magkaibang bahay sa kalye na ito. 'May eroplano dati na bumagsak dito, dalawa ang namatay. Tapos may lalaking nagpakamatay habang ginagawa pa lang ang isa pang bahay, tapos eto pa ang nangyari ngayon. Talagang nakakabigla,' sabi niya. Nakaranas ng apat na pagkasawi sa magkakahiwalay na insidente ang Flame Tree Street sa Casula, sa tatlong magkaibang bahay. Isang 50-taong-gulang na lalaki ang kinasuhan sa pagpatay kay Vesna Crnobrnja na nangyari nitong Lunes. Siya ay hindi pinayagang magpiyansa at haharap sa korte sa Campbelltown sa pamamagitan ng video link sa Disyembre 3. Anim na taon na ang nakalipas, dalawang magaan na eroplano ang nagbanggaan sa ere sa itaas ng Flame Tree Street. Parehong namatay ang mga babaeng piloto nang bumagsak ang isa sa mga ito sa isang bahay sa Casula. Nagpahayag si Katarina Marinkovic ng matinding pagkagulat sa mga serye ng pangyayaring nagresulta ng apat na kamatayan sa tatlong bahay sa Flame Tree Street. Nagsimula ito noong 2008 nang magbanggaan ang dalawang eroplano at bumagsak ang isa sa bahay sa nasabing kalye. Naalala rin niya ang pagkabigla nang mabalitang may nagpakamatay sa isang bahay habang ginagawa pa ito. 'Talagang napakalungkot at nakakagulat. Hindi ako nakatulog kagabi,' pahayag niya. Sa maikling pagdinig sa korte, hindi pinayagang magpiyansa si Zoran Crnobrnja, 50. Ang kanyang abogadong si Bart Vasic ay hindi nag-apply ng piyansa ngunit hiniling na ilipat ang kaso sa Campbelltown Local Court. Inurong ni Magistrate Sharon Holdsworth ang pagdinig sa Disyembre 3, kung saan lalabas si G. Crnobrnja sa pamamagitan ng video link. May ilang residente na piniling magkulong sa bahay habang ang iba ay nagsabing normal naman ang pamilya ni Vesna. 'Hindi kami masyadong nagkakausap—kumakaway lang paminsan-minsan. Nagtratrabaho siya sa chicken shop malapit dito at nakikita ko siyang naglilingkod. Mabait siyang tao,' ani Mrs. Marinkovic. Masyadong nalulungkot ang mga kasamahan ni Vesna sa chicken shop kaya hindi sila makapagbigay ng pahayag, ngunit may mga bulaklak at pakikiramay na ipinadala sa tindahan. Sabi pa ng isang kapitbahay, 'Mabait naman ang pamilya, pero hindi kami masyadong nag-uusap. Palaging tumatakbo ang aso nila sa labas, maraming sasakyan, at laging may mga kaibigan ang mga bata. Bihira ko makita ang asawa pero madalas kong makita si Vesna. Nakakaawa talaga ang mga bata at pamilya—nakakalungkot talaga.' Hirap ang mga residente na matanggap na nangyari ang ganitong trahedya sa kanilang lugar sa gitna ng araw. Ang pagkamatay ni Vesna Crnobrnja ang pinakabago sa serye ng malulungkot na pangyayari sa Flame Tree Street.

article_content: With 23% of British adults now classified as obese, it's not surprising that demand for weight-loss surgeries is increasing. In the past decade, there has been a 3000% increase in Britons choosing surgery to help them lose weight. A new Channel 5 documentary, 'When Gastric Bands Go Wrong,' reveals that these procedures can sometimes lead to serious complications. Samantha Haworth was only 22 when she underwent gastric band surgery after being told her weight of 29 stone put her at risk of early death. She lost an impressive 15 stone, but about a year after surgery, she began suffering severe stomach pain. Surgeons discovered her gastric band had slipped, causing part of her stomach tissue to die. A fungal infection developed on the band, leading to a septic condition and the rupture of her stomach. Samantha had to be placed in a medically induced coma and lost most of her stomach, leaving just a small part remaining. Five years later, she still faces ongoing health issues, including an inability to absorb vitamin B12, leaving her constantly fatigued and unable to work. Rachel, a 40-year-old mother from Oxfordshire, also faced serious consequences after her gastric bypass surgery. Initially healthy, she gained weight in her 30s and opted for surgery at age 32. While many have successful procedures, Rachel's operation led to ruptured stitches in her bowel, severe internal complications, and a large abdominal wound. Further surgeries left her intestines more vulnerable, resulting in chronic and uncontrollable diarrhoea. Rachel describes her life as isolated by embarrassment and the daily challenges caused by these side effects. She carries a bag with spare clothes and cleaning supplies whenever she leaves the house. 'When Gastric Bands Go Wrong' airs Wednesday, 16 October on Channel 5 at 9pm.

Sa nakaraang dekada, tumaas ng 3000% ang bilang ng mga Briton na nagpapasurgery para magpapayat. Isang bagong dokumentaryo ng Channel 5, 'When Gastric Bands Go Wrong,' ang nagpapakita na ang mga operasyon na ito ay maaaring magdulot ng seryosong komplikasyon. Dalawampu't dalawang taong gulang lang si Samantha Haworth nang sumailalim siya sa gastric band surgery matapos sabihan na ang timbang niyang 29 na bato ay naglalagay sa kanya sa panganib ng maagang pagkamatay. Nakabawas siya ng 15 na bato, pero pagkalipas ng isang taon mula surgery, nakaranas siya ng matinding sakit ng tiyan. Nadiskubre ng mga surgeon na ang gastric band niya ay dumulas, na naging sanhi ng pagkamatay ng parte ng kanyang tiyan. Nagkaroon ng fungal infection sa band at naging septic ito, na nauwi sa pagkasira ng kanyang tiyan. Kinailangan siyang ilagay sa medically induced coma at halos lahat ng kanyang tiyan ay natanggal, kaya't maliit na bahagi na lang ang natira. Limang taon makalipas ang operasyon, patuloy pa rin ang kanyang mga problema sa kalusugan, kasama na ang kawalan ng kakayahang sumipsip ng vitamin B12, dahilan ng madalas niyang pagkapagod at kawalang-kakayahan magtrabaho. Si Rachel, 40 taong gulang na ina mula Oxfordshire, ay nakaranas din ng seryosong epekto matapos ang kanyang gastric bypass surgery. Dati siyang payat, ngunit tumaba siya sa kanyang 30s at nagpasyang magpaopera sa edad na 32. Bagaman maraming nagtatagumpay sa operasyon, nag-rupture ang tahi sa bituka ni Rachel, na nagdulot ng matinding komplikasyon at malaking sugat sa kanyang tiyan. Ang mga sumunod na operasyon ay nagpalala ng kalagayan ng kanyang bituka, kaya’t kinailangang harapin ang tuluy-tuloy at hindi mapigil na pagtatae. Ikinuwento ni Rachel na nagiging mahirap at nakakahiya ang araw-araw niyang buhay dahil sa mga epekto ng operasyon. Palagi siyang may dalang bag na may ekstrang damit at mga panlinis tuwing lalabas ng bahay. Mapapanood ang 'When Gastric Bands Go Wrong' sa Miyerkules, 16 Oktubre sa Channel 5 ng 9pm.

article_content: Vilet Torrez, a 38-year-old mother from Florida, went missing on March 31 after last being seen at her apartment. Her husband, Cid Torrez, waited three days before filing a missing person report. Authorities later found Vilet's company car parked at her apartment, but she failed to go to work or get in touch with family. The Miramar Police Department recently released a recording believed to feature Cid Torrez, where he says, 'I definitely did it,' in relation to events over the weekend. Vilet and Cid, who began dating in high school, had a turbulent relationship and had separated after 15 years of marriage. On the day of her disappearance, surveillance footage captured Vilet entering her gated community home. Police suspect someone inside let her in by unlocking the security latch, as reported by ABC News. While Cid Torrez is described as a person of interest, investigators stress he has not been named a suspect and has cooperated by providing DNA and fingerprint samples. His attorney stated that Cid's comment in the recording was made when he was upset and while trying to piece together his actions and phone calls with Vilet and her mother. Allegations of abuse and jealousy in the marriage have emerged, with Vilet's brother, Javier Blanco, describing Cid as controlling and having witnessed past physical disputes. Javier also claimed that Cid previously misled new acquaintances by saying Vilet was dead. A judge has ordered that Vilet and Cid’s three children remain in the care of their mother's family and restricted the father's unsupervised contact. Police have searched both Vilet’s and Cid’s vehicles and residences, but so far, no suspects have been identified.

Natagpuan ng mga awtoridad ang kotse ni Vilet sa parking ng apartment, ngunit hindi siya nagpakita sa trabaho o nagbigay-alam sa pamilya. Kamakailan, naglabas ang Miramar Police Department ng isang recording na pinaniniwalaang si Cid Torrez, kung saan narinig siyang nagsabi ng, 'Ako talaga ang gumawa,' kaugnay sa mga pangyayari noong weekend. Lumabas din ang mga alegasyon ng pagiging abusado at seloso, ayon kay Javier Blanco, kapatid ni Vilet, na nagsabing kontrolado ni Cid si Vilet at ilang beses na niyang nasaksihan ang hindi pagkakaunawaan nila.
