article_content:
Journalist and author Will Self is in discussions to become the first writer in residence at BBC Radio 4. The news follows comments from the station’s controller, Gwyneth Williams, who expressed a desire to add excitement and creative flair to the station’s programming. If appointed, Self would serve as a creative figurehead, appearing on flagship programs such as Today, and may also write a blog about the network or contribute fiction inspired by Radio 4's content, according to The Guardian.

In outlining her plans for 2013, Williams emphasized a renewed focus on the station’s cultural offerings and invited artists to share their talents on Radio 4. She noted that while coverage of politics and economics has attracted record audiences, she is eager to broaden the station’s appeal with more arts and culture without reducing existing budgets for news or politics.

Williams described the current atmosphere of political and economic reporting as somewhat stagnant, and believes infusing arts and culture will refresh Radio 4’s output. She said: “It’s nice to have a taste of culture and arts… I want to throw some fireworks into the network – colourful, unpredictable, original work.”

Will Self is recognized for books such as the 2006 novel The Book of Dave and the 2004 story collection Dr Mukti and Other Tales of Woe. Williams has indicated the writer-in-residence role would be modestly paid and open-ended to test its impact.

The initiative is part of a wider push to increase arts coverage at Radio 4, including a £1 million partnership with the creative organization Artangel to commission new works by artists across the UK. The station also plans a ‘cultural exchange’ project featuring 75 smaller commissioned works in art, literature, photography, and architecture, and will launch a talent search series called So You Want To Be A Writer? to discover aspiring fiction authors.

Ang mamamahayag at manunulat na si Will Self ay kasalukuyang pinag-uusapan upang maging kauna-unahang writer in residence ng BBC Radio 4. Nangyari ito matapos ipahayag ng controller ng istasyon na si Gwyneth Williams na nais niyang magdagdag ng sigla at malikhaing elemento sa mga programa ng istasyon. Kung siya ay matutuloy, magsisilbing creative figurehead si Self, lilitaw sa mga pangunahing programa tulad ng Today, at maaaring magsulat ng blog tungkol sa network o gumawa ng fiction na hango sa nilalaman ng Radio 4, ayon sa The Guardian.

Sa kanyang pagsasalarawan ng mga plano para sa 2013, binigyang-diin ni Williams ang layuning mas palakasin ang cultural offerings ng istasyon at inanyayahan ang mga artist na magbahagi ng kanilang talento sa Radio 4. Habang mataas ang bilang ng tagapakinig dahil sa political at economic coverage, nais niyang palawakin pa ang appeal ng istasyon sa pamamagitan ng pagdadagdag ng mas marami pang sining at kultura—ngunit hindi isasakripisyo ang budget para sa balita o pulitika.

Ayon kay Williams, tila nananatili sa isang estado ng hindi paggalaw ang usapin tungkol sa politika at ekonomiya, at naniniwala siyang mapapasigla ng sining at kultura ang programming ng Radio 4. Aniya: “Masarap magkaroon ng lasa ng sining at kultura… Gusto kong magpasabog ng paputok sa network – makukulay, hindi inaasahan, orihinal na mga likha.”

Kilala si Will Self sa kanyang mga libro tulad ng The Book of Dave (2006) at koleksyong Dr Mukti and Other Tales of Woe (2004). Nilinaw ni Williams na ang writer-in-residence na posisyon ay may maliit na bayad at open-ended ang kontrata upang masuri ang epekto nito.

Bahagi ito ng mas malawak na proyekto upang palakasin ang sakop ng sining sa Radio 4, kabilang ang £1 milyong partnership sa creative organization na Artangel para mag-commission ng mga bagong likha ng artist sa UK. Plano rin ng istasyon ang isang 'cultural exchange' na proyekto na magbibigay ng 75 maliliit na commission para sa sining, panitikan, potograpiya, at arkitektura, at maglulunsad ng talent search series na So You Want To Be A Writer? upang matuklasan ang mga bagong fiction author.

article_content: LOS ANGELES — Dr. James Heaps, a former gynecologist at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), can be retried on charges involving additional women, according to a judge’s ruling on Friday. The Superior Court judge approved prosecutors’ request to retry Heaps on nine charges after a jury was unable to reach a verdict on those counts last fall. A new trial date has not yet been set. Heaps, 67, was sentenced to 11 years in prison in April. Last October, he was found guilty of five counts of sexually abusing two female patients. The jury acquitted him on seven other counts and deadlocked on remaining charges involving four women. Heaps was a gynecologist at UCLA for 35 years and was accused of sexually assaulting hundreds of patients during his career. He was arrested in 2019 amid broader scrutiny over sexual misconduct by university doctors. UCLA agreed to pay nearly $700 million in settlements to hundreds of Heaps’ former patients, the largest such payout by a public university. Lawsuits alleged that Heaps groped patients, made inappropriate comments, or carried out unnecessarily invasive exams. Plaintiffs said UCLA ignored and concealed abuse complaints for decades at the student health center, Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center, and Heaps’ campus office. Heaps continued to practice until he retired in June 2018.

Pinayagan ng Superior Court judge ang hiling ng mga tagausig na muling litisin si Heaps sa siyam na kaso matapos mabinbin ang desisyon ng hurado noong nakaraang taon. Wala pang napapetsang bagong paglilitis. Si Heaps, 67, ay sinentensyahan ng 11 taong pagkakakulong noong Abril. Noong Oktubre, napatunayang nagkasala siya sa limang bilang ng sekswal na pang-aabuso sa dalawang babaeng pasyente. Napawalang-sala siya sa pitong iba pang kaso at hindi nagkaisa ang hurado sa natitirang mga kaso na may kinalaman sa apat na babae. Si Heaps ay naging gynecologist sa UCLA ng 35 taon at inakusahan na inabuso ang daan-daang pasyente sa kanyang karera. Inaresto siya noong 2019, kasabay ng pag-usbong ng mga isyu ng sekswal na pang-aabuso ng mga unibersidad na doktor. Pumayag ang UCLA na magbayad ng halos $700 milyon sa mga settlement para sa daan-daang dating pasyente ni Heaps, na pinakamalaki sa kasaysayan ng pampublikong unibersidad. Ayon sa mga demanda, minolestiya ni Heaps ang mga pasyente, nagbitiw ng hindi angkop na mga komento, o nagsagawa ng hindi kinakailangang invasive na eksaminasyon. Sinabi ng mga nagsampa ng kaso na pinabayaan at tinakpan ng UCLA ang mga reklamo ng pang-aabuso sa loob ng mga dekada sa student health center, Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center, at opisina ni Heaps sa campus. Nagpatuloy sa pagpraktis si Heaps hanggang magretiro noong Hunyo 2018.

article_content: A sham marriage between Nigerian Joseph Iwueke, 33, and Slovakian Ingrida Stojkova, 29, was stopped by authorities in Leeds last July after a registrar became suspicious of the couple’s behavior. Iwueke, Stojkova, and two others were arrested minutes before the ceremony when officials noticed Iwueke reading his bride’s details from his hand and the pair could not spell each other’s names. The four have since been jailed for conspiracy to facilitate a breach of UK immigration law. Obinna Odelugo, 49, and Robert Stojka, both found with large sums of cash at the ceremony, were described as the 'fixers' who arranged the marriage for financial gain. Odelugo was discovered hiding in a toilet cubicle after attempting to flee. Leeds Crown Court heard that Iwueke organized the fake wedding to stay in the UK, while Stojkova agreed for financial reasons to support herself and her son. Both pleaded guilty and received prison sentences: Iwueke for two years and nine months, Stojkova for 15 months. Odelugo and Stojka both received sentences of two years and three months. The judge said the marriage was arranged purely for immigration and financial gain. Iwueke is to be deported after serving his sentence, and the court ordered Stojka and Odelugo to pay back £1,000 and £2,000, respectively. Home Office investigator Mark Runagall stated that sham marriage abuse would not be tolerated, and those attempting to cheat the system would face prison terms.

Inaresto sina Iwueke, Stojkova, at dalawa pa ilang minuto bago ang seremonya nang mapansin ng mga opisyal na binabasa ni Iwueke ang detalye tungkol sa kanyang mapapangasawa mula sa kanyang kamay at hindi nila maisulat nang tama ang pangalan ng isa’t isa. Nakulong ang apat dahil sa sabwatan na labagin ang batas ng imigrasyon ng UK. Nahuli rin sa seremonya sina Obinna Odelugo, 49, at Robert Stojka na may dalang malaking halaga ng pera at tinukoy na ‘fixers’ o tagapag-ayos ng kasal kapalit ng pera. Natagpuan si Odelugo na nagtago sa banyo matapos subukang tumakas. Ibinunyag sa Leeds Crown Court na inorganisa ni Iwueke ang huwad na kasal upang manatili sa UK, habang pumayag si Stojkova kapalit ng pera para masuportahan ang sarili at anak. Pareho silang umamin at nakatanggap ng parusang pagkakakulong: si Iwueke ng dalawang taon at siyam na buwan, si Stojkova ng labinlimang buwan. Parehong hinatulan sina Odelugo at Stojka ng dalawang taon at tatlong buwan. Ayon sa hukom, ang kasal ay isinagawa lamang para sa imigrasyon at pinansyal na kapakinabangan. Ipade-deport si Iwueke matapos makulong, at naatasan ang korte na bayaran nina Stojka at Odelugo ang £1,000 at £2,000. Sinabi ni Mark Runagall mula Home Office na hindi papayagan ang pang-aabuso sa huwad na kasal at ang sinumang lumabag ay makukulong.

article_content: A Norman Rockwell painting titled 'Saying Grace' was sold at a New York City auction for $46 million, setting a new record for the Saturday Evening Post illustrator, according to Sotheby's. The painting was initially estimated to sell for $15 million to $20 million. The $46 million price includes the auction house premium. In 2006, Sotheby's sold Rockwell's 'Breaking Home Ties' for over $15 million, which was then a record price. 'Saying Grace' depicts a crowded restaurant where a grandmother and her grandson bow their heads in prayer at their table. The painting was sold to an undisclosed buyer. Another Rockwell painting, 'The Gossips,' sold for just under $8.5 million, while 'Walking to Church' fetched slightly more than $3.2 million at the same auction. For almost twenty years, all three paintings were on loan to the Norman Rockwell Museum in Stockbridge, Massachusetts, which houses the world's largest collection of original Rockwell artworks. The museum is located in the artist's hometown. Norman Rockwell was paid $3,500 for 'Saying Grace.' The painting appeared on the cover of The Saturday Evening Post's Thanksgiving issue in 1951 and was later voted readers’ favorite cover in a 1955 poll. The idea for the illustration was inspired by a reader who had seen a Mennonite family praying in a restaurant. Rockwell's son, Jarvis, was one of the models for the artwork. 'The Gossips,' also sold at the auction for just under $8.5 million, was a cover illustration for the March 6, 1948 issue of The Saturday Evening Post and depicts the artist’s neighbors, his wife Mary, and Rockwell himself gossiping on the telephone. 'Walking to Church,' which was featured on the April 4, 1953 cover, shows a family in their Sunday best walking along a city street. Rockwell based the painting on a work by the Dutch artist Johannes Vermeer. These three paintings, along with four other Rockwell pieces, were sold by the family of Kenneth Stuart, Rockwell’s longtime art director at The Saturday Evening Post. The sale took place after years of legal disputes among Stuart’s three sons. Rockwell and Stuart worked together for 18 years at the magazine. Laurie Norton Moffatt, director of the Norman Rockwell Museum, expressed hope that the paintings would eventually return. 'We cared for them like children... We hope they come back someday. We believe that's where they belong,' she said.
translated_content: Isang painting ni Norman Rockwell na pinamagatang 'Saying Grace' ay naibenta sa isang auction sa New York City ng $46 milyon, na bagong rekord para sa illustrator ng Saturday Evening Post, ayon sa Sotheby’s. Tinatayang nagkakahalaga ito ng $15 milyon hanggang $20 milyon bago ang auction. Kasama na sa $46 milyon ang auction house premium. Noong 2006, naibenta rin ng Sotheby’s ang 'Breaking Home Ties' ni Rockwell ng higit $15 milyon, na siyang record noon. Makikita sa 'Saying Grace' ang eksena sa masikip na restaurant kung saan magkasamang nagdarasal ang isang lola at kanyang apo sa kanilang mesa. Hindi ibinunyag kung sino ang bumili ng painting. Ang isa pang obra ni Rockwell, ang 'The Gossips,' ay nabenta ng halos $8.5 milyon, samantalang ang 'Walking to Church' ay nabili ng higit $3.2 milyon sa parehong auction. Halos dalawampung taon ding naka-loan sa Norman Rockwell Museum sa Stockbridge, Massachusetts ang tatlong painting, na siyang may pinakamalaking koleksyon ng mga orihinal na gawa ni Rockwell. Matatagpuan ang museo sa bayan ng artist. Si Norman Rockwell ay binayaran ng $3,500 para sa 'Saying Grace.' Lumabas ito sa cover ng Thanksgiving issue ng The Saturday Evening Post noong 1951 at napili ng mga mambabasa bilang paborito noong 1955. Ang ideya ng painting ay inspirasyon mula sa isang mambabasa na nakakita ng Mennonite family na nagdarasal sa restaurant. Isa sa mga modelong ginamit ni Rockwell ay ang kanyang anak na si Jarvis. Ang 'The Gossips,' na nabenta rin ng halos $8.5 milyon, ay ginamit sa cover ng March 6, 1948 issue ng The Saturday Evening Post at nagpapakita ng mga kapitbahay ng artist, ang kanyang asawang si Mary, at si Rockwell mismo na nag-uusap sa telepono. Ang 'Walking to Church,' na lumabas sa cover ng April 4, 1953, ay nagpapakita ng isang pamilyang bihis na bihis na naglalakad sa isang kalye ng lungsod. Hinango ito ni Rockwell mula sa likha ng Dutch artist na si Johannes Vermeer. Ang tatlong painting na ito, at apat pang iba, ay ibinenta ng pamilya ni Kenneth Stuart, dating art director ni Rockwell sa The Saturday Evening Post. Ang bentahan ay naganap matapos ang ilang taon ng alitan ng tatlong anak ni Stuart. Magkasama sina Rockwell at Stuart ng 18 taon sa magazine. Ipinahayag ni Laurie Norton Moffatt, direktor ng Norman Rockwell Museum, ang pag-asa na babalik ang mga painting. 'Inalagaang parang mga anak ang mga yun… Sana bumalik sila balang araw. Naniniwala kaming doon talaga sila bagay,' sabi niya.

article_content: Drivers are generally expected to follow the Highway Code, but in some cases, this can be challenging. Unusual new road markings at a junction in Stamford Hill, north London, have confused motorists by seemingly directing them straight into a traffic island. Another marking further ahead — noticed by Paul Wood, 50, from Harlow, Essex, while driving in the area — appeared to give drivers the option of turning into oncoming traffic. Mr Wood saw a sign that read ‘New Road Layout’ before encountering the unusual markings at the junction of Seven Sisters Road and Amhurst Park. The first arrow offered the choice to turn left, consistent with the traffic flow, or to continue straight toward a traffic island. After the island, another marking appeared to allow turning into oncoming vehicles. Mr Wood said, ‘After you would bear left, if you look to the right, there’s a traffic cone, then another sign instructing you to turn left — but that leads into oncoming traffic.’ Comparing Google Street View images shows how the road looked before and after the new markings were painted. Mr Wood, who grew up in the area, added, ‘I nearly followed the broken lines — I had to do a double take and continued on the correct path.’ Dana Skelley, Director of Roads at Transport for London, explained that these confusing markings were temporary and inadvertently left after essential bridge waterproofing was completed. She told MailOnline: ‘These temporary road markings, which were put in place during bridge waterproofing works, should have been removed when the work finished. They will be taken away and replaced by our highway contractor this evening. We apologize for any confusion this has caused.’

Nakalilito ang mga bagong markang pangkalsada sa isang junction sa Stamford Hill, hilagang London, dahil parang itinuturo nito ang mga motorista diretso sa traffic island. Isa pang marka pa sa unahan — napansin ni Paul Wood, 50, mula Harlow, Essex, habang nagmamaneho sa lugar — ay parang binibigyan ang mga drayber ng opsyon na lumiko papunta sa kasalubong na trapiko. Nakita ni Ginoong Wood ang karatulang ‘New Road Layout’ bago niya makita ang kakaibang mga marka sa pagitan ng Seven Sisters Road at Amhurst Park. Ang unang arrow ay nag-alok ng pagpipilian na lumiko pa-kaliwa, na ayon sa daloy ng trapiko, o umabante diretso papunta sa traffic island. Paglampas ng island, may isa pang marka na lumilitaw na pumapayag lumiko sa kasalubong na mga sasakyan. Sabi ni G. Wood, ‘Pagkatapos mong kumanan, kung titingnan mo sa kanan, may traffic cone, tapos may isa pang karatula na nagsasabi na lumiko pa-kaliwa — pero papunta na iyon sa kasalubong na trapiko.’ Pinapakita ng paghahambing sa Google Street View kung ano ang itsura ng kalsada bago at pagkatapos ipintura ang mga bagong marka. Dagdag pa ni G. Wood, na lumaki sa lugar, ‘Halos sundan ko na ang mga broken lines — kailangan kong mag-double take kaya dumiretso na lang ako sa tamang daan.’ Ipinaliwanag ni Dana Skelley, Director of Roads ng Transport for London, na pansamantala lang ang mga markang ito at hindi sinasadyang naiwan matapos ang trabaho sa waterproofing ng tulay. Sabi niya sa MailOnline: ‘Ang mga pansamantalang marka sa kalsada na ito, na inilagay habang ginagawa ang waterproofing ng tulay, ay dapat tinanggal na matapos ang proyekto. Tatanggalin ito at papalitan ng aming highway contractor ngayong gabi. Humihingi kami ng paumanhin sa anumang kalituhan na dulot nito.’

article_content: Where excitement might be expected, there is instead anxiety. Where there is hope, there is also fear. England not only dreams of victory—it braces for a night of drama and tension at Wembley Stadium as the national team seeks World Cup qualification. Roy Hodgson’s side knows that one win against Poland would guarantee a place at next year’s World Cup in Brazil, but memories of past disappointment loom large—especially the 1973 qualifier, where Poland, led by goalkeeper Jan Tomaszewski, denied England a World Cup spot with a 1-1 draw. Despite dominating that match, England failed to win, marking one of the most disappointing nights in their football history. Now, Poland, with the support of over 18,000 fans, hopes to challenge England once again. Hodgson admits feeling worried ahead of the match, saying, 'Anyone who works in football is a worrier.' Still, he trusts in his squad’s ability, acknowledging that football’s unpredictability makes managers uneasy. England’s qualifying campaign has been inconsistent, with draws against Ukraine, Poland, and Montenegro, and only recent convincing wins against San Marino, Moldova, and Montenegro. Former Polish goalkeeper Tomaszewski criticized England’s current form, suggesting they are not as strong as in past eras, but still the best team in their group. England last failed to qualify for a major tournament in 2008, ending Steve McClaren’s tenure and stirring anxieties when they lost heavily to Germany at the 2010 World Cup. If England does not beat Poland and Ukraine defeats San Marino, England will face the playoffs. However, Poland has not beaten England in a competitive match for 40 years, and Hodgson remains confident, emphasizing each game is unique. Spain also needs a result to qualify—just a draw against Georgia to secure a World Cup spot. France could overtake Spain if they slip up, but French captain Hugo Lloris expects Spain to advance. France could meet Portugal in the playoffs unless Portugal achieves a major win and Russia loses in their final matches. Bosnia can qualify for their first-ever World Cup with a win over Lithuania while Greece faces Liechtenstein. Bosnia’s coach Safet Susic is optimistic, noting the team’s strong preparation. Iceland is also on the verge of history, needing a positive result against Norway to reach the playoffs. Captain Aron Gunnarsson says his young team is ready for the occasion. In Group D, Turkey, Romania, and Hungary are in a tight race for playoff spots as Turkey faces the Netherlands and Romania hosts Estonia. In South America, Chile and Ecuador need only a draw in their match to qualify, while Uruguay could qualify if results go their way.
translated_content: Sa halip na kasabikan, kaba ang nangingibabaw. Sa likod ng pag-asa, may kasamang takot. Hindi lang tagumpay ang inaasahan ng England—handa sila sa isang gabing puno ng tensyon at drama sa Wembley Stadium habang sinusubukan nilang makapasok sa World Cup. Alam ng grupo ni Roy Hodgson na isang panalo laban sa Poland ang kailangan para masiguro ang slot sa World Cup sa Brazil sa susunod na taon, ngunit nananatili ang mapapait na alaala—lalo na noong 1973 qualifier kung saan si Jan Tomaszewski, goalkeeper ng Poland, ang naging dahilan ng pagkabigo ng England sa pamamagitan ng 1-1 draw. Kahit na umabante ang England sa laban na iyon, bigong manalo ang koponan—isa ito sa mga pinakamalungkot na gabi sa kasaysayan ng football ng England. Ngayon, umaasa ang Poland, na suportado ng mahigit 18,000 fans, na muling hadlangan ang England. Inaamin ni Hodgson na kinakabahan siya bago ang laban: 'Lahat ng nagtatrabaho sa football ay nag-aalala.' Gayunpaman, buo pa rin ang tiwala niya sa kakayahan ng kanyang koponan, at tinatanggap niyang hindi tiyak ang football kaya’t madalas mabahala ang mga coach. Hindi naging tuloy-tuloy ang tagumpay ng England sa qualifiers, may mga draw kontra Ukraine, Poland, at Montenegro, at kamakailan lamang sila nakakuha ng solidong panalo kontra San Marino, Moldova, at Montenegro. Pinuna ni Tomaszewski, dating Polish goalkeeper, na hindi kasing lakas ng dati ang England ngayon, pero sila pa rin pinakamalakas sa kanilang grupo. Huling hindi naka-qualify ang England sa malaking torneo noong 2008, na naging dahilan ng pagpapatalsik kay Steve McClaren at bumalik ang pangamba nang matalo sila sa Germany noong 2010 World Cup. Kung hindi mananalo ang England at magwagi ang Ukraine kontra San Marino, sa playoffs dadaan ang England. Ngunit lampas 40 taon nang hindi nagwawagi ang Poland laban sa England sa opisyal na laro, kaya may kumpiyansa si Hodgson at binibigyang-diin na bawat laban ay kakaiba. Kailangan din ng Spain ng magandang resulta para makapasok—tabla kontra Georgia ay pasok na sila sa World Cup. Maaaring lampasan ng France ang Spain kung magkamali ang huli, pero inaasahan ni kaptan Hugo Lloris na magtatagumpay ang Spain. Maaaring makatunggali ng France ang Portugal sa playoffs maliban na lang kung makakuha ng malaking panalo ang Portugal at matalo ang Russia sa kanilang huling laban. Unang beses na makakapasok sa World Cup ang Bosnia kung matatalo nila ang Lithuania habang kakalabanin naman ng Greece ang Liechtenstein. Kumpiyansa ang coach ng Bosnia na si Safet Susic sa handa ng koponan. Malapit nang magsulat ng kasaysayan ang Iceland, basta't maganda ang resulta kontra Norway para makuha ang playoff spot. Ayon sa captain na si Aron Gunnarsson, handang-handa na ang kabataang koponan ng Iceland. Sa Group D, mahigpit ang labanan ng Turkey, Romania, at Hungary para sa playoff spots—makakaharap ng Turkey ang Netherlands at Romania naman ay Estonia. Sa South America, isang tabla lang ang kailangan ng Chile at Ecuador para makapasok. Maaari ring makalusot ang Uruguay kung papabor ang mga resulta.

article_content: A new documentary features FBI agents who described how Boston mobster James 'Whitey' Bulger was ultimately captured, thanks in part to a stray cat and records of plastic surgery. For 16 years, America's most-wanted criminal, Bulger, and his partner, Catherine Greig, avoided capture by blending in as an elderly couple in Santa Monica, California. The FBI revealed that they closed in on the couple when two clues emerged: Greig's care for a stray cat, and records of her past breast augmentation. Bulger, a notorious Boston crime figure, was sentenced to life in prison earlier this month for decades of murder, extortion, money laundering, arms trafficking, and drug dealing. The 84-year-old was arrested in 2011 with Greig at their Santa Monica apartment, where they had lived quietly for years. Neighbors, such as Barbara Gluck, noted how Greig regularly fed a stray cat whose owner had died, ensuring the couple blended in seamlessly. Bulger had previously embarrassed the FBI after infiltrating the Boston office and receiving protection from compromised agents, allowing him to flee in 1995 before his indictment. For over a decade, agents struggled to find solid leads or photographs of the couple. Appeals to veterinarians about their love of animals were unsuccessful. However, agents pursued another lead: Greig's reported plastic surgery. Dr. Matthias Donelan found her records, including photographs, providing vital information. Agent Tommy MacDonald recounted how they quickly secured these photos, which helped focus the investigation on Greig. Using the photographs, the FBI produced public service announcements on daytime talk shows aimed at women, eventually receiving a tip from a neighbor who described Greig's care for a cat. This tip matched other evidence and prompted immediate action. When law enforcement arrested Bulger in 2011, they discovered more than $822,000 and 30 guns hidden in the walls of their rent-controlled apartment. The couple had been living under assumed names, with Greig handling daily errands. Bulger's life sentence, delivered earlier this month, ended a case that exposed deep FBI corruption and led many to doubt he would be brought to justice. Bulger remained defiant, calling his trial a sham and refusing to cooperate with probation officials. He was convicted in 11 of 19 murders; Greig received an eight-year sentence for aiding him.
translated_content: Isang bagong dokumentaryo ang nagtatampok ng mga ahente ng FBI na nagkwento kung paano nahuli sa wakas si Boston mobster James 'Whitey' Bulger, sa tulong ng isang pusang ligaw at mga rekord ng plastic surgery. Sa loob ng 16 na taon, naiwasan nina Bulger at ng kanyang kasama na si Catherine Greig na mahuli sa pamamagitan ng pamumuhay bilang ordinaryong matandang mag-partner sa Santa Monica, California. Ibinunyag ng FBI na napalapit sila sa dalawa nang magtagpo ang dalawang mahalagang pahiwatig: ang pag-aalaga ni Greig sa pusang ligaw at ang rekord ng kanyang breast augmentation noon. Si Bulger, isang kilalang kriminal sa Boston, ay hinatulan ng habambuhay na pagkakakulong ngayong buwan dahil sa mga kasong pagpatay, pangingikil, money laundering, arms trafficking, at pagbebenta ng droga. Naaresto si Bulger, 84, noong 2011 kasama si Greig sa kanilang apartment sa Santa Monica, kung saan tahimik silang namuhay ng ilang taon. Kuwento ng kapitbahay na si Barbara Gluck, laging pinapakain ni Greig ang pusang ligaw na naulila, kaya naging hindi napansin ang kanilang pagtira roon. Dati nang naging kahihiyan para sa FBI si Bulger matapos niyang pasukin ang Boston office at nakakuha ng proteksyon mula sa mga tiwaling ahente, dahilan para makatakas siya noong 1995 bago siya kasuhan. Mahigit sampung taon ding nahirapan ang mga ahente na makahanap ng matibay na lead o litrato ng dalawa. Hindi rin nagtagumpay ang pakikipag-ugnayan nila sa mga beterinaryo tungkol sa pagmamahal ng mag-partner sa hayop. Pero may isa pang nahanap na lead ang mga ahente: ang plastic surgery ni Greig. Natagpuan ni Dr. Matthias Donelan ang mga rekord at litrato niya, na naging mahalagang impormasyon. Ikinuwento ni Agent Tommy MacDonald kung paano nila agad nakuha ang mga litratong ito na naging sentro ng imbestigasyon kay Greig. Gamit ang mga litrato, gumawa ang FBI ng mga public service announcement sa mga daytime talk show na tumutok sa mga kababaihan, hanggang sa makatanggap ng tip mula sa kapitbahay hinggil sa pag-aalaga ni Greig sa pusa. Tugma ito sa iba pang ebidensya kaya agad silang umaksyon. Nang hulihin si Bulger noong 2011, natagpuan ng mga awtoridad ang mahigit $822,000 at 30 baril na itinago sa dingding ng kanilang apartment na rent-controlled. Gumamit sila ng pekeng pangalan at si Greig ang namimili at nagbabayad ng bills. Ang habambuhay na sentensiya kay Bulger na ibinigay ngayong buwan ay nagtapos sa isang kasong nagbunyag ng malalim na katiwalian sa FBI, kaya marami ang nagdudang mahuhuli pa siya. Nanatiling matigas si Bulger, tinawag na 'sham' ang kaniyang paglilitis at tumanggi makipagtulungan sa opisyal ng probation. Nahatulan siya sa 11 sa 19 na kasong pagpatay; si Greig naman ay nahatulan ng walong taon para sa pagtulong sa kaniya.

article_content: President-elect Barack Obama announced Thursday that he has chosen former Senator Tom Daschle to lead the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). Obama emphasized that addressing health care is crucial to repairing the economy. In addition to heading HHS, Daschle will serve as director of the White House Office of Health Reform. Obama has also selected Jeanne Lambrew to be the deputy director of that office. Obama praised Daschle as “one of America’s foremost health care experts,” and said Daschle will not only implement the administration’s health care plan, but also play a key role in designing it. Daschle expressed enthusiasm for his dual role in crafting and putting health care reforms into action. He highlighted that health care has long been America's leading domestic policy challenge, and said that fixing the system will improve citizens’ health, help businesses become more competitive, reduce personal bankruptcies and foreclosures, and support economic recovery. CNN previously reported that Daschle, a 61-year-old former Senate majority leader from South Dakota, was Obama’s expected choice. Earlier, Daschle had voiced excitement about helping to reform the nation’s health care system, serving on Obama’s health care advisory group, and writing the plan Obama will submit to Congress. He hopes to have the plan enacted next year, though full implementation will take several years. Daschle has said, “We can't afford not to do it. If we do nothing, we’ll be paying twice as much on health care in 10 years as we do today.” Daschle served as Democratic leader in the Senate from 1995 until 2004, after representing South Dakota in the House from 1978 and being elected to the Senate in 1986. He recently wrote the book “Critical: What We Can Do About the Health Care Crisis,” advocating for universal health care through expanding federal health benefits and integrating private plans with Medicaid and Medicare. Many Republicans oppose such proposals, arguing they would give too much power to the government, and some have raised concerns about Daschle’s recent work with a Washington lobbying firm. Tom Daschle’s wife, Linda Daschle, is a registered lobbyist whose firm represents health care clients. However, a source told CNN that Linda Daschle plans to leave her job at the end of the year to open her own company focusing on transportation lobbying to avoid conflicts of interest. In addition to these appointments, three Democratic sources say Obama is likely to nominate Steven Chu, director of the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, as Energy Secretary. The announcement is expected next week in Chicago, along with the naming of Carol Browner, former EPA administrator under President Clinton, as the White House’s new 'climate czar.' Reporters Candy Crowley and Ed Henry contributed to this story.

Pinuri ni Obama si Daschle bilang “isa sa pinaka-eksperto sa health care sa Amerika” at sinabi na hindi lang ipatutupad ni Daschle ang health care plan ng administrasyon kundi magiging susi rin siya sa pagdisenyo nito. Inihayag ni Daschle ang kanyang kasabikan sa dual role na ito—gagawa at magpapatupad ng health care reforms. Binanggit niyang matagal nang pangunahing policy challenge sa Amerika ang health care at ang pagsasaayos ng sistema ay makakatulong sa kalusugan ng mga tao, sa pagiging kompetitibo ng mga negosyo, at makakabawas sa bankruptcies at foreclosures, pati na rin makakatulong sa pagbangon ng ekonomiya. Iniulat ng CNN dati na si Daschle, 61 taong gulang at dating Senate majority leader mula South Dakota, ang inaasahang pipiliin ni Obama. Kung wala tayong gawin, doble na ang gagastusin natin sa health care pagkalipas ng 10 taon.” Naging Senate Democratic leader si Daschle mula 1995 hanggang 2004. Bago nito, nagsilbi siya bilang representative ng South Dakota sa House mula 1978 at natalaga bilang senador noong 1986. Maraming Republican ang tumututol sa mga ganitong panukala, sinasabing masyadong lalaki ang kapangyarihan ng gobyerno, at may ilang nagtataas ng isyu tungkol sa pagtratrabaho ni Daschle sa Washington lobbying firm. Ang kanyang asawa na si Linda Daschle ay isang registered lobbyist at ang kanilang kumpanya ay may health care clients. Ngunit ayon sa source ng CNN, plano ni Linda Daschle na umalis sa trabaho niya sa pagtatapos ng taon para magtayo ng sariling kumpanya na nakatutok sa transportation lobbying upang maiwasan ang conflict of interest. Bukod dito, ayon sa tatlong Democratic sources, posible ring italaga ni Obama si Steven Chu, direktor ng Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, bilang Energy Secretary. Inaasahang iaanunsyo ito sa susunod na linggo sa Chicago, kasama ang pagtatalaga kay Carol Browner, dating EPA administrator noong Clinton administration, bilang bagong 'climate czar' ng White House. Nag-ambag sa ulat sina Candy Crowley at Ed Henry ng CNN.

article_content: A new global space race is underway, with scientists and engineers working on a project that once seemed like pure science fiction: the space elevator. This concept involves building a cable anchored to the Earth's surface and extending tens of thousands of kilometers into space, balanced by a counterweight. The elevator would provide direct, low-cost access to orbit. Hundreds of engineers and scientists from Asia, Europe, and the Americas are collaborating to develop practical designs. A conference scheduled in Japan this November will further discuss these developments. Carbon nanotubes, with their exceptional strength and lightweight properties, are considered the leading material for the elevator's cable. Though prototypes exist, current carbon nanotube tethers have only a fraction of the required strength. Researchers hope the necessary materials will be ready during the 2020s or 2030s. Potential uses for the space elevator include transporting people and cargo into space more efficiently, deploying solar panels for terrestrial power, and disposing of nuclear waste. The idea, made popular in novels like Arthur C. Clarke’s 'The Fountains of Paradise,' is now a subject of serious scientific effort. Organizations such as the Japan Space Elevator Association (JSEA), the U.S.-based Spaceward Foundation, and the Liftport Group are actively pursuing the project, supported by more than 300 scientists and engineers worldwide. NASA is incentivizing innovation via a $4 million Space Elevator Challenge. Major obstacles remain: manufacturing extremely long, strong cables from carbon nanotubes, securing financial investment, addressing legal issues around international cooperation, and selecting a site near the equator and away from natural hazards like typhoons. Suggested locations include the South China Sea, western Australia, and the Galapagos Islands. Professor Jeff Hoffman of MIT notes that while the materials science is advancing rapidly, the ability to manufacture sufficient lengths of carbon nanotube cable remains a key hurdle. Akira Tsuchida of JSEA adds that funding and public belief in the project are significant challenges, as is shifting public perception. Both Hoffman and Tsuchida believe that building a space elevator is a matter of 'when,' not 'if.' Hoffman describes it as a project with the revolutionary power to usher in a new era for humanity, potentially transforming not just space travel but our entire technological future.
translated_content: Isang bagong pandaigdigang lahi sa espasyo ang isinasagawa ngayon, kung saan nagtutulungan ang mga siyentista at inhinyero sa proyektong dati'y kathang-isip lang: ang space elevator. Isa itong kable na nakakabit sa mundo at binabalanse ng counterweight na umaabot ng libu-libong kilometro sa kalawakan. Layunin nitong gawing diretso at mas mura ang pagpunta sa orbit. Daan-daang inhinyero at siyentista mula Asya, Europa, at Amerika ang nagsasama-sama para sa mga praktikal na disenyo. Magkakaroon ng conference sa Japan ngayong Nobyembre upang palawakin pa ang diskusyon ukol sa mga development. Carbon nanotubes ang pangunahing tinitingnang materyales para sa kable dahil sa tibay at gaan nito. Bagama't may prototype na, nasa bahagi pa lang ng lakas na kailangan ang mga umiiral na kable. Umaasa ang mga eksperto na makakamit ang wastong materyales sa 2020s o 2030s. Maaaring gamitin ang space elevator sa mas epektibong pagdadala ng tao at kargo sa kalawakan, pag-deploy ng solar panels para sa enerhiya rito sa mundo, at pagtatapon ng nuclear waste. Sumikat ito noon sa aklat na 'The Fountains of Paradise' ni Arthur C. Clarke ngunit seryosong tinatrabaho na ito ngayon ng agham. Ang Japan Space Elevator Association (JSEA), Spaceward Foundation mula US, at Liftport Group ay mga organisasyong masigasig sa proyekto—tinutulungan ng mahigit 300 siyentipiko/inhinyero sa buong mundo. May patimpalak na $4M din ang NASA para sa mga inobasyon dito. Ilan sa mga hamon ay: paggawa ng sobrang tibay at habang kable gamit ang carbon nanotubes, pagkuha ng pondo, pagsasaayos ng mga legal at international na usapin, at pagpili ng lokasyon malapit sa ekwador na iwas sa bagyo. Mga tinitingnang lugar ay South China Sea, western Australia, at Galapagos Islands. Paliwanag ni Prof. Jeff Hoffman (MIT), mabilis ang usad ng research pero mahirap gumawa ng sapat na mahaba/tibay na kable. Dagdag ni Akira Tsuchida (JSEA), hamon din ang pagkuha ng pondo at pagbago ng pananaw ng publiko ukol dito. Para kina Hoffman at Tsuchida, tiyak na darating ang panahon ng space elevator. Sabi ni Hoffman, magiging rebolusyonaryo ito para sa sangkatauhan, di lang para sa space travel kundi pati sa teknolohiya.

article_content: A sudden cloudburst over Lhonak Lake triggered severe flooding in a valley of northeastern Sikkim state, India. Heavy rainfall is hindering the search for 23 Indian soldiers who went missing after the flash flood. The state capital, Gangtok, has been cut off by road, according to defence officials. The flood struck a valley about 150 km (93 miles) north of Gangtok, near the border with China. The Indian Army stated that a flash flood occurred in the Teesta River due to a sudden cloudburst over Lhonak Lake in North Sikkim, leading to 23 personnel reported missing. Search operations are ongoing. A defence spokesperson in Guwahati, Assam, reported that some army facilities along the valley have been affected. Rising water, following the release from a dam, submerged some vehicles. The area is remote, close to India’s border with Nepal, and Lhonak Lake is located at the base of a glacier near Kangchenjunga, the world’s third-highest mountain. The Army reported that water released upstream from the Chungthang dam had already raised the river to more than 4.5 meters (15 feet) above normal. About 15,000 people living nearby are likely to be impacted, and at least eight major bridges along the Teesta River have been destroyed, according to VS Pathak, Sikkim's Chief Secretary. An Indian Army spokesperson released a video showing a thick stream of brown water sweeping through the forested valley, with washed-out roads and fallen power lines. The India Meteorological Department has warned of possible landslides and flight disruptions as heavy rain is forecast in some regions of Sikkim. Flash floods and landslides frequently occur during the monsoon season, which starts in June and usually ends by late September in the Indian subcontinent. By October, the heaviest monsoon rains typically subside. Experts say climate change is making such disasters more frequent and intense. Other Army photos showed water flooding the first floors of buildings and flowing through towns, with only the tip of a construction crane visible above water. Local media depicted Sikkim Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang visiting Singtam town during heavy rain to meet officials about the flood situation downstream of the missing soldiers’ location. The monsoon happens when summer heat warms the subcontinent, causing air to rise and draw in cooler Indian Ocean winds, resulting in heavy rain. However, this also leads to annual destruction from landslides and floods. Melting glaciers and unregulated development in flood-prone areas worsen the damage. According to the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), Himalayan glaciers are melting faster due to climate change. Their report from June indicated glaciers disappeared 65 percent more quickly during 2011-2020 compared to the previous decade. At current emission rates, glaciers may lose up to 80 percent of their current volume by century’s end.
translated_content: Isang biglaang matinding pag-ulan sa ibabaw ng Lhonak Lake ang nagdulot ng matinding pagbaha sa isang lambak sa hilagang-silangang estado ng Sikkim, India. Nahihirapan ang mga awtoridad na hanapin ang 23 sundalong Indiano na nawala matapos ang biglaang pagbaha dahil sa patuloy na malakas na ulan. Naisara ang kabisera ng estado, Gangtok, dahil sa baha, ayon sa mga opisyal ng depensa. Tumama ang pagbaha sa isang lambak mga 150 km (93 milya) sa hilaga ng Gangtok, malapit sa hangganan ng China. Ayon sa Indian Army, naganap ang biglaang pagbaha sa Ilog Teesta matapos ang cloudburst sa ibabaw ng Lhonak Lake sa North Sikkim, dahilan ng pagkawala ng 23 sundalo. Patuloy pa rin ang search operations. Sinabi ng tagapagsalita ng depensa mula Guwahati, Assam, na naapektuhan ang ilang kampo ng army sa lambak. Tumaas ang tubig matapos ang paglabas mula sa isang dam at nilubog nito ang mga sasakyan. Ang lugar ay malayo at malapit sa hangganan ng Nepal, at ang Lhonak Lake ay nasa paanan ng glacier malapit sa Kangchenjunga, ang ikatlong pinakamataas na bundok sa mundo. Iniulat ng Army na ang tubig mula sa Chungthang dam ay nagdulot ng pagtaas ng ilog nang higit sa 4.5 metro (15 talampakan) kaysa karaniwan. Humigit-kumulang 15,000 tao ang maaaring maapektuhan at hindi bababa sa walong pangunahing tulay sa tabi ng Ilog Teesta ang winasak, ayon kay VS Pathak, Chief Secretary ng Sikkim. Nagpakita ng isang video ang Army ng rumaragasa at makapal na putik na tubig sa kakahuyang lambak, nilamon ang mga kalsada at pinatumba ang mga linya ng kuryente. Nagbabala ang India Meteorological Department ng posibleng landslide at pagkaantala ng biyahe ng eroplano sa ilang bahagi ng Sikkim dahil sa malakas na ulan. Karaniwan nang nararanasan ang flash flood at landslide tuwing panahon ng tag-ulan, na nagsisimula ng Hunyo at kadalasang nagtatapos pagsapit ng Setyembre sa subkontinente ng India. Sa Oktubre, kalimitang tapos na ang pinakamabibigat na ulan. Sabi ng mga eksperto, pinalala ng climate change ang tindi at dalas ng mga ganitong sakuna. Ipinakita rin sa ibang litrato ng Army na nilamon ng tubig ang unang palapag ng mga gusali at dumadaloy ito sa mga kalsada ng mga bayan, na tanging dulo na lamang ng isang construction crane ang makikita. Tampok sa lokal na media si Sikkim Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang na bumisita sa bayan ng Singtam sa gitna ng ulan para makipagpulong sa mga opisyal tungkol sa baha sa bahagi ng ilog na downstream sa pinaghahanap na mga sundalo. Nangyayari ang monsoon kapag umiinit ang lupa ng subkontinente tuwing tag-init, dahilan upang tumaas ang hangin at humigop ng mas malamig na hangin mula Indian Ocean na nagdadala ng malakas na ulan. Ngunit dulot din nito taon-taong pinsala dahil sa landslide at baha. Lalong pinalala ng natutunaw na glacier at hindi reguladong pagpapatayo sa mababang lugar ang pinsala. Ayon sa International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), mas mabilis nang natutunaw ang mga Himalayan glacier dahil sa climate change. Sa kanilang ulat ng Hunyo, napag-alamang 65 porsyento nang mas mabilis ang pagkatunaw ng glacier mula 2011-2020 kumpara sa naunang dekada. Kapag hindi nagbago ang polusyon, posibleng mabawasan ng hanggang 80 porsyento ang glacier sa dulo ng siglo.

article_content: Children belonging to our early ancestors did not develop as quickly as modern humans, according to new research. Scientists studied the Taung Child, a 3.3 million-year-old skull discovered 90 years ago in South Africa. They found that the Taung Child, known as Australopithecus africanus, did not experience the same rapid brain growth in its first few months as modern human babies do. This indicates it was less human-like than previously thought. The first reconstruction of the Taung Child fossil shows it did not have a postnatal brain growth spurt like modern infants. Found in South Africa 90 years ago, the roughly 3.3 million-year-old fossil is believed to have belonged to a child aged 3 to 4 years old. The Taung Child is historically and scientifically significant as a key example of early hominin brain evolution. Its discovery in 1924 was among the first early human fossils found in Africa, bringing attention to the continent as a possible origin for the human family tree. The findings challenge the idea that this early hominin showed similar infant brain development in the prefrontal region as modern humans. The skull was scanned at high-resolution, with no evidence found for cranial adaptations that support such brain growth, contrary to previous claims. Careful dental analysis estimated the child's age at death at 3.3 years. The Taung Child is thought to have been killed by an eagle, since puncture marks were found at the bottom of the eye sockets. Dr. Kristian J. Carlson and colleagues at the University of the Witwatersrand conducted a virtual dissection of the skull. Carlson noted recent claims that the fossil displayed features for rapid postnatal brain growth, but their results show no evidence that such adaptations evolved before Homo, nor a link to early prefrontal lobe expansion.
translated_content: Ayon sa bagong pananaliksik, ang mga bata ng ating sinaunang ninuno ay hindi kasing-bilis ang pag-unlad kumpara sa mga modernong tao. Sinuri ng mga siyentipiko ang Taung Child, isang bungo na 3.3 milyong taong gulang na natuklasan 90 taon na ang nakalilipas sa Timog Africa. Natuklasan nila na ang Taung Child, na kilala rin bilang Australopithecus africanus, ay hindi nakaranas ng mabilis na paglaki ng utak sa unang mga buwan nito, di tulad ng mga sanggol ngayon. Ipinapahiwatig nito na hindi ito kasing-tulad ng tao gaya ng dati nang inisip. Ipinapakita ng unang rekonstruksiyon ng Taung Child fossil na wala itong karanasan ng postnatal brain growth spurt gaya ng sa mga modernong sanggol. Natuklasan ito sa Timog Africa, mga 3.3 milyong taon na ang nakalipas, at pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa batang may edad na 3 hanggang 4 na taon. Ang Taung Child ay mahalaga sa kasaysayan at agham bilang isang pangunahing halimbawa ng ebolusyon ng utak ng mga sinaunang hominin. Ang pagkakatuklas dito noong 1924 ay itinuturing na isa sa mga unang fossil ng tao na natuklasan sa Africa, na nagbigay-diin sa kontinente bilang isang posibleng pinagmulan ng human family tree. Hinahamon ng mga natuklasan ang ideya na ang sinaunang hominin na ito ay may kahalintulad na pag-unlad ng utak sa prefrontal region kagaya ng mga modernong tao. Isinailalim sa high-resolution na pag-scan ang bungo, at walang nakitang ebidensya ng cranial adaptations para sa gayong paglaki ng utak, taliwas sa mga naunang pahayag. Ayon sa maingat na pagsusuri ng ngipin, tinatayang namatay ang bata sa edad na 3.3 taon. Pinaniniwalaang napatay ang Taung Child ng isang agila dahil sa mga butas sa ilalim ng kanyang eye sockets. Sina Dr. Kristian J. Carlson at mga kasamahan mula University of the Witwatersrand ang nagsagawa ng virtual dissection ng bungo. Binanggit ni Carlson na may mga kamakailang pahayag na nagpapakita ng mga katangian ng mabilis na brain growth pagkatapos ipanganak, ngunit base sa resulta ng kanilang pag-aaral, walang ebidensya na lumitaw ang ganitong adaptasyon bago pa ang Homo, pati na rin ang ugnayan sa maagang paglawak ng prefrontal lobe.

Teresa Meehan, a 75-year-old widow living in Plymouth, faced unexpected police scrutiny after her lost cat, Rambo, returned home following a four-month absence. Overjoyed at first, Meehan soon learned that Rambo had been microchipped and adopted by another person from Plymouth Cat Rescue, who renamed him Butch.

Although the other owner decided not to keep the cat, the situation escalated. Police began investigating Meehan for allegedly stealing Rambo, and local posters with photos offered a reward and accused her of theft. Officers contacted Meehan repeatedly as part of a three-week probe into who should keep the cat.

Upset by the public accusations and references to the animal shelter, Meehan asked a lawyer to intervene and contacted the police and Devon and Cornwall’s crime commissioner. She expressed anger that police responded more thoroughly to this case than to her previous burglary. Plymouth’s Labour MP Alison Seabeck also got involved, stating the case was distressing but that authorities took it seriously. While Rambo is safe with Meehan for now, she remains fearful of letting him outdoors. Plymouth Cat Rescue did not comment.
translated_content:
Si Teresa Meehan, isang 75-anyos na balo mula sa Plymouth, ay naimbestigahan ng pulisya nang bumalik ang kanyang nawawalang pusa, si Rambo, makalipas ang apat na buwan. Labis ang tuwa ni Meehan, ngunit nalaman niyang na-microchip at inampon ng ibang tao si Rambo mula sa Plymouth Cat Rescue, at tinawag na Butch.

Hindi na rin binalik ng bagong amo si Rambo, pero lalong lumala ang isyu. Inimbestigahan si Meehan ng pulisya sa paratang na ninakaw niya ang sariling pusa. Kumalat ang mga poster na may larawan ni Rambo na may alok na gantimpala, at inaakusahan si Meehan ng pagnanakaw. Paulit-ulit siyang kinontak ng mga pulis sa loob ng tatlong linggo hinggil sa pag-aari ng pusa.

Dahil sa mga akusasyon at pagbanggit sa animal shelter, kumuha si Meehan ng abogado para matanggal ang mga poster, at humingi ng tulong sa pulisya at crime commissioner ng Devon at Cornwall. Ipinunto niyang mas inasikaso ng pulisya ang kasong ito kaysa sa naunang pagnanakaw sa kanyang bahay. Bagama't kasama na ni Meehan si Rambo, natatakot pa rin siyang palabasin ito. Tumanggi namang magbigay ng pahayag ang Plymouth Cat Rescue.

article_content: NEW DELHI: Driven by a strong recovery in travel after the Covid pandemic, Thomas Cook India reported record profit growth for July-September 2023 (Q2 FY24). Profit surged to Rs 76.6 crore, compared to Rs 4.9 crore in the same period last year. This growth was led by the travel businesses of Thomas Cook and SOTC, as well as by their Foreign Exchange and Sterling Holidays segments. The company’s overseas travel division turned profitable, posting a profit of Rs 8 crore versus a loss of Rs 17.6 crore in the previous year’s quarter. As of September 30, 2023, the group had a cash and bank balance of Rs 13.4 billion. Executive Chairman Madhavan Menon stated, 'The Thomas Cook (India) Group delivered another strong performance this quarter, with EBITDA rising 2.4 times to Rs 1,308 million compared to Rs 548 million in Q2 FY23. Our consolidated profit before tax soared over 16 times to Rs 766 million, up from Rs 49 million last year. The outstanding performance across the Group—including Foreign Exchange, Travel (leisure, business, and MICE), Sterling Holidays, and DEI—demonstrates our teams’ efficiency and service quality.' Menon also highlighted, 'Our overseas travel business showed a complete turnaround, with profit before tax reaching Rs 80 million compared to a loss of Rs 176 million in Q2 FY23. The leisure segment grew 36% year-on-year, mainly driven by Thomas Cook and SOTC. Forward bookings in our Travel Services are up 32% for the festive season and beyond. We expect to finish the year strongly and will continue focusing on technology improvements to enhance customer experience and productivity.'

Tumaas ang kita sa Rs 76.6 crore, mula sa Rs 4.9 crore sa parehong panahon noong nakaraang taon. Ang pagtaas na ito ay pinangunahan ng mga travel business ng Thomas Cook at SOTC, pati na ng Foreign Exchange at Sterling Holidays segments. Naging profitable din ang overseas travel division ng kumpanya ngayong taon, na nagtala ng kita na Rs 8 crore kumpara sa pagkalugi ng Rs 17.6 crore noong nakaraang taon. Noong Setyembre 30, 2023, may cash at bank balance ang grupo na Rs 13.4 bilyon. Ayon kay Executive Chairman Madhavan Menon, “Nagpakita ang Thomas Cook (India) Group ng panibagong malakas na performance ngayon quarter, kung saan ang EBITDA ay tumaas ng 2.4x sa Rs 1,308 milyon kumpara sa Rs 548 milyon noong Q2 FY23. Umangat ng mahigit 16 na beses ang aming consolidated profit bago buwis sa Rs 766 milyon mula sa Rs 49 milyon noong nakaraang taon. Ang kahanga-hangang performance ng buong grupo—kabilang ang Foreign Exchange, Travel (leisure, business, at MICE), Sterling Holidays, at DEI—ay nagpapakita ng husay at kalidad ng aming serbisyo.” Dagdag ni Menon, “Lubusang bumuti ang aming overseas travel business, na nagtala ng profit bago buwis na Rs 80 milyon kumpara sa pagkalugi ng Rs 176 milyon noong Q2 FY23. Ang leisure segment ay lumago ng 36% year-on-year, karamihan ay dahil sa Thomas Cook at SOTC. Tumaas ng 32% ang forward bookings sa aming Travel Services ngayong festive season at lampas pa. article_content: What will weather reports be like in 2050? According to researchers, they could be dramatic and unsettling if climate change is not controlled. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) is releasing a series of videos demonstrating how global warming may affect our planet in the coming decades. These fictional weather reports illustrate potential problems such as droughts, floods, and heat waves over the next 30 years. The WMO, headquartered in Geneva, is sharing these scenarios based on the continuation of current climate change trends. Researchers warn that if greenhouse gas emissions keep rising, Earth's average temperature could increase by more than 4°C (7.2°F) by the end of the 21st century. A report released earlier this year also concluded that emissions from agriculture could continue to grow as global meat and dairy consumption rises. If not addressed, nitrous oxide from fields and methane from livestock could double by 2070, making it nearly impossible to reach climate targets. Experts from Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden emphasize that reducing meat and dairy consumption is key to lowering agricultural emissions. 'Broad dietary change can take a long time. We should consider how to make food more climate-friendly,' the researchers note. By 2050, estimates suggest that beef and lamb could account for half of all agricultural greenhouse gas emissions but provide only about three percent of human calorie intake. Cheese and other dairy products may be responsible for around a quarter of total agricultural emissions. To help people visualize these impacts, the WMO invited television weather presenters from Europe, South America, and the US to create imagined weather reports set in 2050. The resulting videos offer dramatic scenarios based on the latest climate science. A preview video has been released, with more to follow throughout September on the WMO website. The project aims to support discussions at the UN Climate Summit 2014 on September 23. UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon will urge leaders from government, finance, business, and civil society to take decisive action against climate change. The WMO hopes a meaningful legal agreement will emerge to start seriously reducing greenhouse gas emissions from next year. Rising global temperatures could lead to more extreme events like storms, droughts, and flooding worldwide. The videos are being released ahead of the UN Climate Summit 2014.
translated_content: Ano kaya ang magiging lagay ng panahon sa mga ulat sa 2050? Ayon sa mga mananaliksik, maaaring maging mas dramatiko at nakakabahala ang mga ito kung hindi mapipigilan ang climate change. Ang World Meteorological Organization (WMO) ay naglalabas ng serye ng mga video na nagpapakita kung paano maaaring maapektuhan ang ating planeta ng global warming sa mga susunod na dekada. Ipinapakita ng mga kathang-isip na ulat ng panahon ang mga posibleng problema gaya ng tagtuyot, pagbaha, at matitinding init sa susunod na 30 taon. Ang WMO, na nakabase sa Geneva, ay nagbabahagi ng mga senaryong ito base sa patuloy na paglala ng climate change. Nagbabala ang mga mananaliksik na kung patuloy na tataas ang greenhouse gas emissions, ang average na temperatura ng mundo ay maaaring tumaas ng higit sa 4°C (7.2°F) pagsapit ng katapusan ng ika-21 siglo. Ayon din sa ulat na inilabas ngayong taon, maaaring patuloy pang tumataas ang emissions mula sa agrikultura dahil sa pagtaas ng pagkonsumo ng karne at dairy sa buong mundo. Kung hindi mapipigilan, ang nitrous oxide mula sa mga taniman at methane mula sa mga hayop ay maaaring dumoble pagsapit ng 2070, na magpapahirap makamit ang mga climate target. Binigyang-diin ng mga eksperto mula sa Chalmers University of Technology sa Sweden na mahalaga ang pagbawas ng pagkain ng karne at dairy para mapababa ang emissions sa agrikultura. 'Maaaring abutin ng matagal ang malawakang pagbabago sa pagkain. Dapat nating pag-isipan kung paano gagawing mas climate-friendly ang ating pagkain,' sabi ng mga mananaliksik. Pagsapit ng 2050, tinatayang ang baka at tupa ay magiging responsable sa kalahati ng greenhouse gas emissions mula sa agrikultura ngunit nagbibigay lamang ng humigit-kumulang tatlong porsyento ng ating calorie intake. Samantalang ang keso at iba pang dairy products ay maaaring magdulot ng isang-kapat ng kabuuang emissions sa agrikultura. Upang mas maunawaan ng mga tao ang mga epekto ng climate change, inimbitahan ng WMO ang mga weather presenter mula sa Europe, South America, at US na gumawa ng mga kathang-isip na ulat ng panahon para sa taong 2050. Ang mga video na ito ay naghahatid ng dramatikong senaryo batay sa pinakabagong climate science. May inilabas nang preview video, at marami pang ibang video ang ilalabas ngayong Setyembre sa website ng WMO. Layon ng proyektong ito na suportahan ang mga talakayan sa UN Climate Summit 2014 sa ika-23 ng Setyembre. Hihimukin ni UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon ang mga pinuno ng gobyerno, pinansyal na sektor, negosyo at civil society na gumawa ng malinaw na aksyon laban sa climate change. Umaasa ang WMO na magkakaroon ng makabuluhang kasunduan para simulan ang seryosong pagbawas ng greenhouse gas emissions simula sa susunod na taon. Ang patuloy na pag-init ng mundo ay maaaring magdulot ng mas maraming matinding bagyo, tagtuyot, at pagbaha sa buong mundo. Inilalabas ang mga video bilang paghahanda para sa UN Climate Summit 2014.

article_content: Pakistan captain Babar Azam has responded to criticism of his leadership as his team faces near-elimination from the 2023 Cricket World Cup in India. Ahead of their crucial match against England at Eden Gardens, Kolkata on Saturday, Babar acknowledged underperforming but stood by his leadership, saying: "I have not performed the way I should have in the World Cup, that's why people say I'm under pressure. Over the last two and a half to three years, I was the one performing for the side and leading the team." He criticized the volume of external opinions, adding: "If someone really wants to advise me, everyone has my number, but it's easy to give advice on TV." Pakistan started the tournament with wins against the Netherlands and Sri Lanka but suffered a four-match losing streak, including difficult defeats to Afghanistan and South Africa. Fakhar Zaman's outstanding unbeaten 126 off 81 balls against New Zealand in their last match has kept their hopes alive. To reach the semifinals, Pakistan must beat England by a massive margin. They need to bat first, post a huge total, and then bowl England out for a very low score—winning by at least 287 runs to surpass New Zealand on net run rate. Historically, Pakistan’s highest ODI total against England is 361, set in 2019. If they repeat this score, they would need to bowl England out for 74 or fewer to have a chance. Babar stressed that the team is planning carefully: "This scenario is on our minds, and we will try to achieve it. But we can't just go in and start attacking blindly—we have to plan each phase of the match, from the first 10 overs to the next 20, focusing on partnerships and roles." England is also under pressure. Their 2023 World Cup campaign has been disappointing, with just two wins and six losses. Test captain Ben Stokes, who requires knee surgery, has stayed with the squad to support them. Jos Buttler, England's white-ball captain since 2022, has faced criticism for his decisions during the tournament. England must win this match to qualify for the Champions Trophy, which has become their primary motivation. "It's great to be heading there with something on the line," said Buttler. In 88 one-day internationals between the sides, Pakistan has won 32 and England 56, with no draws. England won the last three encounters in 2021 despite fielding a weakened squad due to COVID-19. Pakistan's last victory over England was at the 2019 World Cup in Nottingham. Both teams are desperate for a win, but only an extraordinary result will be enough for Pakistan to stay in the tournament.

Sa loob ng dalawa't kalahati hanggang tatlong taon, ako ang nagdadala at namumuno sa koponan." Ipinunto niya rin ang dami ng opinyon mula sa iba: "Kung talagang gusto nilang magbigay ng payo, alam ng lahat ang number ko, pero parang mas madali yatang magpayo sa TV." Nagsimula ang Pakistan sa torneo na panalo laban sa Netherlands at Sri Lanka, ngunit nagkaroon ng apat na sunod na pagkatalo, kabilang ang masaklap na pagkalugi kontra Afghanistan at South Africa. Ang napakagandang performance ni Fakhar Zaman na hindi na-out sa 126 mula sa 81 bola laban sa New Zealand ang nagbigay ng pag-asa sa kanila. Para makapasok sa semifinals, kailangan talunin ng Pakistan ang England nang malaking agwat. Kailangan nilang maunang mag-bat, makapuntos ng malaki, at mapabagsak agad ang England—kailangang manalo ng hindi bababa sa 287 runs para malampasan ang net run rate ng New Zealand. Ang pinakamataas na ODI total ng Pakistan kontra England ay 361 noong 2019. Kung mauulit ito, kailangan nilang ma-bowled out ang England sa 74 runs o mas mababa pa. Binigyang-diin ni Babar na may plano ang koponan: "Nasa isip namin ang ganitong scenario, at susubukan naming makamit ito. Pero hindi pwedeng bara-bara lang—kailangan naming planuhin bawat yugto ng laro, mula sa unang 10 overs, pagkatapos ay sa susunod na 20; mag-focus sa partnership at role ng bawat isa." Kailangan ding manalo ng England sa laban para makapasok sa Champions Trophy, na siyang pangunahing motibasyon nila. "Maganda na may nakataya pa rin sa laban na ito," ani Buttler. Sa 88 one-day international na laban ng dalawang koponan, 32 ang napanalunan ng Pakistan, 56 ng England, at wala pang tabla. Huling nanalo ang England sa tatlong magkasunod na laban noong 2021 kahit kulang ang kanilang line-up dahil sa COVID-19. Huling panalo ng Pakistan sa England ay noong 2019 World Cup sa Nottingham. Parehong desperado sa panalo ang parehong koponan, ngunit kakaibang milagro ang kailangan ng Pakistan para manatili sa torneo.

article_content:
ETA’s constructive and affirmative reply to the declaration from the International Conference group in Donostia-San Sebastian marks significant progress in Basque peace negotiations. This achievement follows years of persistent dialogue and effort, highlighting the need to maintain momentum as the process moves forward.

My engagement with establishing peace in the Basque Country began around the time of the 1998 Irish peace agreement. Fr. Alex Reid, an Irish priest instrumental to our peace process, brought his expertise to the Basque region at the request of local clergy. Since that time, Sinn Féin leaders, myself included, have continued to meet with representatives from the Basque community and the Spanish government. It’s evident that many in the Basque region are deeply invested in building peace and are keen to learn from the Irish journey.

About two years ago, the Abertzale Left, which encompasses the banned Batasuna party, agreed on a new approach centered solely on democratic and political methods. This stance is notably reminiscent of Ireland’s, grounded in principles like those developed by former US Senator George Mitchell during our peace talks. Their commitment includes rejecting violence, honoring all parties’ voices, and upholding democratic standards.

Recently, I returned to Donostia-San Sebastian to participate in an international conference on the Basque peace process, joined by figures such as Kofi Annan, Jonathan Powell, Bertie Ahern, Pierre Joxe, and Gro Harlem Brundtland. We offered recommendations for immediate progress, stressing that violence often persists when alternatives are absent and that achieving peace means providing those alternatives, seeking understanding across divides, and prioritizing dialogue above all else. Each conflict is different, but practices like dialogue, addressing the root causes, inclusiveness, mutual respect, and confidence-building are vital across contexts.

Post-conference, the International Group affirmed that ending Europe’s last armed conflict is feasible. ETA was urged to publicly announce an end to armed activity and to seek discussions with Spanish and French officials about the conflict’s aftermath. ETA’s announcement fulfills this request and Spain has welcomed the move.

To solidify this advance, attention should now turn to reconciliation, supporting the victims, demilitarizing the region, ensuring all political parties have equal rights, and recognizing the Basque people’s right to self-determination. Experience in Ireland and South Africa illustrates that peace, while complex, is achievable if leaders are willing to take risks and show vision.

*Note: The views presented reflect those of Gerry Adams.*
translated_content:
Ang malinaw at positibong sagot ng ETA sa pahayag ng International Conference group sa Donostia-San Sebastian ay isang malaking hakbang patungo sa kapayapaan sa Basque. Bunga ito ng maraming taon ng patuloy na diyalogo at pagsisikap, at napakahalagang mapanatili ang momentum ng proseso.

Nagsimula ako sa paglahok sa kapayapaan sa Basque Country noong kasagsagan ng kasunduan sa Ireland noong 1998. Si Fr. Alex Reid, isang paring Irish na may makabuluhang ambag sa peace process namin, ay inanyayahan ng ilang pari sa Basque upang magbahagi ng kanyang kaalaman. Mula noon, kami ng mga pinuno ng Sinn Féin ay regular na bumibisita at nakikipagpulong sa mga kinatawan ng komunidad ng Basque at pamahalaan ng Espanya. Malinaw ang dedikasyon ng marami sa Basque sa kapayapaan at ang kagustuhang matuto mula sa Irish na karanasan.

Dalawang taon na ang nakalipas ng magpasa ng bagong estratehiya ang Abertzale Left, kasama ang ipingbabawal na Batasuna party, na pulos demokratiko at politikal ang paraan sa pagtamo ng layunin. Malapit ito sa wika’t prinsipyo sa Ireland sa ilalim ng gabay ni dating Senador George Mitchell. Kabilang dito ang pagtalikod sa dahas, paggalang sa lahat ng panig, at pagsusulong ng demokrasya.

Kamakailan, bumalik ako sa Donostia-San Sebastian para sa isang internasyonal na kumperensya para itulak ang kapayapaan sa Basque, kasama sina Kofi Annan, Jonathan Powell, Bertie Ahern, Pierre Joxe, at Gro Harlem Brundtland. Nagbigay kami ng mungkahi para sa agarang progreso at binigyang-diin ko ang mahalagang papel ng diyalogo, pag-unawa sa magkabilang panig, at pagtutok sa tunay na ugat ng problema. Tanging sa pamamagitan ng inklusibong usapan at pagbubuo ng tiwala mapagwawagi ang ganitong mga proseso.

Matapos ang kumperensya, nagbigay pahayag ang International Group na maaaring tapusin ang natitirang armadong tunggalian sa Europa. Hinikayat nila ang ETA na magdeklara ng tuluyang pagtigil sa armadong aksyon at simulan ang pag-uusap kasama ang pamahalaan ng Espanya at Pransya hinggil sa mga epekto ng hidwaan. Tinugunan ito ng ETA at tinanggap ng gobyerno ng Espanya.

Upang patatagin itong tagumpay, dapat nang umarangkada patungo sa pagkakasundo, pagtulong sa mga biktima, demilitarisasyon, paggalang sa pantay na karapatan ng lahat ng partido, at pagkilala sa karapatan ng mga taga-Basque sa sariling pagpapasya. Ang karanasan sa Ireland at South Africa ay patunay na makakamit ang kapayapaan kung may tapang at malasakit ang mga lider.

*Tandaan: Ang mga opinyong ito ay mula kay Gerry Adams.*

article_content: Nigeria’s Federal Government has unveiled the ‘Vision to Action’ strategy, a five-year plan (2023-2027) to strengthen defense against infectious diseases and address emerging health threats. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) launched the initiative in Abuja after analyzing lessons from its previous plan covering 2017-2022. The strategy prioritizes digital transformation and the improvement of health information systems. It maps out seven goals, 41 objectives, and 225 activities to be pursued through collaborations among federal, state, and local governments, the private sector, and development partners. Dr. Ifedayo Adetifa, NCDC’s Director General, explained that the new plan emphasizes building resilient systems, expanding reach, and ensuring sustainable impact through the Strategic, Ambitious, Speed, and Scale framework. He pointed out that Nigeria’s score in the World Health Organization’s Joint External Evaluation (JEE) rose from 39% in 2018 to 54% in 2023, positioning the country as the third worldwide to complete a second JEE round. The strategy is designed to fortify surveillance, laboratory services, and outbreak response throughout Nigeria. A performance management structure will oversee implementation and align various initiatives to expand health security in the country, with the support of all health partners.
translated_content: Inilunsad ng Pederal na Pamahalaan ng Nigeria ang estratehiyang ‘Vision to Action’, isang limang taon na plano (2023-2027) para palakasin ang depensa laban sa mga nakahahawang sakit at mga bagong banta sa kalusugan. Inilathala ito ng Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) sa Abuja, matapos nilang suriin ang mga natutunan mula sa nauna nilang plano noong 2017-2022. Ang estratehiya ay nakatuon sa digital transformation at pagpapabuti ng mga sistema ng impormasyon sa kalusugan. Kabilang dito ang pitong layunin, 41 na mga tunguhin, at 225 na aktibidad na isasagawa sa tulong ng magkakatuwang na pambansa, estado, at lokal na pamahalaan, pribadong sektor, at mga kaagapay na organisasyon. Ayon kay Dr. Ifedayo Adetifa, Director General ng NCDC, pinapalakas ng bagong plano ang matatag na sistema, mas malawak na sakop, at pangmatagalang resulta gamit ang Strategic, Ambitious, Speed, at Scale na framework. Binigyang-diin niyang tumaas ang marka ng Nigeria sa Joint External Evaluation (JEE) ng World Health Organization mula 39% noong 2018 tungong 54% noong 2023, kaya't ang Nigeria ay pangatlo sa buong mundo na nakagawa ng ikalawang JEE. Layunin ng estratehiya na patingkarin ang surveillance, mga serbisyo sa laboratoryo, at kakayahan sa pagtugon sa mga outbreak sa buong bansa. May performance management structure din upang bantayan at iugnay ang mga inisyatibo para palakasin ang seguridad sa kalusugan ng bansa kasama ang mga katuwang na ahensya.

article_content: Superman and Wonder Woman, two of DC Comics’ most well-known heroes, are set to begin a romantic relationship in the upcoming Justice League comic. This change follows DC Comics’ recent overhaul of key characters, which notably ended Superman’s relationship with Lois Lane. Their new romance, launching after a pivotal event in Justice League issue 12 as reported by The Guardian, features prominently on the comic’s cover, showing Superman and Wonder Woman locked in a passionate kiss. Fans are reacting with a mix of excitement and skepticism about this major storyline, especially given that both characters juggle secret identities and unusual schedules. The update is one of several for Superman, who recently lost his adoptive parents Jonathan and Martha Kent and underwent a notable costume change, leaving out his iconic red shorts. In film news, the next Superman movie, 'Man of Steel,' will feature Henry Cavill as Superman, Russell Crowe as Jor-El, and Amy Adams as Lois Lane, with rumors circulating about a possible Wonder Woman movie. Lynda Carter, known for her 1970s TV portrayal, remains an enduring symbol of the character.

article_content: Scientists have achieved a significant breakthrough in uncovering the cause of age-related memory loss, bringing hope for the future development of drugs to reverse this process. A recent study provides strong evidence that age-related memory loss is a separate condition from pre-Alzheimer's, and could eventually be treatable. Researchers at Columbia University Medical Center examined brain tissue from both young and older individuals who died with no signs of neurological disease. Their investigations identified that in a specific part of the hippocampus—the brain's memory center—a certain gene stops functioning properly as people age, leading to a reduction in a key protein called RbAp48. This region, known as the dentate gyrus, has long been thought especially vulnerable to aging. Importantly, it is not the same brain region where Alzheimer's disease typically begins. The findings suggest that a decrease in RbAp48 is connected to age-related memory loss. To better understand this, researchers studied mice, which experience memory decline with age similar to humans. They found that reducing the protein in healthy young mice caused memory problems similar to those seen in older mice. Even more promising, boosting RbAp48 levels in older mice reversed memory loss, returning their cognitive abilities to those of much younger animals. Dr. Eric Kandel, a Nobel laureate who led the Columbia team, called this 'the best evidence so far' that age-related memory loss differs from early Alzheimer’s disease. The results raise further questions about whether such memory decline is an inevitable part of normal aging or can be prevented. Dr. Scott Small, a senior author of the study, emphasized the importance of even mild memory decline as people live longer and face increasingly complex cognitive demands. He noted that these findings open new paths for intervention research. However, Dr. Molly Wagster of the National Institute on Aging, who was not involved in the study, cautioned that this is early-stage research and will require years of further work to confirm. She highlighted that not everyone develops Alzheimer's as they age, and that normal aging can involve weakening neuron connections, making it harder—but not impossible—to retrieve memories, unlike Alzheimer’s, which kills neurons outright. The research underscores that many pathways contribute to memory, and the RbAp48 protein is involved in transforming short-term memories into long-term ones. Encouragingly, scientists know that exercise enhances the functioning of the dentate gyrus, and ongoing studies are investigating whether nutrition might also play a role.
translated_content: Nagtagumpay ang mga siyentipiko sa pagtuklas ng sanhi ng pagkawala ng memorya dulot ng pagtanda, na nagbibigay ng pag-asa para sa mga gamot na posibleng makabawi ng memorya sa hinaharap. Ayon sa isang bagong pag-aaral, may matibay na ebidensiya na ang pagkawala ng memorya dahil sa edad ay hiwalay sa pre-Alzheimer’s at maaaring maagapan o magamot balang araw. Sinuri ng mga mananaliksik mula sa Columbia University Medical Center ang utak ng mga batang at matandang namatay na walang sintomas ng neurological disease. Napag-alaman nilang sa isang partikular na bahagi ng hippocampus – memory center ng utak – may gene na tumitigil ang paggana habang tumatanda, kaya nababawasan ang protinang RbAp48. Kilala nang bahagi ang dentate gyrus na matindi ang epekto ng pagtanda at hindi ito ang lokasyon ng simula ng Alzheimer’s. Napagbigyang-diin ng resulta na ang pagbaba ng RbAp48 ay nauugnay sa pagkawala ng memorya sa pagtanda. Para maintindihan pa ito, pinag-aralan sa mga daga ang epekto ng protein na ito. Kapag binawasan ito sa mga batang daga, bumababa ang kakayahang maalala – gaya ng matatandang daga. Kapag dinagdagan naman sa matatanda, bumabalik ang memorya nila parang bata ulit. Sabi ni Nobel laureate Dr. Eric Kandel, ito ang ‘pinakamalakas na ebidensya’ na magkaiba ang age-related memory loss at early Alzheimer’s. Dahil dito, lumalabas na puwede palang hindi normal lang ang pagkalimot habang tumatanda. Binanggit ni Dr. Scott Small na mahalaga rin ito dahil mas tumatagal ang mga tao at mas nagiging mahirap ang mga iniisip. Nagbubukas ang research na ito ng bagong paraan para maghanap ng lunas. Ngunit ayon kay Dr. Molly Wagster ng National Institute on Aging (hindi kabilang sa pag-aaral), ito ay unang hakbang pa lang at kailangan pa ng matagal na pananaliksik. Dagdag niya na kahit tumatanda tayo, hindi ibig sabihin mapupunta agad sa Alzheimer’s. Sa normal na pagtanda, nanghihina lang ang ugnayan ng neurons kaya mas mahirap tandaan ang ilan, hindi tulad ng Alzheimer’s na sumisira talaga ng mga neuron. Lumalabas sa research na maraming paraan para gumana ang memorya at kasama ang RbAp48 sa paglilipat mula short-term patungong long-term memory. Magandang balita rin na nakakatulong ang ehersisyo para gumana ang dentate gyrus, at tinitingnan din kung ang nutrisyon ay may epekto.
