article_content: Asian markets edged higher on Tuesday as investors awaited an important U.S. inflation report that could affect the Federal Reserve’s next steps. Meanwhile, the Japanese yen lingered near a one-year low against the dollar, approaching intervention territory. The MSCI Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan rose 0.49%, Tokyo’s Nikkei gained 0.36%, and Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 climbed 0.61%. The yen traded at 151.71 per dollar after briefly touching 151.92—a one-year low and close to a 33-year low at 151.94. Japan’s Finance Minister Shunichi Suzuki reiterated the government’s readiness to respond to excessive currency moves, calling sharp swings undesirable. Investors are closely watching the U.S. inflation data due later, following comments from Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell that rates may still be insufficient to tame inflation. Reuters-polled economists anticipate that headline U.S. consumer price inflation slowed to 3.3% in October from 3.7% in September, with core inflation holding steady. ActivTrades trader Anderson Alves said the results hold major sway over future Fed policy. Lower-than-expected core inflation could ease expectations of further hikes, while a higher figure may increase short-term rate forecasts. Chinese shares advanced, with the CSI 300 up 0.40% and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng up 0.57%, ahead of this week’s summit between U.S. and Chinese leaders. U.S. benchmark 10-year Treasury yields rose 2.2 basis points to 4.654%, down from Monday’s one-week high of 4.696%. Moody’s recently cut its U.S. credit outlook to 'negative' from 'stable', citing growing deficits and lower debt affordability. Fitch downgraded the U.S. credit rating in August. Dalma Capital CIO Gary Dugan said this move exposes structural U.S. challenges, including high debt and fiscal leniency, noting that major reforms are unlikely before the upcoming election. The U.S. risks a partial government shutdown by Saturday if Congress fails to pass a stopgap bill. Attention has returned to the yen after its 14% drop against the dollar this year sparked speculation over a possible intervention. The currency briefly rebounded in New York on options market activity but remains weak. Standard Chartered macro strategist Nicholas Chia remarked that these swings reveal market nerves about intervention, which may help counter excessive speculation. Japan has not intervened in currency markets since October last year. The U.S. dollar index edged up to 105.69, but it is down 1% in November, expected to break a three-month streak. Oil prices ticked higher after OPEC said market conditions remain strong. U.S. crude rose to $78.46 per barrel; Brent was flat. Separately, India’s Income Tax Department is investigating Apple, Google, and Amazon’s Indian units over potential transfer pricing issues dating back to a 2021 probe. Indians have become the largest investors in Dubai’s real estate market, influencing the city’s property sector. Digital payments firm Razorpay plans a cross-border merger to relocate its parent to India, potentially incurring $250-300 million in U.S. taxes. article_content: Disney's Epcot has relaunched its Habit Heroes attraction after facing significant criticism for shaming overweight children. Initially, the interactive exhibit showcased cartoon figures like 'Snacker,' an overweight fairy, 'Lead Bottom,' who avoided exercise, and 'The Glutton,' a villain driven by overeating. These characters were pitted against positive heroes Will Power and Callie Stenics. Public backlash followed, with groups like the National Association to Advance Fat Acceptance condemning Disney for perpetuating negative stereotypes. Dr. Yoni Freedhoff, a medical expert, also criticized shaming tactics in a setting meant for enjoyment. Responding to the controversy, Disney shut down the original attraction within a month. The exhibit has since reopened, with feedback from health professionals leading to the removal of the problematic characters. Brent Strong of Walt Disney Imagineering said visitor feedback indicated some elements distracted from the main message of healthy lifestyles. The updated attraction now focuses on encouraging everyone to make healthy choices, regardless of body size. Tony Jenkins from Florida Blue, which sponsors Habit Heroes, highlighted that the new approach aims to inspire families and communities to work together for better health.
translated_content: Muling binuksan ng Disney ang Habit Heroes attraction sa Epcot matapos itong batikusin dahil umano'y pinapahiya nito ang mga batang matataba. Sa unang bersyon, ipinakita ang mga cartoon na karakter tulad ni 'Snacker,' isang matabang diwata, 'Lead Bottom' na umiiwas mag-ehersisyo, at ang kontrabidang si 'The Glutton' na mahilig sa pagkain. Nilalabanan sila ng mga positibong bayani na sina Will Power at Callie Stenics. Tumanggap ng matinding batikos ang Disney mula sa mga grupo tulad ng National Association to Advance Fat Acceptance dahil sa pagpapalaganap ng negatibong stereotype. Nagsalita rin si Dr. Yoni Freedhoff, isang eksperto sa medisina, na hindi dapat ginagamit ang kahihiyan bilang taktika lalo na sa isang lugar ng kasiyahan. Bilang tugon, ipinasara agad ng Disney ang orihinal na attraction sa loob ng isang buwan. Muling binuksan ang exhibit matapos kumonsulta sa mga propesyonal sa kalusugan, at tinanggal na ang mga karakter na naging sanhi ng kontrobersiya. Ayon kay Brent Strong ng Walt Disney Imagineering, lumabas sa feedback ng mga bisita na may mga bahagi ng palabas na hindi tumutulong para maiparating ang mensahe ng mas malusog na pamumuhay. Sa bagong bersyon ngayon, hinihikayat ng attraction na gumawa ng malusog na desisyon ang lahat ng bisita, anuman ang kanilang katawan. Ipinahayag naman ni Tony Jenkins mula Florida Blue, ang sponsor ng Habit Heroes, na ang bagong layunin ng attraction ay hikayatin ang mga pamilya at komunidad na magtulungan para sa mas maayos na kalusugan.

article_content: J.Lindeberg, a Swedish brand known for its ski and golf collections, is expanding its presence in tennis. The company began its ambassador program in 2022 by signing Mirjam Bjorklund of Sweden and Petra Martic of Croatia, and added 2023 Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova from the Czech Republic in August 2023. A new male tennis ambassador is set to join at the start of the 2024 season. Seeking to bridge fashion and sports, J.Lindeberg offers tennis apparel that merges elegant design with athletic functionality. 'We believe we can bring a fresh perspective to tennis by introducing innovative designs that blend sophistication and sportiness,' says Karin Elwin, Head of Marketing. The brand views tennis as an opportunity to engage a style-conscious audience both on and off the court. By selecting ambassadors whose values align with the company, J.Lindeberg aims to connect with wider audiences and tell its brand story through sports and fashion. Upcoming collections feature bolder patterns and reflect the brand's commitment to diversity and inclusion. Bringing in a male ambassador is intended to further enhance this lineup. In recent years, many non-traditional brands, including J.Lindeberg, have focused on both professional and recreational tennis. Its collections for male and female players emphasize modern, bold, and inclusive designs, uniting technological advancement with fashion. Highlights of J.Lindeberg’s tennis collection include stretch technology for comfort, tailored fits, 37.5 technology for climate regulation, moisture-wicking fabrics, and breathable mesh paneling in high-heat areas. These features are designed to enhance athletic performance while looking stylish. For J.Lindeberg, tennis represents more than just a sport—it’s a lifestyle. The brand’s apparel blends passion, performance, style, and functionality. Marketa Vondrousova shares this vision, praising the brand’s focus on innovation in tennis attire. Looking forward, J.Lindeberg plans to continually evolve its tennis collections with input from athletes like Vondrousova, offering a fresh mix of style and performance.

Inaasahan ring sumali ang isang male tennis ambassador sa simula ng 2024 season. Layunin ng J.Lindeberg na pagsamahin ang fashion at sports gamit ang tennis apparel na may eleganteng disenyo at athletic functionality. article_content: Arijit Guha, a PhD candidate at Arizona State University, was just 30 when he was diagnosed with stage four colon cancer. He soon found out that his student health insurance from Aetna, for which he paid $400 a month, had a $300,000 lifetime coverage cap. After reaching that limit during treatment, Guha was left with more than $114,000 in unpaid medical expenses, risking severe financial hardship. While the Affordable Care Act had eliminated lifetime limits on insurance, this reform hadn't started for student health plans like his. Feeling desperate, Guha brought his case to Twitter and directly contacted Mark Bertolini, Aetna’s CEO. Their exchange attracted widespread attention online, with many users openly criticizing Aetna’s policies and CEOs compensation. Under mounting public scrutiny, Bertolini spoke with Guha and eventually agreed that Aetna would cover all of Guha’s hospital costs. Before this development, Guha launched a t-shirt fundraiser called “Poop Strong,” collecting over $100,000 for his treatment; now, he intends to donate that amount to charity. In the aftermath, Bertolini admitted there were deep problems in the health system, while Guha said he was in disbelief and deeply relieved by the outcome.

Nang umabot siya sa limit na ito habang nagpapagamot, iniwan si Guha na may mahigit $114,000 na hindi bayad na hospital bills at nalagay siya sa alanganing sitwasyon sa pinansyal. Kahit tinanggal na ng Affordable Care Act ang mga lifetime limit, hindi pa ito naipatupad sa student health plans tulad ng sa kanya. Bilang sagot sa matinding pangangailangan, ginamit ni Guha ang Twitter para ilahad ang kanyang kaso at direktang tinag si Mark Bertolini, CEO ng Aetna. Maraming netizen ang nakigulo at pumuna sa polisiya ng Aetna at malaki nitong CEO salary. Dahil sa lumalaking pressure online, direktang nakipag-usap si Bertolini kay Guha at sa huli ay pumayag ang Aetna na sagutin lahat ng hospital bills niya. Nauna nang nag-launch si Guha ng fundraising campaign na “Poop Strong” kung saan nakalikom siya ng lampas $100,000 para sa gamutan, na balak niyang i-donate na lang sa charity ngayong sagot na ng Aetna ang lahat ng gastusin. Inamin mismo ni Bertolini na may seryosong problema sa health system, at labis ang pasasalamat at ginhawa ni Guha sa naging solusyon.

article_content: Protests against a 10-cent increase in bus fares erupted into violence in Rio de Janeiro, with rioters seizing control of the city's main railway station. Police responded with tear gas and stun grenades as hundreds of demonstrators took to the streets following Mayor Eduardo Paes' announcement of the fare hike. During the chaos, Santiago Andrade, a cameraman for Band TV, was struck in the head by an explosive device—possibly a police stun grenade or a homemade explosive thrown by protesters. He was taken to a hospital, underwent surgery, and remains in serious condition. Members of the 'Free Pass' movement occupied Central do Brasil station, destroyed ticket barriers, and allowed commuters to travel without paying. This protest is the latest in a series since last June, following a crackdown in São Paulo over similar fare increases, which led to the reversal of those hikes. On Thursday, about 800 protesters gathered in central Rio before marching to the train station, carrying signs condemning the government's spending on the World Cup and calling for better hospitals, schools, and infrastructure. The situation escalated inside the train station, where police used batons, tear gas, and tried to disperse members of the Black Block anarchist movement. Demonstrators responded by throwing rocks. Authorities closed the station, leaving thousands of commuters stranded; some bystanders fell ill or fainted due to the tear gas. Protesters also set fire to vehicles and built makeshift barricades in the streets. One protester, Thais Jorao, 22, explained that the demonstration was not just about the fare increase but about broader issues, saying, 'If it was a public transportation fare hike when we had good health services and education, you wouldn't have this many people on the street... We want health, education, decent public transportation.'

Gumanti ang pulisya gamit ang tear gas at stun grenades habang daan-daang tao ang nagmartsa matapos ianunsyo ni Mayor Eduardo Paes ang taas-pasahe. Sa gitna ng kaguluhan, tinamaan sa ulo ng pampasabog si Santiago Andrade, cameraman ng Band TV—maaaring stun grenade mula sa pulis o sariling likhang bomba ng mga nagpoprotesta. Dinala siya sa ospital, inoperahan, at nananatiling nasa malubhang kalagayan. Inokupa ng mga kasapi ng 'Free Pass' movement ang Central do Brasil station, sinira ang mga ticket barriers, at pinayagan ang mga tao na sumakay ng libre. Ang protesta ay bahagi ng serye simula pa noong Hunyo, matapos ang matinding aksyon ng pulis sa São Paulo kaugnay din ng taas-pasahe, na nagresulta dati sa pagpapawalang-bisa ng taas presyo. Nitong Huwebes, humigit-kumulang 800 ang nagtipon sa sentro ng Rio bago nagmartsa patungong istasyon, may dalang mga karatula na kinokondena ang pondo para sa World Cup at humihiling ng mas maayos na ospital, paaralan, at imprastraktura. Uminit ang sitwasyon sa loob ng istasyon ng tren, kung saan gumamit ang pulis ng baton, tear gas, at sinubukang paalisin ang mga miyembro ng Black Block anarchist movement. Gumanti ang mga nagpoprotesta sa pamamagitan ng paghahagis ng bato. Pansamantalang isinara ng mga otoridad ang istasyon at maraming biyahero ang na-stranded; may ilan ding hinimatay o nagkasakit dahil sa tear gas. Nagliyab din ang ilang sasakyan at nagtayo ng makeshift barricades sa kalsada ang mga nagpoprotesta. Isa sa kanila, si Thais Jorao, 22, ang nagsabi: 'Kung taas-pasahe lang ito at maganda ang serbisyo ng kalusugan at edukasyon, wala sanang ganitong kalaking protesta... Ang gusto namin ay kalusugan, edukasyon at disenteng pampublikong transportasyon.'

article_content: With Halloween on the horizon and autumn in full swing, it's prime time for settling in with a lineup of chilling movies. While horror classics abound, here’s a curated list of 10 favorites that bring the perfect atmosphere for a scary movie night. This isn’t a definitive ranking—just a personally chosen set of Halloween-worthy titles—and you're invited to share your own picks too.  Kicking things off: John Carpenter’s 'The Thing.' Set in Antarctica, this cult classic follows a research crew’s fight for survival against a shapeshifting alien that can impersonate anyone. Although not a success at first, it's now a fan favorite.  '10 Cloverfield Lane' features tight storytelling and first-rate acting from John Goodman and Mary Elizabeth Winstead. Its suspenseful, confined narrative keeps viewers guessing throughout.  The eerie silence in 'A Quiet Place' makes for heart-pounding viewing, as John Krasinski (director and star) and Emily Blunt portray a family forced to live in near-total quiet due to alien invaders drawn to sound.  Stanley Kubrick’s adaptation of Stephen King's 'The Shining' offers a masterclass in psychological terror, anchored by Jack Nicholson’s unforgettable performance inside a haunted hotel.  Jordan Peele’s 'Get Out' brilliantly combines horror with sharp commentary on racism. Daniel Kaluuya leads a talented ensemble in this clever and haunting tale.  In 'Alien,' Ridley Scott mixes industrial sci-fi with horror, enhanced by H.R. Giger’s unsettling creature design. Sigourney Weaver’s strong lead as Ripley has become legendary.  'Army of Darkness,' the third Evil Dead film from Sam Raimi and Bruce Campbell, is a witty, fast-paced horror-comedy—perfect for a lighthearted addition to your movie night.  No horror selection is complete without 'The Exorcist.' Adapted by William Peter Blatty, its legacy lives on thanks to its shocking story, turbulent production, and critical acclaim as the first horror film to win Academy Awards.  'The Conjuring' revives the haunted house genre, inspired by cases of real paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren. Its spine-tingling vibe makes it a Halloween staple.  Closing out the picks: 'Silence of the Lambs,' an intense psychological thriller highlighted by Anthony Hopkins and Jodie Foster’s standout performances. This film favors psychological suspense and storytelling over gory spectacle.  Many more could join this list—from 'The Blair Witch Project' to 'Scream' and 'Event Horizon.' What terrifying movies are a must for your Halloween? Share your favorites!

Hindi ito ranggo ng 'pinakamagaling'—mga personal choice lang, kaya welcome kang magbahagi ng sarili mong picks.  Umpisahan natin sa 'The Thing' ni John Carpenter. Sa gitna ng Antarctica, isang grupo ng siyentipiko ang sinusubok ng isang alien na kayang magbago ng anyo at gayahin ang kahit sino. Hindi ito sumikat noong una, pero kulto classic na ngayon.  Sa '10 Cloverfield Lane,' matindi ang tensyon at solid ang acting nina John Goodman at Mary Elizabeth Winstead—hindi mo mahuhulaan ang susunod na mangyayari hanggang sa huli.  Sa 'A Quiet Place,' mapapansin mo ang kakaibang katahimikan habang sina John Krasinski (director at bida) at Emily Blunt ay namumuhay nang halos walang ingay dahil sa mga alien na nagte-tele based sa tunog. article_content: UK Independence Party (UKIP) leader Nigel Farage claimed today that his party could help shape the next UK government, should another hung parliament occur. Despite UKIP not having any Members of Parliament, Farage pointed to the party’s rising trajectory, hinting that UKIP could become a kingmaker if no single party wins a majority. This assertion coincides with Prime Minister David Cameron’s efforts to counter the electoral threat posed by the Eurosceptic UKIP, as he prepares to deliver a major speech in the Netherlands on the Conservative Party’s stance regarding Britain’s future with the EU. Tensions between the Conservative Party and UKIP have grown, especially as UKIP’s poll ratings have reached 16 percent—up from 4.5 percent the previous year. In response, Cameron referred to UKIP members as 'pretty odd people,' further straining relations and suggesting that a pre-election pact with UKIP is unlikely. Farage, however, insisted that if UKIP’s momentum continues, the party could help form a coalition government if the 2015 election results in another hung parliament. He acknowledged challenges, saying, 'The first-past-the-post system is tough on parties like us. We have work to do, but who’s to say UKIP won’t be needed in a coalition?' Still, he cautioned against overconfidence, referencing David Steel's infamous call for the Liberal Party to 'prepare for government,' which became a subject of ridicule. Speaking to BBC Radio 4, Farage emphasized, 'We are making progress but aren’t poised to take government yet. We represent ordinary people and aren’t bound by political correctness. We’ve shown we can campaign effectively—let’s see where the UKIP story goes.' Meanwhile, the British Prime Minister criticized UKIP supporters, calling them 'pretty odd people,' as former Labour minister Lord Mandelson warned that jeopardizing the UK’s EU membership would be 'economically insane.' UKIP is expected to perform strongly in the 2014 European Parliament elections and has beaten both the Conservatives and Liberal Democrats in recent by-elections. A recent Survation poll for the Mail on Sunday placed Labour at 38%, the Conservatives at 29%, UKIP at 16%, and the Liberal Democrats at 11%. If reflected in a general election, these results could lead to the Conservatives losing 51 seats and Labour achieving a majority of 94. Cameron reiterated his position against UKIP, referencing past descriptions of UKIP supporters as 'fruitcakes, loonies, and closet racists.' Farage responded by highlighting the diversity and individuality within UKIP, contrasting it with what he perceives as the blandness of other parties’ MPs. Cameron is set to make a major speech in the Netherlands by the end of the month, expected to propose repatriating powers from Brussels and pledging to put the new settlement to a referendum. He will reject the idea of the UK leaving the EU to become a Norway-like trading partner, instead arguing for renegotiation from within. In The Guardian, Lord Mandelson warned that Cameron cannot coerce EU leaders into granting new powers, arguing that pursuing a referendum could ultimately divide the Conservative Party and risk the UK’s economic interests. He described beginning 2013 by questioning EU membership as 'economically insane.'

Bagaman walang kinatawan sa Parliament ang UKIP, binigyang-diin ni Farage ang tumataas na suporta sa kanilang partido at posibilidad na maging mahalagang salik sila sakaling walang makakuha ng malinaw na mayorya. Kasabay ito ng pagsusumikap ni Prime Minister David Cameron na tapatan ang banta ng UKIP, na tutol sa EU, habang naghahanda siyang magbigay ng mahalagang talumpati sa Netherlands tungkol sa polisiya ng Conservatives ukol sa kinabukasan ng Britain sa EU. Lalong lumala ang tensyon sa pagitan ng Conservatives at UKIP, lalo na’t umangat sa 16 porsyento ang rating ng UKIP—mula 4.5 porsyento noong nakaraang taon. Bilang tugon, tinawag ni Cameron ang mga miyembro ng UKIP na 'medyo kakaibang tao,' na lalo pang nagpalabo ng posibilidad ng alyansa bago ang halalan. Pero iginiit ni Farage na kung magpapatuloy ang paglakas ng UKIP, maaaring makatulong silang bumuo ng coalition government kung muling magkaroon ng hung parliament sa 2015. Marami pa kaming kailangan gawin, pero sino ang makakapagsabing hindi kakailanganin ang UKIP sa coalition?' Nagbabala siya laban sa labis na kumpiyansa, na binanggit ang panawagan noon ni David Steel sa Liberal Party na 'maghanda para sa gobyerno,' na nauwi sa katatawanan. Kumakatawan kami sa karaniwang tao at hindi natatali sa political correctness. Napapatunayan naming mahusay kami sa kampanya—tingnan natin kung saan patutungo ang kwento ng UKIP.' Samantala, muling binatikos ng Punong Ministro ang mga tagasuporta ng UKIP at tinawag silang 'medyo kakaibang tao,' habang nagbabala si dating Labour minister Lord Mandelson na delikado sa ekonomiya kung ilalagay sa alanganin ang pagiging miyembro ng UK sa EU. Inaasahang malakas ang UKIP sa 2014 European Parliament elections at natalo na nila ang Conservatives at Liberal Democrats sa mga nakalipas na by-election. Sa pinakahuling Survation poll para sa Mail on Sunday, nakuha ng Labour ang 38%, Conservatives 29%, UKIP 16%, at Liberal Democrats 11%. Kung magkatotoo ito sa halalan, maaaring mawalan ng 51 upuan ang Conservatives at makakuha ng 94 na mayorya ang Labour. Muling binigyang-diin ni Cameron ang kanyang pagtutol sa UKIP at sinariwa ang mga naunang tinawag na 'fruitcakes, loonies, at closet racists' ang UKIP supporters. Tinugon naman ito ni Farage at binigyang-diin ang pagkakaiba-iba at pagiging totoo ng UKIP kumpara sa tingin niyang kabastusan ng ibang MPs. Magbibigay ng malaking talumpati si Cameron sa Netherlands bago matapos ang buwan, kung saan inaasahang ilalatag niya ang panukalang ibalik ang ilang kapangyarihan mula Brussels at isasailalim ang napagkasunduan sa referendum. Tinututulan din niya ang ideya na tuluyang umalis sa EU ang UK at maging kahalintulad ng Norway bilang trading partner. Sa isang artikulo sa The Guardian, nagbabala si Lord Mandelson na hindi maaaring pilitin ni Cameron ang mga lider ng EU na ibigay ang mga karagdagang kapangyarihan, at ang pagtulak daw ng referendum ay maaaring magdulot ng pagkakahati sa Conservative Party at magbanta sa ekonomiyang interes ng UK. Tinawag niyang 'ekonomikong baliw' ang pagkuwestyon sa EU membership sa umpisa ng 2013.

article_content: Pixel launch day arrived with drama: Google unexpectedly discontinued the Pixel Watch 2 just before the event, showcasing only the Pixel 8 series and new Pixel Buds Pro colors. Oddly enough, the Android 14 rollout is limited this month to just the Pixel 8 and 8 Pro, with prior Pixel models allegedly waiting until December. Other leading brands like Samsung, OnePlus, and Xiaomi are said to face delays, as Android 14 may not reach them until mid-2024, reportedly due to technical problems. Android 14’s touted customization and accessibility are now described as 'limited,' with reports noting the lock screen’s AI upgrades require a subscription and are only in select areas. Those exciting generative AI wallpapers? They’re paywalled behind a Google One membership now. Monochrome UI themes and Ultra HDR image support were promised, but both features are currently disabled, with no word on future activation. Health Connect integration has been rolled back, requiring a separate app install instead of seamless setup. The new PIN animation is catching heat for glitches that can show parts of your PIN, while the enhanced six-digit PIN isn’t launching yet. Accessibility features like Magnifier Settings and hearing aid support have been pushed back, leaving only the quick font size adjustment accessible now. As for Flash Notifications, early users claim they cause frequent crashes for several Pixel models. To top it off, sources say the usual Pixel Feature Drop is suspended, making Pixel 8 Pro the lone flagship with camera and AI improvements—but even it attracts complaints of battery drain.
